text: ſo that they alſo, which offered the holocauſtes to our Lod, did offer the ſacrifices to our Lord girded with heareclothes, and there were ashes vpon their head.
label: Judith

text: And they al prayed God with al their hart, that he would viſite his people Iſrael.
label: Judith

text: AND it was told Holofernes the General of the warres of the Aſſyrians, that the children of Iſrael prepared them ſelues to reſiſt, and had shut vp the wayes of the mountaynes,
label: Judith

text: and with exceding furie he chafed in great anger, and called al the princes of Noab and dukes of Ammon,
label: Judith

text: and he ſayd to them: Tel me what is this people which beſetteth the mountaynes: or what, and of what ſorte, and how great their cities are: alſo what their power is, or what is their multitude: or who is the king of their warfare:
label: Judith

text: and why aboue al that dwel in the Eaſt, haue theſe contemned vs, and haue not come forth to meete vs, that they might receiue vs with peace?
label: Judith

text: Then Achior captaine of al the children of Ammon anſwering, ſaid: If thou woutſafe my Lord to heare, I wil tel the truth in thy ſight of this people, which dwelleth in the mountaynes, and there shal not a falſe word come forth of my mouth.
label: Judith

text: This people is of the progenie of the Chaldees.
label: Judith

text: The ſame dwelt firſt in Meſopotamia, becauſe they would not folow the goddes of their fathets, which were in the land of the Chaldees.
label: Judith

text: Forſaking therfore the ceremonies of their fathers, which were in multitude of goddes,
label: Judith

text: they worshipped one God of heauen, who alſo commanded them that they should depart from thence, and should dwel in Charan. And when there was famine ouer al the land, they went downe into Ægypt, and there for foure hundred yeares were ſo multiplied, that the hoſt of them could not be numbred.
label: Judith

text: And when the king of Ægypt oppreſſed them, and in the buildinges of his cities had ſubdewed them in brick and claye, they cried to their Lord, and he ſtroke the whole Land of Ægypt with diuers plagues.
label: Judith

text: And when the Ægyptians had caſt them out from them, and the plague had ceaſed from them, and they would take them againe, and cal them backe to their ſeruice,
label: Judith

text: theſe fleeing away, the God of heauen opened the ſea, ſo that the waters were conſolidated as a wal, on either ſide, and they walking through the botome of the ſea paſſed drie foote.
label: Judith

text: In which place whiles an innumerable armie of the Ægyptians purſewed them, they were ſo ouerwhelmed with the waters, that there was not one remayning, to tel the fact to poſteritie.
label: Judith

text: Alſo being paſt the read ſea, they poſſeſſed the deſertes of Mount Sinai, in which neuer man could dwel, or ſonne of man reſted.
label: Judith

text: There bitter fountaynes were made ſweete for them to drinke, and for fourtie yeares they receiued meate from heauen.
label: Judith

text: Whereſoeuer they entered without bow and arrow, and without shielde and ſword, their God fought for them, and ouercame.
label: Judith

text: And there was not that did inſult againſt this people, but when they departed from the worſhip of the Lord their God.
label: Judith

text: But as often as beſide their owne God, they worshiped an other, they were geuen to praye, and into the ſword, and to reproch.
label: Judith

text: And as often as they were penitent for that they reuolted from the worship of their God, the God of heauen gaue them power to reſiſt.
label: Judith

text: Finally the king of the Chananeites, and of Iebuſeites, and of the Pherezeites, and of the Hetheites, and of the Heueites, and of the Amorrheites, and al the mightie in Heſebon they ouerthrew, and they poſſeſſed their landes, & their cities:
label: Judith

text: and as long as they ſinned not in the ſight of their God, it was wel with them, for their God hateth iniquitie.
label: Judith

text: For theſe yeares alſo paſt when they had reuolted from the way, which God had geuen them, that they ſhould walke in it, they were deſtroyed in battels by manie nations, and verie manie of them were led captiue into a ſtrange land.
label: Judith

text: But of late returning to the Lord their God, from the diſperſion wherein they were diſperſed, they are vnited & are come vp into al theſe mountaynes, and poſſeſſe Ieruſalem againe where their Holies are.
label: Judith

text: Now therfore my Lord, ſearch if there be any iniquitie of theirs in the ſight of their God: and let vs goe vp to them, becauſe their God deliuering wil deliuer them to thee, and they shal be ſubdewed vnder the yoke of thy power:
label: Judith

text: but if there be no offence of this people before their God, we can not reſiſt them, becauſe their God wil defend them: and we shal be a reproche to the whole earth.
label: Judith

text: And it came to paſſe, when Achior had ceaſed to ſpeake theſe wordes, al the great men of Holofernes were angrie, and they thought to kil him, ſaying to each other:
label: Judith

text: who is this, that ſayth the children of Iſrael can reſiſt king Nabuchodonoſor, and his armies, men vnarmed, and without force, and without skil of the feates of warre?
label: Judith

text: That Achior therfore may know that he deceiueth vs, let vs goe vp into the mountaynes: and when their mightie ones shal be taken, then shal he with them be ſtrooken through with the ſword:
label: Judith

text: that euerie nation may know that Nabuchodonoſor is God of the earth, and beſides him there is none other.
label: Judith

text: AND it came to paſſe when they had ceaſed to ſpeake, Holofernes being ſore offended, ſaid to Achior:
label: Judith

text: Becauſe thou haſt prophecied vnto vs ſaying, that the nation of Iſrael is defended of their God, that I may ſheu thee that there is no God, but Nabuchodonoſor:
label: Judith

text: when we shal haue ſtrookē them al as one man, then thy ſelf with them shalt die by the ſword of the Aſſyrians, and al Iſrael with thee shal perish by deſtruction:
label: Judith

text: and thou shalt proue that Nabuchodonoſor is lord of the whole earth: and then the ſword of my warfare shal paſſe through thy ſides, & pearſed thou shalt fal among the wounded of Iſrael, and thou shalt no more fetch breath, til thou be deſtroyed with them.
label: Judith

text: But if thou thinke thy prophecie true, let not thy countenance quaile, and the paleneſſe that is in thy face, let it depart from thee, if thou thinke theſe my wordes can not be accompliſhed.
label: Judith

text: And that thou mayſt know that thou shalt ptoue theſe thinges together with them, behold from this houre thou shalt be aſſociate to their people, that whiles they shal receiue worthie punishment of my ſword, thou withal may be ſubiect to the vengeance.
label: Judith

text: Then Holofernes commanded his ſeruantes that they should take Achior, and lead him into Bethula, and should deliuer him into the handes of the children of Iſrael.
label: Judith

text: And the ſeruantes of Holofernes taking him, went through the champaine: but when they came neere the mountaynes, the ſlingers came forth againſt them.
label: Judith

text: And they turning out of the way by the ſide of the mountayne, tyed Achior to a tree hand and foote, and ſo left him bound with withes, and returned to their lord.
label: Judith

text: Moreouer the children of Iſrael deſcending from Bethulia, came to him. Whom looſnig they brought to Bethulia, and ſetting him in the middes of the people, demanded what was the matter, that the Aſſyrians had left him bound.
label: Judith

text: In thoſe dayes the princes there, were Ozias the ſonne of Micha of the tribe of Simeon, and Charmi, who alſo is Gothoniel.
label: Judith

text: In the middes therefore of the ancientes, and in the ſight of al, Achior told al thinges that he had ſpoken being asked of Holofernes: and how the people of Holofernes would haue killed him for this word,
label: Judith

text: and how Holofernes him ſelfe being angrie commanded him to be deliuered for this cauſe to the Iſraelites: that when he should ouercome the children of Iſrael, then he might command Achior alſo himſelf to die by diuerſe tormentes, for this that he had ſaid: The God of heauen is their defender.
label: Judith

text: And when Achior had declared al theſe thinges, al the people fel on their face, adoring our Lord, and with common lamentation and weeping they powred out their prayers with one accord to our Lord,
label: Judith

text: ſaying: Lord God of heauen and earth, behold their pride, and haue regard to our humilitie, and attend the face of thy ſainctes, and shew that thou forſakeſt not them that preſume of thee and, that thow humbleſt them that preſume of them ſelues, and glorie of their power.
label: Judith

text: Their weeping therfore being ended, & the peoples prayer by the whole day being finished, they comforted Achior,
label: Judith

text: ſaying: The God of our fathers, whoſe power thou haſt ſet forth, he wil geue thee this recompence, that thou rather shalt ſee their deſtruction.
label: Judith

text: And when the Lord our God shal geue this libertie to his ſeruantes, be God with thee alſo in the middes of vs: that as it shal pleaſe thee, ſo thou with al thine mayſt conuerſe with vs.
label: Judith

text: Then Ozias, the counſel being ended, receiued him into his houſe, and made him a greate ſupper.
label: Judith

text: And al the ancientes being called, they refreshed them ſelues together after the faſting was ended.
label: Judith

text: But afterwarde al the people was called together, and al the night long within the church, they prayed deſiring helpe of the God of Iſrael.
label: Judith

text: BVT Holofernes the next day commanded his armies, that they should goe vp againſt Bethulia.
label: Judith

text: And there were of warre foote men an hundred twentie thouſand, and horſe men two and twentie thouſand, beſides the preparations of thoſe men, whom the captiuitie had taken, and had beene led away out of the prouinces and cities, of al youth.
label: Judith

text: Al prepared them ſelues together to the fight agaynſt the children of Iſrael, and they came by the hil ſide vnto the toppe, which looketh toward Dorhaim, from the place which is called Belma vnto Chelmon, which is againſt Eſdrelon.
label: Judith

text: But the children of Iſrael, as they ſaw the multitude of them, laid them ſelues proſtrate vpon the earth, caſting ashes vpon their heades, praying with one accord, that the God of Iſrael would shew his mercie vpon his people.
label: Judith

text: And taking their weapons of warre, they ſate at the places, which by a narrow path way lead directly betwen the mountaynes, and they were keping them al day and night.
label: Judith

text: Moreouer Holofernes, whiles he compaſſeth round about, found that the foūtayne, which ranne in, went directly to their conduite on the ſouth ſide without the citie: and he commanded their conduite to be cut aſunder.
label: Judith

text: Neuertheleſſe there were fountaynes not far from the walles, out of which ſecretly they ſemed to draw water to refresh them ſelues, rather then to drinke.
label: Judith

text: But the children of Ammon, & Moab came to Holofernes, ſaying: The children of Iſrael truſt not in ſpeare, nor in arrow, but the mountaynes defend them, & the hilles ſtanding meruelous ſtipe gard them.
label: Judith

text: Therfore that thou mayſt ouercome them without ioyning battel, ſet kepers of the fountaynes, that they may not draw water of them, and without ſword thou shalt kil them, or at the leaſt being wearied they wil yeld their citie, which they thinck being ſet in the mountaynes, can not be ouercome.
label: Judith

text: And theſe wordes pleaſed Holofernes, and his ſouldiars, and he placed round about an hundred men at euerie fountayne.
label: Judith

text: And when that watch had beene fully kept for twentie dayes, the ceſternes fayled, and the collections of waters to al the inhabitantes of Bethulia, ſo that there was not within the citie, wherof they might be ſatisfied no not for one day, becauſe water was dayly geuen to the people by meaſure.
label: Judith

text: Then al the men, and wemen, yong men, and children, being gathered together to Ozias, al together with one voice,
label: Judith

text: ſaid: God iudge betwen vs and thee, becauſe thou haſt done euil agaynſt vs, in that thou wouldeſt not speake peaceably with the Aſſyrians, and for this cauſe God hath ſold vs into their handes.
label: Judith

text: And there is none to helpe, wheras we lye proſtrate before their eies in thirſt, & great deſtruction.
label: Judith

text: And now aſſemble ye al, that are in the citie, that we may of our owne accord yeld vs al to the people of Holofernes.
label: Judith

text: For it is better, that captiues we bleſſe our Lord liuing, then we should die, and be a reproch to al flesh, when we shal ſee our wiues, and our infantes die before our eies.
label: Judith

text: We cal to witnes this day heauen and earth, and the God of our fathers, which taketh vengeance of vs according to our ſinnes, that now you deliuer the citie into the hand of Holofernes armie, that our end may be short in the edge of the ſword, which is made longer in the drught of thirſt.
label: Judith

text: And when they had ſaid theſe thinges, there was made great weeping and howling of al in the aſſemble, and for manie houres with one voice they cried to God, ſaying:
label: Judith

text: We haue ſinned with our fathers, we haue done vniuſtly, we haue committed iniquitie.
label: Judith

text: Thou becauſe thou art gracious, haue mercie vpon vs, or in thy ſcourge reuenge our iniquities, and deliuer not them that truſt in thee to a people, that knoweth not thee,
label: Judith

text: that they ſay not among the Gentiles: Where is their God?
label: Judith

text: And when they wearied with theſe cries, and tyred with theſe weepings, had held their peace,
label: Judith

text: Ozias ryſing vp embrued with teares, ſaid: Be of good chere bretheren, and theſe fiue daies let vs expect mercie of our Lord.
label: Judith

text: For peraduenture he wil cut of his indignation, and wil geue glorie to his name.
label: Judith

text: But if after fiue daies be paſt there come no aide, we wil doe theſe wordes, which you haue spoken.
label: Judith

text: AND it came to paſſe, when Iudith a widow had heard theſe wordes, which was the daughter of Merari, the ſonne of Idox, the ſonne of Ioſeph, the ſonne of Ozias, the ſonne of Elai, the ſonne of Iamnor, the ſonne of Gedeon, the ſonne of Raphaim, the ſonne of Achitob, the ſonne of Melchias, the ſonne of Enan, the ſonne of Narhanias, the ſonne of Salathiel, the ſonne of Simeon, the ſonne of Iſrael:
label: Judith

text: and her huſband was Manaſſes, who died in the daies of barley harueſt:
label: Judith

text: for he was occupied with them that bound sheues in the field, and the heate came vpon his head, and he died in Bethulia his citie, and was buried there with his father.
label: Judith

text: And Iudith was leaft his widow now three yeares and ſix monethes.
label: Judith

text: And in the higher partes of her houſe she made her ſelf a ſecrete chamber, in which she abode shut vp with her maides,
label: Judith

text: and hauing cloth of heare vpon her loynes, she faſted al the daies of her life but Sabbathes, and new-moones, and the feaſtes of the houſe of Iſrael.
label: Judith

text: And she was of an exceding beautiful countenance, to whom her husband had leaft much richeſſe, and a great familie, and poſſeſſions ful of heardes of oxen, and flockes of sheepe.
label: Judith

text: And she was among al moſt famous, becauſe she feared our Lord very much, neither was there that spake an il word of her.
label: Judith

text: When she therfore had heard that Ozias had promiſed, that after the fifth day were paſt he would yeld the citie, she ſent to the ancientes Chabri and Charmi.
label: Judith

text: And they came to her, and she ſaid to them: What is this word, wherein Ozias hath conſented, to yeld the citie to the Aſſyrians, if within fiue daies there come no ayde to vs?
label: Judith

text: And what are you, that tempt our Lord?
label: Judith

text: This is no word that may prouoke mercie, but rather that may rayſe vp wrath, and inflame furie.
label: Judith

text: You haue ſet a time for the mercie of our Lord, and according to your pleaſure, you haue appointed him a day.
label: Judith

text: But becauſe our Lord is patient, let vs be penitent for this ſame thing, and sheding teares let vs deſire his pardon:
label: Judith

text: for not as man, ſo wil God threaten, neither as the ſonne of man wil he be inflamed to anger.
label: Judith

text: And therfore let vs humble our ſoules to him, and being ſetled in an humble ſpirit, ſeruing him:
label: Judith

text: let vs ſay weeping to our Lord, that according to his wil ſo he doe his mercie with vs: that as our hart is trubled in their pride, ſo alſo we may glorie in our humilitie:
label: Judith

text: becauſe we haue not folowed the ſinnes of our fathers, which forſooke their God, and adored ſtrange goddes,
label: Judith

text: for which abomination they were geuen into the ſword, and into confuſion to their enemies: but we know no other God but him.
label: Judith

text: Let vs humbly expect his conſolation, and he wil require our bloud of the afflictions of our enemies, and he wil humble al Nations, what ſoeuer shal riſe vp againſt vs, and the Lord our God wil make them without honour.
label: Judith

text: And now bretheren, becauſe you are ancientes in the people of God, and their ſoules depende of you: by your ſpeach comforte their hartes, that they be mindful, that our fathers were tempted to be proued, whether they did worſhippe their God truly.
label: Judith

text: They muſt be mindful how our father Abraham was tempted, and by many tribulations proued, was made the freind of God.
label: Judith

text: So Iſaac, ſo Iacob, ſo Moyſes, & al that haue pleaſed God, through manie tribulations haue paſſed faithful.
label: Judith

text: But they that did not receiue the tentations with the feare of our Lord, and vttered their impatience and reproch of their murmuring againſt our Lord,
label: Judith

text: were deſtroyed of the deſtroyer, and perished by ſerpents.
label: Judith

text: And we therfore let vs not reuenge ourſelues for theſe thinges, which we ſuffer,
label: Judith

text: but reputing theſe verie puniſhments to be the ſcourges of our Lord leſſe then our ſinnes, wherwith as ſeruantes we are chaſtiſed, let vs thinke them to haue chanced to our amendement, and not to our deſtruction.
label: Judith

text: And Ozias and the ancientes ſayd to her: Al thinges which thou haſt spoken, be true, and there is no reprehenſion in thy wordes.
label: Judith

text: Now therfore pray for vs, becauſe thou art a holie woman, and fearing God.
label: Judith

text: And Iudith ſaid to them: As you know, that which I could ſpeake to be of God:
label: Judith

text: ſo that which I haue diſpoſed to doe, proue if it be of God, and pray that God eſtablish my counſel.
label: Judith

text: You shal ſtand at the gate this night, and I wil goe out with myne abra: and pray ye, that as you haue ſaid, in fiue dayes our Lord reſpect his people Iſrael.
label: Judith

text: But I wil not that you ſearch my doing, and til I bring you word, let nothing els be done, but pray for me to our Lord God.
label: Judith

text: And Ozias the prince of Iuda ſaid to her: Goe in peace, and our Lord be with thee to the reuenge of our enemies. And returning they departed.
label: Judith

text: WHO going away, Iudith went into her oratorie: and clothing her ſelf with hearecloth, put ashes vpon her head: and falling proſtrate to our Lord, she cried to our Lord, ſaying:
label: Judith

text: Lord God of may father Simeon, who gaueſt him a ſword for defenee againſt ſtrangers, which were rauishers in their coinquination, and diſcouered the virgine vnto confuſion:
label: Judith

text: and gaueſt their wemen into praye, and their daughters into captiuitie: and al the praye to be diuided to thy ſeruantes, which were zelous in thy zele: helpe I beſeech thee ô lord God me a widow.
label: Judith

text: For thou haſt done the thinges heretofore, and haſt purpoſed one thing after another: and that hath bene done which thou wouldeſt.
label: Judith

text: For al thy wayes are readie, and thy iudgementes thou haſt put in thy prouidence.
label: Judith

text: Looke vpon the campe of the Aſſyrians now, as thou didſt voutſafe to ſee the campe of the Ægyptians, when they ran armed after thy ſeruantes, truſting in chariotes, and in their horſemen, and in a multitude of men of warre.
label: Judith

text: But thou didſt looke ouer their campe. and darkeneſſe wearied them.
label: Judith

text: The depth held their feete, and the waters ouerwhelmed them.
label: Judith

text: So let theſe alſo be made ô Lord, which truſt in their multitude, and in their chariotes, and in pikes, and in shieldes, and in their arrowes, and glorie in their ſpeares,
label: Judith

text: and know not thy ſelf art our God, which deſtroyeſt warres from the beginning, and Lord is thy name.
label: Judith

text: Lift vp thyne arme as from the beginning, and dash their power in thy power: let their power fal in thy wrath, which promiſe that they wil violate thy holie thinges, and pollute the tabernacle of thy holie name, & with their ſword throw downe the horne of thyne altar.
label: Judith

text: Bring to paſſe Lord, that his pride be cut of with his owne ſword,
label: Judith

text: let him be caught with the ſnares of his eies in me, and thou shalt ſtrike him from the lippes of my charitie.
label: Judith

text: Geue me conſtancie in mind, that I may contemne him: and powre that I may ouerthrow him.
label: Judith

text: For this shal be a memorial of thy name, when the hand of a woman shal ouerthrow him.
label: Judith

text: For not in multitude is thy power ô Lord, neither in ſtrength of horſes is thy wil, neither haue the proud pleaſed thee from the beginninge: but the prayer of the humble and meeke hath alwayes pleaſed thee.
label: Judith

text: God of the heauens, creatour of the waters, and Lord of euerie creature, heare me wretch, praying and preſuming of thy mercie.
label: Judith

text: Remember Lord thy teſtament, and geue a word in my mouth, and ſtrengthen counſel in my hart, that thy houſe may continew in thy ſanctification:
label: Judith

text: and al Nations may acknowledge, that thou art God, and there is no other beſides thee.
label: Judith

text: AND it came to paſſe, when she had ceaſed to crie to our Lord, she roſe from the place, wherein she lay proſtrate to our Lord.
label: Judith

text: And she called her abra, and going downe into her houſe she tooke from her the hearecloth, and put of the garmentes of her widowhood,
label: Judith

text: and washed her bodie, and anoynted her ſelf with ointement, and plaited the heare of her head, and put a crowne vpon her head, and clothed her ſelf with the garmentes of her ioyfulnes, and put pantofles on her feete, and tooke braceletes, and Lilies, and eareletes, and ringes, and with al her ornamentes she adorned her ſelf.
label: Judith

text: To whom alſo our Lord gaue beautie: becauſe al this trimming did not depend of ſenſualitie, but of vertue: & therfore our Lord amplified this beautie on her, that she might appeare to al mens eies of incomparable comlines.
label: Judith

text: She therfore layd vpon her abra a bottel of wyne, and a veſſel of oyle, and polent, and drie figges, and bread, and cheeſe, and went foreward.
label: Judith

text: And when they were come to the gate of the citie, they found Ozias expecting, and the ancientes of the citie.
label: Judith

text: Who when they ſaw her, being aſtonished maruailed at her beautie exceedingly,
label: Judith

text: Yet asking her no queſtion, they let her paſſe, ſaying: The God of our fathers geue thee grace, and ſtrengthen al the counſel of thy hart, with his powre, that Ieruſalem may glorie vpon thee, and thy name may be in the number of the holie and iuſt.
label: Judith

text: And they that were there ſaid, al with one voyce: So be it, ſo be it.
label: Judith

text: But Iudith praying our Lord, paſſed through the gates she and her Abra.
label: Judith

text: And it came to paſſe, when she went downe the hil, about breake of day the watchmen of the Aſſyrians mette her, and held her, ſaying: whence comeſt thou? or whither goeſt thou?
label: Judith

text: Who anſwered, I am a daughter of the Hebrews, therfore am I fled from their face, becauſe I knew it should come to paſſe, that they should be geuen you vnto spoyle, becauſe that contemning you, they would not of their owne accord yeld themſelues, that they might find mercie in your ſight.
label: Judith

text: For this cauſe I thought with my ſelf, ſaying: I wil goe to the preſence of the prince Holofernes, that I may tel him their ſecretes, and shew him by what entrance he may winne them, ſo that there shal not fal one man of his armie.
label: Judith

text: And when thoſe men had heard her wordes, they conſidered her face, and she was a wonder in their eies, for they marueiled at her beautie excedingly.
label: Judith

text: And they ſaid to her: Thou haſt ſaued thy life, in that thou haſt found ſuch counſel, that thou wouldeſt come downe to our lord.
label: Judith

text: And this know thou, that when thou shalt ſtand in his ſight, he wil deale wel with thee, and thou shalt be moſt gratious in his hart. And they brought her to the tabernacle of Holofernes, telling him of her.
label: Judith

text: And when she was entered before his face, forthwith Holofernes was caught in his eies.
label: Judith

text: And his guard ſaid to him: Who can contemne the people of the Hebrewes, which haue ſo beautiful wemẽ, that we should not worthely fight againſt them for theſe?
label: Judith

text: Iudith therfore ſeeing Holofernes ſitting in a canopie, which was wouen of purple, and gold, and emerauld, and pretious ſtones:
label: Judith

text: and when she had looked in his face, she adored him, falling proſtrate vpon the ground. And the ſeruantes of Holofernes lifted her vp, their lord commanding it.
label: Judith

text: THEN Holofernes ſaid to her: Be of good chere, and feare not in thy hart: becauſe I haue neuer hurt man, that would ſerue Nabuchodonoſor the king.
label: Judith

text: And thy people, if they had not contemned me, I would neuer haue lifted vp my ſpeare ouer them.
label: Judith

text: But now tel me, for what cauſe haſt thou departed from them, and it hath pleaſed thee to come to vs?
label: Judith

text: And Iudith ſaid to him: Take the wordes of thy handmayde, for if thou wilt folow the wordes of thy handmayde, our Lord wil do with thee a perfect thing.
label: Judith

text: For Nabuchodonoſor the king of the earth liueth, and his power liueth which is in thee to the chaſtiſing of al ſtraying ſoules: that not onlie men ſerue him by thee, but alſo the beaſtes of the field obey him.
label: Judith

text: For the induſtrie of thy mind is reported to al nations, and it is declared to al the world, that thou onlie art good, and mightie in al his kingdom, and thy diſcipline is bruted to al prouinces.
label: Judith

text: Neither is that vnknowne, which Achior ſpake, neither are we ignorant of that thou haſt commanded to come vpon him.
label: Judith

text: For it is certaine that our God is ſo offended with ſinnes, that he hath ſent word by his prophetes to the people, that he wil deliuer them for their ſinnes.
label: Judith

text: And becauſe the children of Iſrael know they offended their God, thy dread is vpon them.
label: Judith

text: Moreouer alſo famine hath inuaded them, and for drought of water they are now eſtemed among the dead.
label: Judith

text: Finally they ordayne this, to kil their cattel, and to drinke the bloud of them,
label: Judith

text: and the holie thinges of our Lord their God which God commanded not to be touched, in corne, wine, and oile, theſe haue they purpoſed to beſtow, and they wil conſume the thinges which they ought not to touch with their handes: therfore becauſe they do theſe thinges, it is ſure that they ſhal be geuen into perdition.
label: Judith

text: Which I thy handmayde knowing, am fled from them, and our Lord hath ſent me to tel thee theſe verie thinges.
label: Judith

text: For I thy handmayde worſhippe God, euen now being with thee, and thy handmayde wil goe forth, and I wil pray God,
label: Judith

text: and he wil tel me when he wil repay them their ſinnes, and I coming wil tel thee, ſo that I may bring thee through the middes of Ieruſalem, and thou shalt haue al the people of Iſrael, as ſheepe, that haue no paſtor, and there ſhal not ſo much as one dog barke againſt thee:
label: Judith

text: becauſe theſe thinges are told me by the prouidence of God.
label: Judith

text: And becauſe God is angrie with them, I am ſent to tel theſe vetie thinges to thee.
label: Judith

text: And al theſe wordes pleaſed Holofernes, and his ſeruantes, and they maruailed at her wiſedom, and one ſaid to an other:
label: Judith

text: There is not ſuch a woman vpon the earth in looke, in beautie, and in ſenſe of wordes.
label: Judith

text: And Holofernes ſayd to her: God hath done wel, which ſent thee before the people, that thou mighteſt geue them into our handes:
label: Judith

text: and becauſe thy promiſe is good, if thy God shal doe this for me, he shal alſo be my God, and thou shalt be great in the houſe of Nabuchodonoſor, and thy name shal be renowmed in al the earth.
label: Judith

text: THEN he bad her goe in where his treaſures were layd vp, and bad her tarie there, and he appoynted what should be geuen her of his owne banket.
label: Judith

text: To whom Iudith anſwered, and ſaid: Now I can not eate of theſe thinges, which thou commandeſt to be geuen me, leſt there come diſpleaſure vpon me: but I wil eate of theſe thinges, which I haue brought.
label: Judith

text: To whom Holofernes ſaid: If theſe thinges which thou haſt brought with thee shal fayle thee, what shal we doe to thee.
label: Judith

text: And Iudith ſaid: Thy ſoule liueth my lord, that thy handmayde shal not ſpend al theſe thinges, til God doe by my hand theſe thinges, which I haue purpoſed. And his ſeruantes brought her into the tabernacle, which he had commanded.
label: Judith

text: And whiles she went in, she deſired that she might haue licence to goe forth, in the night and before day to prayer, and to beſech our Lord.
label: Judith

text: And he commanded his chamberlaynes, that as it pleaſed her, she should goe out & come in to adore her God for three dayes.
label: Judith

text: And she went forth in the nightes into the vale of Bethulia, and washed her ſelf in a fountaine of water.
label: Judith

text: And as she came vp, she prayed our Lord the God of Iſrael, that he would direct her way to the deliuerie of his people.
label: Judith

text: And going in, she remayned pure in the tabernacle, vntil she tooke her owne meate in the euening.
label: Judith

text: And it came to paſſe in the fourth day, Holofernes made a ſupper to his ſeruantes, and ſayd to Vagao his eunuch: Goe, and perſwade that Hebrew woman, that ſhe conſent of her owne accord to dwel with me.
label: Judith

text: For it is a foule thing with the Aſſyrians, if a woman mocke a man in doing, that she paſſe free from him.
label: Judith

text: Then Vagao went in to Iudith, & ſaid: Let not the good yong maide feare to goe in to my Lord, that she may be honoured before his face, that she may eate with him and drinke wine in ioyfulnes.
label: Judith

text: To whom Iudith anſwered: Who am I, that I should gayneſay my lord?
label: Judith

text: Al that shal be good and beſt before his eies, wil I doe. And whatſoeuer shal pleaſe him, that shal be beſt to me al the dayes of my life.
label: Judith

text: And she aroſe, and decked herſelf with her garmentes, and going in she ſtood before his face.
label: Judith

text: And the hart of Holofernes was ſtrooken: for he burnt in the concupiſcence of her.
label: Judith

text: And Holofernes ſaid to her: Drinke now, and ſit downe in ioyfulnes, becauſe thou haſt found grace before me.
label: Judith

text: And Iudith ſaid: I wil drinke my lord, becauſe my ſoule is magnified this day aboue al my dayes.
label: Judith

text: And she tooke, and did eate, and dranke before him thoſe thinges, which her handmayde had prepared her.
label: Judith

text: And Holofernes was made pleaſant toward her, and dranke wine exceeding much, ſo much as he had neuer drunke in his life?
label: Judith

text: AND when it was waxen late, his ſeruantes made haſt to their lodgings, and Vagao shut the chamber doores, and went his way.
label: Judith

text: And they were al ouerladen with wine.
label: Judith

text: And Iudith was alone in the chamber.
label: Judith

text: Moreouer Holofernes lay in his bed, faſt a ſlepe with very much drunkennes.
label: Judith

text: And Iudith ſaid to her mayd that ſhe should ſtand without before the chamber, and watch.
label: Judith

text: And Iudith ſtood before the bed, praying with teares, and with mouing of her lippes in ſilence,
label: Judith

text: ſaying: Confirme me o Lord God of Iſrael, and in this houre haue reſpect to the workes of my handes, that as thou haſt promiſed, thou mayſt aduance Ieruſalem thy citie: and I may bring to paſſe that which I beleuing that it may be done by thee, haue purpoſed.
label: Judith

text: And when she had ſayd theſe thinges, she went to the piller, that was at his beds head, and his ſword that hong tyed on it, she looſed.
label: Judith

text: And when she had drawen it out, she tooke him by the heare of his head, and ſayd: Confirme me ô Lord God in this houre,
label: Judith

text: and she ſtroke twiſe vpon his necke, and cut of his head, and tooke his canopie from the pillers, and rolled aſide his bodie a truncke.
label: Judith

text: And after a while she went out, and deliuered the head of Holofernes to her mayde, and bad her put it into her wallet.
label: Judith

text: And they two went forth, according to their cuſtome, as it were to prayer, and they paſſed the campe, and compaſſing the valley, they came to the gate of the citie.
label: Judith

text: And Iudith a far of ſaid to the keepers of the walles: Open the gates, becauſe God is with vs, which hath wrought power in Iſrael.
label: Judith

text: And it came to paſſe, when the men had heard her voyce, they called the ancientes of the citie.
label: Judith

text: And they ran al to meete her, from the leaſt to the greateſt: becauſe they hoped not that now she would come.
label: Judith

text: And they lighting lightes gathered round about her euerie one: and she going vp into a higher place, commanded ſilence to be made. And when al had held their peace,
label: Judith

text: Iudith ſaid: Prayſe yee the Lord our God, who hath not forſaken them that hope in him:
label: Judith

text: and in me his handmayde he hath fulfilled his mercie, which he promiſed to the houſe of Iſrael: and he hath killed by my hand the enemie of his people this night.
label: Judith

text: And bringing forth the head of Holofernes out of the wallet, she shewed it them, ſaying: Loe the head of Holofernes the general of the armie of the Aſſyrians, and behold his canopie, wherein he lay in his drunkennes, where the Lord our God ſtroke him by the hand of a woman.
label: Judith

text: But the ſame our Lord liueth, that his Angel hath kept me, both going hence, and abyding there, and from thence returning hither: and our Lord hath not ſuffered me his handmayde to be defyled, but without pollution of ſinne he hath called me backe to you, reioyſing in this victorie, in my eſcape, and in your deliuerie.
label: Judith

text: Confeſſe ye al to him, becauſe he is good, becauſe his mercie is for euer.
label: Judith

text: And they al adoring our Lord, ſaid to her: Our Lord hath bleſſed thee in his power, becauſe by thee he hath brought our enemies to nothing.
label: Judith

text: Moreouer Ozias the prince of the people of Iſrael, ſaid to her: Bleſſed art thou daughter of our Lord the high God aboue al wemen vpon the earth.
label: Judith

text: Bleſſed be our Lord, which made heauen and earth, which hath directed thee vnto the woundes of the head of the prince of our enemies.
label: Judith

text: Becauſe this day he hath ſo magnified thy name, that thy prayſe shal not depart out of the mouth of men, which shal be mindeful of the power of our Lord for euer, for that thou haſt not spared thy life for the diſtreſſes and tribulation of thy kinred, but haſt holpen the ruine before the preſence of our God.
label: Judith

text: And al the people ſayd: So be it, ſo be it.
label: Judith

text: Moreouer Achior being called came, and Iudith ſaid to him: The God of Iſrael, to whom thou gaueſt teſtimonie, that he reuengeth him ſelf of his enemies, he hath cut of the head of al the vnfaithful this night by my hand.
label: Judith

text: And that thou mayſt proue that it is ſo, loe the head of Holofernes, who in the contempt of his pride contemned the God of Iſrael: and threatened thee death, ſaying: When the people of Iſrael shal be taken, I wil command thy ſides to be pearſed with a ſword.
label: Judith

text: But Achior ſeing the head of Holofernes, being in anguish for feare, fel on his face vpon the earth, and his ſoule was ſore trubled.
label: Judith

text: But after taking ſpirit agayne he was refreshed, & fel downe at her feete, and adored her, and ſayd:
label: Judith

text: Bleſſed art thou of thy God in euerie tabernacle of Iacob, becauſe in euerie nation, which shal heare thy name, the God of Iſrael shal be magnified in thee.
label: Judith

text: AND Iudith ſaid to al the people: Heare me brethren, hang ye this head vpon our walles:
label: Judith

text: and it shal be, when the ſunne shal riſe, let euerie man take his armour, and yſſue ye forth with violence, not that you goe downe beneath, but as it were inuading violently.
label: Judith

text: Then the watchmen muſt of neceſſitie runne to rayſe vp their prince to battel.
label: Judith

text: And when the captaynes of them shal runne to the tabernacle of Holofernes, and shal finde him headles rowled in bloud, feare wil fal vpon them.
label: Judith

text: And when you shal know that they flee, goe after them ſecurely, becauſe our Lord wil deſtroy them vnder your feete.
label: Judith

text: Then Achior ſeeing the power, that God of Iſrael wrought, forſaking the rite of gentilitie, beleued God, and circuncided the flesh of his prepuce, and was ioyned to the people of Iſrael, and al the ſucceſſion of his kinred vntil this preſent day.
label: Judith

text: And immediatly as day brake, they hong the head of Holofernes vpon the walles, and euerie man tooke his armour, and they went forth with great noyſe and shouting.
label: Judith

text: Which the watchmen ſeing, ranne to the tabernacle of Holofernes.
label: Judith

text: Moreouer they that were in the tabernacle, coming, and before the dore of the tabernacle making a noyſe, to rayſe him, they endeuored by art to diſquiet him, that Holofernes might awake not by them rayſing him, but by them making a noyſe.
label: Judith

text: For no man durſt by knocking, or entring, to open the chamber of the chiefe of the Aſſyrians.
label: Judith

text: But when his dukes and tribunes were come, and al the chiefe of the armie of the king of the Aſſyrians, they ſaid to the chamberlayns:
label: Judith

text: Goe in, and awake him, becauſe the mice yſſuing out of their holes, haue preſumed to prouoke vs to battel.
label: Judith

text: Then Vagao entring into his chamber, ſtoode before the cortine, and made a clapping with his handes: for he thought that he ſlept with Iudith.
label: Judith

text: But when with the ſenſe of his eares he percieued no motion of perſon lying, he came neere to the cortine, and lifting it vp, and ſeing the bodie without the head of Holofernes weltred in his bloud lye vpon the ground, cried out in a lowd voyce with weeping, and rent his garmentes.
label: Judith

text: And going into the tabernacle of Iudith, he found her not, and he lept forth to the people,
label: Judith

text: and ſayd: One Hebrewe woman hath made confuſion in the houſe of king Nabuchodonoſor: for behold Holofernes lyeth vpon the ground, and his head is not vpon him.
label: Judith

text: Which when the princes of the power of the Aſſyrians had heard, they al rent their garmentes, and intollerable feare and dread fel vpon them, and theit mindes were trubled excedingly.
label: Judith

text: And there was made an incomparable crie in the middes of their campe.
label: Judith

text: AND when al the armie heard that Holofernes was beheaded, courage and counſel fel from them, and being shaken with trembling onlie and feare, they helpe them ſelues by flight,
label: Judith

text: ſo that none ſpake with his neighbour, but hanging the head, al thinges leaft behind, they made haſt to eſcape the Hebrewes, whom they heard to come armed vpon them, fleing by the waies of the fieldes, and the pathes of the hilles.
label: Judith

text: The children of Iſrael therfore ſeing them fleing, folowed them. And they went downe ſounding with trumpettes, and shouting after them.
label: Judith

text: And becauſe the Aſſyrians were not vnited together, they went headlong into flight: but the children of Iſrael purſewing in one companie, diſcomfited al that they could find.
label: Judith

text: Ozias therfore ſent meſſengers through al the cities and countries of Iſrael.
label: Judith

text: Euerie countrie therfore, and euerie citie ſent choſen youth armed after them, and they purſewed them in the edge of the ſword, vntil they came to the extremetie of their borders.
label: Judith

text: And the reſt that were in Bethulia, entered into the campe of the Aſſyrians, and tooke away the praye, which the Aſſyrians fleing had leaft, and were loden excedingly.
label: Judith

text: But they that were returned conquerers to Bethulia, tooke away with them al thinges that were theirs, ſo that there was no number in cattel, and beaſtes, and al their moueables, that from the leaſt vnto the greateſt al were made rich of their prayes.
label: Judith

text: And Ioachim the high Prieſt came from Ieruſalem into Bethulia with al his ancientes to ſee Iudith.
label: Judith

text: Who when she was come out to him, they al bleſſed her with one voyce, ſaying: Thou art the glorie of Ieruſalem, thou the ioy of Iſrael, thou the honour of our people:
label: Judith

text: becauſe thou haſt done manfully, and thy hart was ſtrengthened, for that thou haſt loued chaſtitie, and after thy husband not knowne any other: therfore alſo the hand of our Lord hath ſtrengthened thee, and therfore shalt thou be bleſſed for euer.
label: Judith

text: And al the people ſayd: So be it, ſo be it.
label: Judith

text: And for thirtie daies, ſcarſe were the ſpoyles of the Aſſyrians gathered of the people of Iſrael.
label: Judith

text: Moreouer al thinges, that were proued to be the peculiar goodes of Holofernes, they gaue to Iudith in gold, and ſiluer, and garmentes, and pretious ſtones, and al ſtuffe, and al the thinges were deliuered her of the people.
label: Judith

text: And al the people reioyſed with wemen, and virgins, and yongmen, on inſtrumentes and harpes.
label: Judith

text: THEN ſang Iudith this ſong to our Lord, ſaying:
label: Judith

text: Beginne ye to our Lord in timbrels, ſing ye to our Lord in cymbals, tune to him a new pſalme, reioyſe, and inuocate his name.
label: Judith

text: Our Lord confoundeth battels, Lord is his name.
label: Judith

text: Who hath ſet his campe in the middes of his people, that he might deliuer vs from the hand of al our enemies.
label: Judith

text: Aſſur came out of the mountaynes from the North in the multitude of his ſtrength: whoſe multitude ſtopped vp the torrentes, and their horſes couered the valles.
label: Judith

text: He ſaid that he would ſet my borders on fyre, and kil my yongmen with the ſword, to geue my infantes into praye, and virgins into captiuitie.
label: Judith

text: But our Lord omnipotent hath hurt him, and hath deliuered him into the hands of a woman, and hath pearſed him.
label: Judith

text: For, not by yongmen is their mightie one fallen, neither haue the ſonnes of Titan ſtrooken him, neither did the high giantes ſet them ſelues vpon him, but Iudith the daughter of Merari in the beautie of her face diſſolued him.
label: Judith

text: For she put from her the garmentes of widowhood, and put on her the garmentes of ioy, in the reioyſing of the children of Iſrael.
label: Judith

text: She anoynted her face with oyntment, and tyed together her lockes with a crowne, ſhe tooke a new ſtole to deceiue him.
label: Judith

text: Her ſandals rauished his eies, her beautie made his ſoule captiue, she with a ſword cut of his head.
label: Judith

text: The Perſians did quake at her conſtancie, and the Medes at her boldneſſe.
label: Judith

text: Then did the campe of the Aſſyrians howle, when my humble ones appeared, withering in thirſt.
label: Judith

text: The ſonnes of yongwemen haue pearſed them, and they haue killed them as boyes fleing away: they haue periſhed in battel before the face of the Lord my God.
label: Judith

text: Let vs ſing an hymne to our Lord, let vs ſing a new hymne to our God.
label: Judith

text: Adonai ô Lord great art thou, and noble in thy power, and whom no man can ouercome.
label: Judith

text: Let euerie creature of thyne ſerue thee: becauſe thou ſaydſt, and they were made: thou didſt ſend thy spirit, and they were created, and there is none that can reſiſt thy voyce.
label: Judith

text: The mountaynes with the waters shal be moued with the foundations: the rockes shal melt as waxe before thy face.
label: Judith

text: But they that feare thee, shal be great with thee in al thinges.
label: Judith

text: Wo be to the nation, that ryſeth vp vpon my kinred: for our Lord omnipotent wil be reuenged on them, in the day of iudgement he wil viſite them.
label: Judith

text: For he wil geue fyre, and wormes into their flesh, that they may be burnt, and may feele for euer.
label: Judith

text: And it came to paſſe after theſe thinges, al the people after the victorie came into Ieruſalem to adore our Lord: and forthwith as they were purified, they al offered holocauſtes, and vowes, and their promiſes.
label: Judith

text: Moreouer Iudith offered for an anathema of obliuion al the inſtrumentes of warre of Holofernes, which the people gaue her, and the canopie that her ſelf had taken away out of his chamber.
label: Judith

text: And the people was pleaſant according to the face of ſainctes, and for three monethes the ioy of this victorie was celebrated with Iudith.
label: Judith

text: And after thoſe daies euerie man returned into his houſe, and Iudith was made great in Bethulia, and she was more glorious to al the land of Iſrael.
label: Judith

text: There was alſo chaſtitie ioyned to her vertue, ſo that she knew not man al the daies of her life, after that Manaſſes her huſband was dead.
label: Judith

text: And on feſtiual daies she came forth with great glorie.
label: Judith

text: And she abode in her husbands houſe, an hundred fiue yeares, and diſmiſt her abra free, and she died and was buried with her huſband in Bethulia.
label: Judith

text: And al the people mourned for her ſeuen dayes.
label: Judith

text: And in al the space of her life there was not that trubled Iſrael, and after her death manie yeares.
label: Judith

text: But the day of the feſtiuitie of this victorie is receiued of the Hebrewes in the number of holie daies, and is worshiped of the Iewes from that time vntil this preſent day.
label: Judith

text: I N the daies of Aſſuerus. who reigned from India vnto Æthiopia ouer an hundred twentie ſeuen prouinces:
label: Esther

text: when he ſate in the throne of his kingdõ, the citie Suſã was in the begynning of his kingdom.
label: Esther

text: In the third yeare therfore of his empyre he made a great feaſt to al the princes, and to his ſeruantes, to the moſt valiant of the Perſians, and the nobles of the Medes, and the rulers of the prouinces in his ſight,
label: Esther

text: that he might shew the riches of the glorie of his kingdom, and the greatnes, & vaunting of his might, a great time, to witte, an hundred & foure ſcore dayes.
label: Esther

text: And when the daies of the feaſt were accomplished, he inuited al people, that was found in Suſan, from the greateſt to the leaſt: and commanded ſeuen daies a feaſt to be prepared in the entrance of the garden, and of the wood, which was planted with royal garnishing and with hand.
label: Esther

text: And there hong on euerie ſide hangings of skie colour, and grene, and hyacinthine colour, held vp with cordes of ſilke, and of purple, which were put into rings of yuorie, and were held vp with marble pillers. Beddes alſo of gold and ſiluer, were placed in order vpon the floore paued with the emerauld, and the touch ſtone: which paynting adorned with meruelous varietie.
label: Esther

text: And they that were inuited, dranke in golden cuppes, and the meates were brought in change of veſſels. Wine alſo plenteous and the beſt was ſet downe, as was worthie of a kings magnificence.
label: Esther

text: Neither was there that compelled them to drinke that would not, but as the king had appointed, making ech of his princes ouerſeer of euerie table, that euerie man might take what he would.
label: Esther

text: Vaſthi alſo the queene made a feaſt for the wemen in the palace, where king Aſſuerus had accuſtomed to remayne.
label: Esther

text: Therfore the ſeuenth day, when the king was merier, and after very much drinking was wel warmed with wine, he commanded Maumam, and Bazatha, and Harbona, and Bagatha, and Abgatha, and Zethar, and Charchas, the ſeuen eunuches, that miniſtred in his ſight,
label: Esther

text: that they should bring in queene Vaſthi before the king, the crowne ſet vpon her head, that he might shew her beautie to al the peoples and princes: for she was exceding beautiful.
label: Esther

text: Who refuſed, and contemned to come at the kings commandment, which he had commanded by the eunuches. Wherupon the king being wrath, and chaffed with exceding furie,
label: Esther

text: ( asked the wiſemen, which after the manner of a king were alwayes preſent with him, and he did al thinges by their counſel, which knew the lawes, and rightes of the elders:
label: Esther

text: (and the chiefe and neareſt him were, Charſena, and Sethar, and Admatha, and Tharſis, and Mares, and Marſana, and Mamuchan, ſeuen dukes of the Perſians, and of the Medes, which ſaw the face of the king, and were wont to ſitt firſt after him)
label: Esther

text: to what ſentence Vaſthi the queene should be ſubiect, that would not do Aſſuerus the kings commandment, which he had commanded by the eunuches.
label: Esther

text: And Mamuchan anſwered, the king hearing, and the princes: Queene Vaſthi hath not only hurt the king, but alſo al peoples, and princes, that are in al the prouinces of king Aſſuerus.
label: Esther

text: For the word of the queene wil goe forth to al wemen, that they wil contemne their husbands, and wil ſay: King Aſſuerus commanded that the queene Vaſthi ſhould come in to him, and she would not.
label: Esther

text: And by this example al the wiues of the princes of the Perſians and the Medes, wil little eſteeme the commandmentes of their husbandes: wherfore the kings indignation is iuſt.
label: Esther

text: If it pleaſe thee, let an edict goe forth from thy face, and let it be written according to the law of the Perſians and of Medes, which is not lawful to be tranſgreſſed, that Vaſthi come in no more to the king, but an other, that is better then ſhe, take her kingdome.
label: Esther

text: And let this be published into al the empire of thy prouinces (which is moſt large) and let al the wiues, as wel of the greater as of the leſſer geue honour to their husbandes.
label: Esther

text: His counſel pleaſed the king, and the princes: and the king did according to the counſel of Mamuchan,
label: Esther

text: and he ſent letters to al the prouinces of his kingdome, as euerie nation could heare and reade, in diuers languages and characters, that the husbandes should be princes and maiſters in their houſes: and that this ſhould be published through al peoples.
label: Esther

text: THESE thinges ſo done, after the indignation of king Aſſuerus was aſſwaged, he remembred Vaſthi, and what ſhe had done, or what she had ſuffered:
label: Esther

text: and the kings ſeruantes and his miniſters ſaid: Let there be maydens ſought for the king, virgins and beautiful,
label: Esther

text: and let there be ſent that may viewe through al prouinces beautiful maydens and virgins: and let them bring them to the citie of Suſan, and deliuer them into the houſe of wemen vnder the hand of Egeus the eunuch, who is ouerſeer of the kings wemen: and let them receiue wemens ornamentes, and other things neceſſarie to be vſed.
label: Esther

text: And which ſo euer among al shal pleaſe the kings eies, let her reigne for Vaſthi. The word pleaſed the king: and ſo as they had ſuggeſted, he commanded to be done.
label: Esther

text: There was a man in the citie of Suſan a Iew, named Mardocheus, the ſonne of Iair, the ſonne of Semei, the ſonne of Cis, of the ſtocke of Iemini,
label: Esther

text: who had beene tranſported from Ieruſalem the ſame time, that Nabucodonoſor the king of Babylon tranſported Iechonias the king of Iuda,
label: Esther

text: who was the foſter father of his brothers daughter Ediſſa, which by an other name was called Eſther: and she had loſt both her parentes: exceeding beautiful, and of comely face. And her father and mother being dead, Mardocheus adopted her for his daughter.
label: Esther

text: And when the kings commandment was bruited abrode, and according to his commandement many fayre virgins were brought to Suſan, and were deliuered to Egeus the eunuch: Eſther alſo among the reſt of the maydens was deliuered to him, that she might be kept in the number of the wemen.
label: Esther

text: Who pleaſed him, and found grace in his ſight. And he commanded the eunuch, that he should haſten the wemens ornamentes, and should deliuer her, her partes, & ſeuen the moſt beautiful maydens of the kings houſe, and should adorne and decke both her and her wayting maydes.
label: Esther

text: Who would not tel him her people and countrie. For Mardocheus had commanded her, that of this thing she should altogether keepe ſilence:
label: Esther

text: who walked daily before the entrance of the houſe, wherin the choſen virgins were kept, taking care of Eſthers welfare, and deſirous to know what should chance vnto her.
label: Esther

text: And when the time of euerie virgin in order was come, that they should goe in to the king, al things accomplished that perteyned to wemens ornamentes, it was the twelfth moneth: yet ſo, that for ſix monethes they were anoynted with oyle of myrtle, and other ſix monethes they vſed certayne payntings and ſweete ſpices.
label: Esther

text: And going in to the king, what ſoeuer they asked that perteyned to adorning they receiued: and being trimmed, as it pleaſed them, they paſſed from the chamber of the wemen to the kings chamber.
label: Esther

text: And she that went in at euening, came out in the morning, and from thence she was brought to the ſecond houſe, that was vnder the hand of Suſagazus the eunuch, who was chiefe ouer the kings concubines: neither had she power to returne any more to the king, vnleſſe the king had willed, and had commanded her to come by name.
label: Esther

text: And the time by order coming about, the day was at hand, that Eſther the daughter of Abihail the brother of Mardocheus, whom he had adopted for his daughter, should goe in to the king. Who ſought not wemens ornamentes, but whatſoeuer Egeus the eunuch the keper of the virgins would, thoſe things he gaue her to her adorning. For she was exceding fayre, and of incredible beautie, she ſemed to al mens eies gratious and amiable.
label: Esther

text: She therfore was brought to the chamber of king Aſſuerus the tenth moneth, which is called Tebeth, in the ſeuenth yeare of his reigne.
label: Esther

text: And the king loued her more then al the wemen, and she had grace and mercie before him aboue al the wemen, and he put the crowne of the kingdom on her head, and made her reigne in ſteede of Vaſthi.
label: Esther

text: And he commanded a verie magnifical feaſt to be prepared to al the princes, and to his ſeruantes, for the coniunction, and mariage of Eſther. And he gaue reſt to al the prouinces, and beſtowed giftes according to princely magnificence.
label: Esther

text: And when virgins were ſought the ſecond time and gathered together, Mardocheus taried at the kings gate,
label: Esther

text: neither had Eſther as yet vttered her countrie, & people, according to his cõmandment. For what ſoeuer he commanded, Eſther obſerued: and she did al thinges ſo as she was wont at that time, when he nourished her a litle one.
label: Esther

text: At that time therfore, when Mardocheus abode at the kings gate, Bagathan, and Thares were angrie, two of the kings eunuches, that were porters, and were chiefe in the firſt entrie of the palace: and they would make inſurrection againſt the king, and kil him.
label: Esther

text: Wherof Mardocheus gotte notice, and immediatly he told it to queene Eſther: and she to the king in the name of Mardocheus, who had reported the thing vnto her.
label: Esther

text: It was examined, and found: and they were both hanged on a gibbet. And it was put in the hiſtories, and regiſtred in the cronicles before the king.
label: Esther

text: AFTER theſe things king Aſſuerus aduanced Aman the ſonne of Amadathi, which was of the ſtocke of Agag: & he put his throne aboue al the princes which he had.
label: Esther

text: And al the kings ſeruantes, that were in the doores of his pallace, bowed their knees, and adored Aman: for ſo the emperour had commanded them, onlie Mardocheus did not bowe his knee, nor adore him.
label: Esther

text: To whom the kings ſeruantes, that were chiefe at the doores of the pallace, ſaid: Why doeſt thou aboue the reſt not obſerue the kings commandment.
label: Esther

text: And when they ſaid this often, and he would not heare, they told Aman, deſirous to know whether he would perſeuere in his ſentence: for he had told them that he was a Iew.
label: Esther

text: Which when Aman had heard, and had proued by experience that Mardocheus bowed not his knee vnto him, nor adored him, he was angrie excedingly.

text: And he counted it a matter of nothing to lay his handes vpon Mardocheus alone: for he had heard that he was of the nation of the Iewes, and he would rather deſtroy al the nation of the Iewes, that were in the kingdom of Aſſuerus.
label: Esther

text: The firſt moneth (which is called Niſan) in the twelfth yeare of the reigne of Aſſuerus; the lot was caſt into a potte which in Hebrew is called Phur, before Aman, in what day and what moneth the nation of the Iewes should be ſlayne: and there came forth the twelfth moneth, which is called Adar.
label: Esther

text: And Aman ſaid to king Aſſuerus: There is a people diſperſed through al the prouinces of thy kingdom, and ſeparated one from an other, vſing new lawes and ceremonies, moreouer alſo contemning the kings ordinances: And thou knoweſt very wel that it is not expedient for thy kingdom that they waxe inſolent by libertie.
label: Esther

text: If it pleaſe thee, decree that they may perish, and I wil pay ten thouſand talentes to the cofferers of thy treaſure.
label: Esther

text: and he ſaid to him: The ſiluer which thou doeſt promiſe, be it thine: but concerning the people doe that which pleaſeth thee.
label: Esther

text: And the kings ſcribes were called in the firſt moneth, Niſan, the thirtenth day of the ſame moneth: and there was written, as Aman had commanded, to al the kings lieuftenantes, and iudges of the prouinces, and of diuers nations, as euerie nation could read, and heare according to the varietie of languages, in the name of king Aſſuerus: and the letters ſigned with his ring,
label: Esther

text: WHICH things when Mardocheus had heard, he rent his garmentes, and was clothed with ſackcloth, ſprinkling ashes on his head: and in the ſtreat of the middes of the citie he cried with a lowed voyce, shewing the anguish of his mind,

text: And Eſthers maides and the eunuches went in, and told her. Which she hearing was aſtonyed: and she ſent a garment, that the ſackcloth being taken away, they should put it on him: which he would not take.

text: for if thou wilt now hold thy peace, the Iewes shal be deliuered by an other occaſion: and thou, and thy fathers houſe shal perish. And who knoweth whether thou cameſt to the kingdom therfore, that in ſuch a time thou mightſt be readie?

text: And the king by and by, who is, quoth he, in the court? For Aman had entered the inner court of the kings houſe, that he might ſuggeſt to the king, and ne might command Mardocheus to be hanged faſt on the gibbet, which was prepared for him.

label: Esther

label: Esther

text: To whom she anſwered, If I haue found grace in thyne eies ô king, and if it pleaſe thee, geue me my life for the which I make requeſt, and my people for the which I beſech.

text: and al thinges, which are conteyned in the hiſtorie of this booke, which is called Eſther.

label: Esther

text: Whoſe ſtrength and empire, and the dignitie and highneſſe, wherewith he exalted Mardocheus, are written in the bookes of the Medes, and of the Perſians:
label: Esther

text: and how Mardocheus of the Iewes kinred was ſecond after king Aſſuerus: and great with the Iewes, and acceptable to the people of his bretheren, ſeking good to his people, and ſpeaking thoſe things, which pertayned to the good of his ſeede.
label: Esther

text: And Mardocheus ſaid: Theſe things are done of God.

label: Esther

label: Esther

text: But the two dragons: I am, and Aman.
label: Esther

text: The nations, that were aſſembled: are they that endeuoured to deſtroy the name of the Iewes.
label: Esther

text: And my nation: is Iſrael, which cried to, our Lord, and our Lord hath ſaued his people: and he hath deliuered vs from al euils, and hath done great ſignes and wonders among the nations:
label: Esther

text: and he commanded that there ſhould be two lottes, one of the people of God, and the other of al Nations.
label: Esther

text: And both lottes are come to the day appointed euen now from that time before God to al nations:
label: Esther

text: and our Lord hath remembred his people, and hath had mercie on his inheritance.
label: Esther

text: And theſe daies shal be obſerued in the moneth of Adar the fourtenth, and fiſtenth day of the ſame moneth, with al diligence, and ioy of the people gathered into one aſſemblie, through out al the generations hereafter of the people of Iſrael.
label: Esther

text: IN the fourth yeare when Ptolomee and Cleopatra reigned, Doſitheus, which named himſelf a Prieſt, and of the Leuitical kinred, and Ptolomee his ſonne brought this epiſtle of Phurim, which they ſayd Lyſimachus the ſonne of Ptolomee did interprete in Ieruſalem.
label: Esther

text: In the ſecond yeare, when Artaxerxes the greateſt reigned, in the firſt day of the moneth Niſan, Mardocheus the ſonne of Iairi, the ſonne of Semei, the ſonne of Cis, of the tribe of Beniamin.
label: Esther

text: A Iew which dwelt in the citie of Suſan, a great man and among the firſt of the kings court, ſaw a dreame.
label: Esther

text: And he was of that number of captiues, whom Nabuchodonoſor the king of Babylon had tranſported from Ieruſalem with Ieconias the king of Iuda:
label: Esther

text: and this was his dreame: Thete appeared voices, and tumultes, and thunders and earth quakes, and perturbation vpon the earth:
label: Esther

text: and behold two great dragons, prepared one againſt an other into battel.
label: Esther

text: At whoſe crie al nations were rayſed vppe, to fight againſt the nation of the iuſt.
label: Esther

text: And that was a day of darkeneſſe and danger, of tribulation and diſtreſſe, and great feare vpon the earth.
label: Esther

text: And the nation of the iuſt fearing their euils, was trubled, and prepared to death.
label: Esther

text: And they cried to God: and they cyring, a litle fountayne grew into a verie great riuer, and abounded into verie manie waters.
label: Esther

text: Light and ſunne aroſe, and the humble were exalted, and they deuoured the glorious.
label: Esther

text: Which when Mardocheus had ſeene, and riſen out of his bed, he muſed what God would doe: and he had it fixed in his mind, deſirous to know what the dreame ſhould ſignifie?
label: Esther

text: AND he abode that time in the kings court with Bagatha and Thara the kings eunuches, which were porters of the palace.
label: Esther

text: And when he vnderſtood their cogitations, and had throughly ſeene their cares he learned that they went about to lay hands on king Artaxerxes, and he told the king therof.
label: Esther

text: Who hauing them both in examination, when they had confeſſſd he commanded them to be led to death.
label: Esther

text: But the king wrote that which was done, in the comentaries: and Mardocheus alſo committed the memorie of the thing to wriring.
label: Esther

text: And the king commanded him, that he ſhould abide in the court of the palace, geuing him giftes for the delation.
label: Esther

text: But Aman the ſonne of Amadathi the Bugeite was moſt glorious before the king, and would hurt Mardocheus, and his people, for the two eunuches of the king, which were put to death.
label: Esther

text: AND this was the copie of the letter. The moſt great king Artaxerxes from India vnto Æthiopia, to the princes of an hundred and ſeuen and twentie prouinces, and to the captaynes, that are ſubiect to his empire, greeting.
label: Esther

text: Wheras I reigned ouer manie nations, and had ſubdewed al the world to my dominion, I would not abuſe the greatnes of my might, but with clemencie and lenitie gouerne my ſubiectes, that paſſing their life quietly without any terrour, they might enioy peace wiſhed of al men.
label: Esther

text: But when I demanded of my counſelers how this might be accompliſhed, one that excelled the reſt in wiſedom and fidelitie, and was ſecond after the king, Aman by name,
label: Esther

text: told me that there was a people diſperſed through the whole world, which vſed new lawes, and doing againſt the cuſtomes of al Nations, contemned the cōmandmentes of kings, and brake the concord of al nations by their diſſention.
label: Esther

text: Which when we had learned, ſeing one nation rebellious againſt al kind of men to vſe peruerſe lawes, and to goe againſt our commandmentes, and to diſturbe the peace and concord of the prouinces ſubiect to vs,
label: Esther

text: we haue commanded that whomſoeuer Aman ſhal ſhew, who is chiefe ouer al the prouinces, and ſecond after the king, and whom we honour in ſteed of a father, they with their wiues and children be deſtroyed of their enemies, and that none haue pitie on them the fourtenth day of the twelfth moneth Adar of this preſent yeare:
label: Esther

text: that the wicked men going downe to hel in one day, may reſtore the peace to our empire, which they had diſturbed.
label: Esther

text: But Mardocheus beſought our Lord, mindeful of al his workes,
label: Esther

text: and ſaid: Lord Lord king omnipotent, for in thy dominion are al thinges ſet, and there is none that can reſiſt thy wil, if thou determine to ſaue Iſrael.
label: Esther

text: Thou madſt heauen and earth, and whatſoeuer is conteyned in the compaſſe of heauen.
label: Esther

text: Thou art Lord of al, neither is there that can reſiſt thy maieſtie.
label: Esther

text: Thou vnderſtandeſt al things, and knoweſt that I haue not done this for pride and contumelie, and any deſire of glorie, that I adored not the proud Aman,
label: Esther

text: ( for gladly would I be readie for the ſaluation of Iſrael to kiſſe euen the ſteppes of his feete,)
label: Esther

text: but I feared leſt I should tranſferre the honour of my God to a man, and leſt I ſhould adore any except my God.
label: Esther

text: And now ô Lord king, the God of Abraham haue mercie vpon thy poople, becauſe our enemies wil deſtroy vs, and extinguish thyne inheritance.
label: Esther

text: Deſpiſe not thy portion, which thou haſt redemed to thyſelf out of Ægypt.
label: Esther

text: Heare my prayer, and be propitious to thy lot and corde, and turne our mourning into ioy, that liuing we may prayſe thy name ô Lord, and doe not ſhut the mouthes of them that ſing to thee.
label: Esther

text: Al Iſrael alſo with like mind and ſupplication cried to our Lord, becauſe certayne death did hang ouer them.
label: Esther

text: ESTHER alſo the queene fled to our Lord, fearing the peril that was at hand.
label: Esther

text: And when she had laid of her royal garmentes, she tooke clothes meete for weeping and mourning, and for diuers oyntmentes, filled her head with aſhes and dung, and her bodie ſhe humbled with faſtes: and al the places, in which before ſhe was accuſtomed to reioyſe, ſhe filled with tearing of her heares.
label: Esther

text: And she beſought our Lord the God of Iſrael, ſaying: My Lord, which onlie art our king, helpe me ſolitarie woman, and which haue no other helper beſide thee.
label: Esther

text: My peril is in my handes.
label: Esther

text: I haue heard of my father that thou Lord didſt take Iſrael out from al Gentiles, and our fathers out of al their predeceſſours before, that thou mightſt poſſeſſe an euerlaſting inheritance, and thou haſt done to them as thou haſt ſpoken.
label: Esther

text: We haue ſinned in thy ſight, and therfore thou haſt deliuered vs into the handes of our enemies:
label: Esther

text: for we haue worshiped their goddes. Thou art iuſt ô Lord.
label: Esther

text: And now it ſuffiſeth them not, that they oppreſſe vs with moſt hard ſeruitude, but imputing the force of their handes to the might of their idols,
label: Esther

text: they wil change thy promiſſes, and deſtroy thine inheritance, and ſhut the mouthes of them that prayſe thee, and extinguish the glorie of thy temple and altar,
label: Esther

text: that they may open the mouthes of Gentiles, and prayſe the ſtrength of idols, and magnifie a carnal king for euer.
label: Esther

text: Deliuer not ô Lord thy ſcepter to them that are not, leſt they laugh at our ruine: but turne their counſel vpon them, and deſtroy him, that hath begune to do cruelly againſt vs.
label: Esther

text: Remember ô Lord: and shew thy ſelf to vs in the time of our tribulation, and geue me confidence Lord king of goddes, and of al power:
label: Esther

text: geue me ſpeach wel framed in my mouth in the preſence of the lion, and turne his hart into the hatred of our enemie, that both him ſelf may perish, and the reſt that conſent vnto him.
label: Esther

text: But deliuer vs in thy hand, and helpe me, hauing no other helpe, but thee ô Lord which haſt the knowlege of al things,
label: Esther

text: and knoweſt that I hate the glorie of the wicked, and deteſt the bed of the vncircumciſed, and of euerie ſtranger.
label: Esther

text: Thou knoweſt my neceſſitie, that I abhorre the ſigne of my pride and glorie, which is vpon my head in the daies of my oſtentation, and deteſt it as the cloth of a woman in her monthlie floores, and weare it not in the daies of my ſilence,
label: Esther

text: and that I haue not eaten at Amans table, neither the kings banket hath pleaſed me, and that I haue not drunke the wine of libamentes:
label: Esther

text: and that thy handmayde did neuer reioyſe, ſince I was tranſported hither vnto this day, but in thee ô Lord the God of Abraham.
label: Esther

text: O God ſtrong aboue al, heare the voyce of them, that haue no other hope, and deliuer vs from the hand of the wicked, and deliuer me from my feare.
label: Esther

text: AND he commanded her (no doubt but Mardocheus commanded Eſther) that she ſhould goe vnto the king, and make petition for her people and for her countrie.
label: Esther

text: Remember (quoth he) the daies of thy humilitie, how thou waſt brought vp in my hand, becauſe Aman the ſecond after the king hath spoken againſt vs vnto death:
label: Esther

text: and doe thou inuocate our Lord, and speake to the king for vs, & deliuer vs from death.
label: Esther

text: And in the third day she layd away the garmentes which she ware, & was clothed in her glorie.
label: Esther

text: And when she gliſtered in royal apparel, and had inuocated God the ruler and ſauiour of al, she tooke two wayting maydes,

text: and vpon the one in deede she leaned, as it were for dilicatnes and verie much tendernes not able to beare vp her bodie:
label: Esther

text: but the other of the maydes folowed her ladie, bearing vp her garmentes trayling on the ground.
label: Esther

text: But her ſelf in al her countenance of colour like the roſe, alſo with gratious and ſhining eies hid her mind ful of ſorow, and exceding feare.
label: Esther

text: She therfore entring through al the doores in order, ſtood before the king, where he ſate vpon the throne of his kingdom, clothed with royal garmentes, and glittering in gold, and pretious ſtones, and he was terrible to behold.
label: Esther

text: And when he had lifted vp his face, and with burning eies had ſhewed the furie of his breaſt, the Queene fel downe, and her colour being changed into palenes, she reſted her wearie head vpon her handmayde.
label: Esther

text: And God turned the kings ſpirit in to mildnes, and in haſt and fearing he lept out of the throne, and holding her vp in his armes, til ſhe came to her ſelf, ſpake her fayre with theſe wordes:
label: Esther

text: What ayleth thee Eſther? I am thy brother, feare not.
label: Esther

text: Thou shalt not die: for this law is not made for thee, but for the common ſorte.
label: Esther

text: Come neere therfore, and touch the ſcepter.
label: Esther

text: And when ſhe held her peace, he tooke the golden rod, & put it vpon her necke, and kiſſed her, and ſayd: Why ſpeakeſt thou not to me?
label: Esther

text: Who anſwered: I ſaw thee, my Lord, as an angel of God, and my hart was trubled for the feare of thy glorie.
label: Esther

text: For thou, my lord, art exceding maruelous, and thy face is ful of graces
label: Esther

text: And when she spake, she fel downe agayne, and was almoſt in a ſowne.
label: Esther

text: But the king was trubled, and al his ſeruantes did comfort her.
label: Esther

text: THE great king Artaxerxes, from India to Æthiopia to the dukes and princes of an hundred twentie ſeuen prouinces, which obey our commandment, ſendeth greeting.
label: Esther

text: Manie haue abuſed vnto pride the goodnes of princes, and the honour, that hath beene beſtowed vpon them:
label: Esther

text: and they do not only endeuour to oppreſſe the kings ſubiectes, but not bearing the glorie that is geuen them, they worke treaſon againſt them that gaue it.
label: Esther

text: Neither are they content not to geue thankes for the benefittes, and to violate in them ſelues the lawes of humanitie, but they thincke they can eſcape the ſentence of God alſo who ſeeth al things.
label: Esther

text: And they haue burſt forth into ſo great madnes, that ſuch as obſerue diligently the offices committed vnto them, and do al thinges ſo that they are worthie of al mens prayſe, them they endeuour to ouerthrow by ſubtil meanes of lies,
label: Esther

text: whiles with craftie fraude they deceiue the ſimple eares of princes, and eſteming others by their owne nature.
label: Esther

text: Which thing is proued both out of old hiſtories, and by theſe thinges, which are done daily, how the enterpriſes of kinges are depraued by the euil ſuggeſtions of certaine men
label: Esther

text: Wherfore we muſt prouide for the peace of al prouinces.
label: Esther

text: Neither muſt you thincke, if we command diuers things, that it cometh of the lightneſſe of our mind, but that we geue ſentence according to the qualitie & neceſſitie of times, as the profite of the common wealth requireth
label: Esther

text: And that you may more plainly vnderſtand, that which we ſay, Aman the ſonne of Amadathi, both in mind and countrie a Macedonian, and an aliene from the Perſians bloud, and with his crueltie ſtayning our pietie, was receiued of vs a ſtranger:
label: Esther

text: and found our humanitie ſo great towardes him, that he was called our father, and was adored of al ſecond after the king:
label: Esther

text: who was puft vp with ſo great ſwelling of arrogancie, that he went about to depriue vs of kingdom and life.
label: Esther

text: For by certaine new deuiſes and not heard of before he hath ſought to kil Mardocheus, by whoſe fidelitie and benefittes we liue, and Eſther the felow of our kingdom with al their nation:
label: Esther

text: thincking this that they being ſlayne, he might worke treaſon to our ſolitarines, and might tranſferre the kingdom of the Perſians to the Macedonians
label: Esther

text: But we haue found the Iewes, which were by that moſt wicked of men oppoynted to be ſlayne, in no fault at al, but contrariwiſe vſing iuſt lawes,
label: Esther

text: and the children of the higheſt and the greateſt, and alwayes louing God, by whoſe benefite the kingdom was geuen both to our fathers and to vs, and is kept vnto this day.
label: Esther

text: Wherfore know ye thoſe letters, which he directed in our name, to be of none effect.
label: Esther

text: For the which heinous fact, before the gates of this citie, that is, of Suſan, both him ſelf that deuiſed it, and al his kinred hang on gibbettes: not we, but God repaying him that which he hath deſerued.
label: Esther

text: But this edict, which we now ſend, let it be ſet forth in al cities, that it be lawful for the Iewes to vſe their owne lawes.
label: Esther

text: Whom you muſt helpe, that thoſe, which had prepared them ſelues to their ſlaughter, they may kil the thirtenth day of the twelfth moneth, which is called Adar.
label: Esther

text: For God omnipotent hath turned this day of ſadnes and mourning into ioy to them.
label: Esther

text: Wherfore count you alſo this day among other feſtiual daies, and celebrate it with al ioy, that hereafter alſo it may be knowne,
label: Esther

text: that al, which faythfully obey the Perſians, receiue worthie reward for their fidelitie: and they that lie in wayte againſt their kingdom, perish for their wicked fact.
label: Esther

text: And euerie prouince and citie, that wil not be partaker of this ſolemnitie, let it perish by ſword and fyre, and let it ſo be deſtroyed, that not onlie men, but alſo beaſtes haue no acceſſe therto for euer, for an example of contempt, and diſobedience.
label: Esther

text: AND it came to paſſe, after that Alexander Philips ſonne the Macedonian, that firſt reigned in Greece, being gone out of the land of Cethim, ſtroke Darius king of the Perſians and the Medes:
