text: There appeared alſo two other yong men comely for ſtrength, excellent of glorie, and beautiful in attyre: which ſtood about him, and on both ſides whipped him, beating him with manie ſtripes without intermiſſion.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Heliodorus ſodenly fel on the ground, & they tooke him being couered round about with much darkenes, and being ſet in a ſeate portatiue, they thruſt him forth.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he that with manie currers, and men of his garde entered into the foreſayde treaſurie, was caried no man geuing him ſuccourſe, the manifeſt powre of God being knowne.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he in deede by the powre of God lay dumbe, and depriued of al hope, and health.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But they bleſſed our Lord, becauſe he magnified his place: and the temple, that a little before was ful of feare and tumult, almightie God appearing, was filled with ioy and gladnes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And then certaine of the freindes of Heliodorus forthwith deſired Onias, that he would inuocate the higheſt to geue him life, who was at the very laſt gaſpe.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the highprieſt conſidering leaſt perhaps the king might ſuſpect ſome malice on the Iewes part downe aboute Heliodorns, offered for the health of the man an healthful hoſt.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when the highprieſt by prayer obteyned, the ſelfe ſame yong men, clothed with the ſame garments, ſtanding by Heliodorus, ſayd: Geue thankes to Onias the prieſt: for him hath our Lord geuen thee life.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But thou being ſcourged of God, declare vnto al men the great workes and the powre of God. And theſe thinges being ſayd, they appeared no more.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Heliodorus hauing offered an hoſt to God, and hauing promiſed great vowes to him, that granted him to liue, and geuing thankes to Onias, taking his armie againe returned to the king.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he teſtified to al men thoſe workes of the great God, which he had ſeene before his owne eyes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when the king had asked Heliodorus; who was meete to be ſent yet once more to Ieruſalem, he ſayd:
label: 2 Machabees

text: If thou haue anie enemie, or traytour to thy kingdome, ſend him thither, and thou shalt receiue him againe ſcourged, if yet he eſcape: becauſe there is vndoubtedly in the place a certaine powre of God.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For he that hath his dwelling in the heauens, is the viſiter, and helper of that place, & them that come to doe euil, he ſtriketh, and deſtroyeth.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Therefore concerning Heliodorus, and the keping of the treaſurie ſo the matter ſtandeth.
label: 2 Machabees

text: BVT Simon the foreſayde betrayer of the money, and of his countrie, ſpake il of Onias, as though he had ſtirred vp Heliodorus to theſe thinges, and had bene the mouer of the euils:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and the prouider for the citie, and defender of his nation, and the emulatour of the law of God, he preſumed to cal a ſecret betrayer of the kingdom.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But when the emnities proceeded ſo far, that murders alſo were committed by certaine of Simons familiars:
label: 2 Machabees

text: Onias conſidering the peril of the contention, and that Appollonius being gouernour of Cæleſyria, and Phænicia, was outragious, which encreaſed the malice of Simon, went to the king,
label: 2 Machabees

text: not as an accuſer of the citizens, but conſidering with himſelf the common profite of the whole multitude.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For he ſaw that without the kings prouidence it was vnpoſſible that peace should be made in thoſe matters, & that Simon would not ceaſe from his follie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But after Seleucus departure out of life, when Antiochus that was called the Noble, had taken the kingdom vpon him, Iaſon the brother of Onias ambiciouſly ſought the highprieſthood:
label: 2 Machabees

text: going to the king, promiſing him three hundred three ſcore talents of ſiluer, and of other reuenewes foure ſcore talents,
label: 2 Machabees

text: aboue this he promiſed alſo an hundred fiftie more, if leaue might be granted him to make a ſchole, and a place for youth, and to intitle them, that were at Ieruſalem, Antiochians.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Which when the king had granted, and he had obteyned the princedom, forthwith he began to tranſport his countrie men to the heathen rite.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And theſe thinges being taken away, which of fauoure had bene decreed by kinges vnto the Iewes, and through Iohn the father of the Eupolemus, who was embaſſadour with the Romans concerning amitie and ſocietie, he diſanulling the lawful rites of the citizens, made wicked ordinances.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For he preſumed vnder the verie caſtle to ſet vp a ſchoole, and to put al the goodlieſt youthes in brothel houſes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And this was not the beginning, but a certaine increaſe, and going forward of the heathen and ſtrange conuerſation, through the abhominable neuer heard before, of Iaſon the impious and not a prieſt.
label: 2 Machabees

text: So that the prieſtes were not now occupied about the offices of the altar, but the temple being contemned, & the ſacrifices neglected, they haſtened to be pertakers of the gamme of wraſtling, and of the vniuſt maintenance therof, and in the exerciſe of the coyte.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And ſetting nought by the honours of their fathers, they eſteemed the Greeke glories for the beſt:
label: 2 Machabees

text: by reaſon wherof they had dangerous contention, and they had emulation toward their ordinances, and in al thinges they coueted to be like to them, whom they had enemies and murderers.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For to doe impiouſly againſt the lawes of God eſcapeth not vnpunished, but this the time folowing wil declare.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when the gamme vſed euerie fifth yeare was kept at Tyre, and the king was preſent,
label: 2 Machabees

text: the wicked Iaſon ſent from Ieruſalem ſinful men, carying three hundred didrachmaes of ſiluer for the ſacrifice of Hercules, which they that caryed it, requeſted that it might not be beſtowed on the ſacrifices, becauſe it ought not, but that it might be deputed for other charges.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And theſe were offered in dede by him that ſent them, vnto the ſacrifice of Hercules: but becauſe of them that were preſent they were geuen to the making of gallees.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Apollonius the ſonne of Mneſtheus being ſent into Ægypt becauſe of the nobles of Ptolomee Philometor the king, when Antiochus vnderſtood that himſelf was made an alien from the affaires of the kingdom, prouiding for his owne commodities, departing thence he came to Ioppe, and from thence to Ieruſalem.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And being magnifically receiued of Iaſon, and the citie, entered in with torch lights, and with prayſes: and from thence he turned his armie into Phænicia.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And after the time of three yeares Iaſon ſent Menelaus brother of the foreſaide Simon, carying money to the king, and to bring anſwers of neceſſarie affayres.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But he being commended to the king, when he had magnified the preſence of his power, wreſted the high prieſthood vpon him ſelf, ouer bidding Iaſon three hundred talents of ſiluer.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And hauing receiued commiſſion from the king, he came, hauing in deede nothing worthie of the prieſthood: but bearing the mind of a cruel tyrant, and the wrath of a wilde beaſt.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Iaſon indeede who had circumuented his owne brother, being himſelf deceiued was driuen out a fugitiue into the countrie of the Ammanites.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Menelaus obteyned the princedom: but concerning the money promiſed to the king he did nothing, wheras Soſtratus that was gouernour of the caſtel exacted it.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For to him perteyned the exacting of the tributes: for which cauſe they were both called out to the king.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Menelaus was remoued from the prieſthood, Lyſimachus his brother ſucceeding: and Soſtratus was made gouernour of the Cyprians.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when theſe things were a doing, it chanced the Tharſians, and the Mallotians to moue ſedition, becauſe they were geuen for a gift to king Antiochus concubine.
label: 2 Machabees

text: The king therfore came in haſt to pacifie them, one of his companions Adronicus being lefte ſubſtitute.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Menelaus ſuppoſing that he had taken a conuenient time, ſtealing certaine veſſels of gold out of the temple, gaue them to Adronicus, and others he had ſould at Tyre, & in their neere cities:
label: 2 Machabees

text: Which thing when Onias vnderſtood moſt certainly, he rebuked him, keeping himſelf in a ſafe place at Antioche beſide Daphne.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Wherupon Menelaus coming to Andronicus, deſired him to kil Onias. Who when he was come to Onias, and right handes being geuen with an oath (although he was ſuſpected of him) had perſwaded him to come out of the ſanctuarie, immediatly he ſlew him, not reuerencing iuſtice.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For which cauſe not only the Iewes, but alſo other nations likewiſe were offended, and tooke it greuouſly for the vniuſt murder of ſo great a man.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But when the king was returned out of the places of Cilicia, the Iewes went vnto him at Antioch, and alſo the Greekes: complayning of the vniuſt murder of Onias.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Antiochus therefore was ſorie in his minde for Onias, and being inclined to pitie, he shed teares, remembring the ſobrietie and modeſtie of the deceaſed.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And his hart being incenſed, he commanded Andronicus being ſpoiled of the purple, to be led about al the citie: and that in the ſame place, wherin he had committed the impiety vpon Onias, the ſacrilegious perſon should be depriued of his life, our Lord repaying him worthie punishment.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And manie ſacrilegies being committed of Lyſimachus in the temple by the counſel of Menelaus, and the rumour being bruited abrode, the multitude gathered together againſt Lyſimachus, much gold being now caryed out.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But the multitudes making inſurrection, and their mindes replenished with anger, Lyſimachus arming almoſt three thouſand began to vſe vniuſt handes, a certaine tyrant being captaine farre growne in age, and alſo in madnes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But as they vnderſtood the endeuour of Lyſimachus, ſome tooke ſtones, ſome ſtrong clubbles: and certaine threw ashes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And manie in deede were wounded, & certaine alſo throwne to the ground, but al were put to flight: the ſacrilegious perſon alſo himſelf they ſlew beſide the treaſurie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Concerning theſe thinges therefore iudgement began to be commenced againſt Menelaus.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when the king was come to Tyre, three men ſent from the ancients, put vp the matter vnto him.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when Menelaus was ouercome, he promiſed Ptolomee to geue much money to perſwade the king.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Ptolomee therfore went to the king being in a certaine courte, as it were to coole himſelf, and brought him from his purpoſe:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and Menelaus certes being guiltie of al the euil was quitted of the crimes: and the poore wretches, who if they had pleaded the cauſe euen before Scythians should be iudged innocent, them he commanded to death.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Quickly then did they vniuſtly ſuffer, which proſecuted the cauſe for the citie, & the people, and the ſacred veſſels.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For the which thing the Tyrians alſo being offended, were very liberal towards the burial of them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Menelaus becauſe of their auarice that were in power, continewed in authoritie, increaſing in malice to the betraying of the citizens.
label: 2 Machabees

text: AT the ſame time Antiochus prepared a ſecond iourney into Ægypt.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And it came to paſſe: that through out the whole citie of Ieruſalem were ſenne for fourtie dayes in the ayre horſemen running hither & thither, hauing golden ſtoles, and ſpeares, as it were companies armed,
label: 2 Machabees

text: and courſing of horſes ſet in orders by rankes, and that there were encounterings together neere hand, and shakings of sheildes, and a multitude of men in helmets with ſwordes drawen, and throwing of darts, and the glittering of golden armour, and of al kind of harnes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Wherefore al prayed that the wonders might be turned to good.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But when there was a falſe rumour gone forth, as though Antiochus had bene parted this life, Iaſon taking vnto him no leſſe then a thouſand men, ſuddenly ſet vpon the citie: and the citizens flying together to the wal, at the laſt the citie being taken, Menelaus fled into the caſtel.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Iaſon ſpared not his citizens in murder, nor conſidered, that proſperitie againſt kinſmen is a verie great euil, ſuppoſing that he should take the victorious ſpoiles of the enemies, and not of his citizens.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the princedome verily he obteyned not, but receiued confuſion, the end of his treacherie, and went againe a fugitiue into the countrie of the Ammanites.
label: 2 Machabees

text: At the laſt to his owne deſtruction being incloſed of Aretas the tyrant of the Arabians, flying from citie to citie, odious to al men, as an apoſtata from the lawes, and execrable, as an enemie of his countrie and citizens, he was thruſt out into Egypt:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and he that had expelled manie out of their countrie, perished in a ſtrange place, going to the Lacedemonians, as being like for kindred ſake to haue refuge there:
label: 2 Machabees

text: but he that caſt away manie vnburyed, himſelfe both vnlamented, and vnburyed is caſt forth, neither enioying forrein buryal, nor partaker of the ſepulcher of his fathers .
label: 2 Machabees

text: Theſe thinges therefore being done, the king ſuſpected that the Iewes would forſake the ſocietie: and for this departing out of Ægypt with a furious mind, he tooke the citie by armes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he bad the ſouldiars kil, and not ſpare them that came in their way, to murder them that went vp into the houſes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Slaughters therfore were made of youngmen & old, and deſtructions of wemen and children, and murders of virgins and litle ones.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And there were in the whole three dayes foure ſcore thouſand ſlaine, fourtie thouſand priſoners, and no leſſe ſold.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But neither do theſe thinges ſuffice, he preſumed alſo to enter into the temple, in al the earth the moſt holie, Menelaus being his leader, who was betrayer of the lawes, and his countrie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And with wicked handes taking the holie veſſels, which by other kinges and cities were ſet for the ornament and the glorie of the place, he vnworthily handled and contaminated them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: So Antiochus being alienated in minde, conſidered not, that for the ſinnes of them that inhabit the citie, God had bene angrie a litle: for the which alſo hapned the contempte about the place:
label: 2 Machabees

text: otherwiſe vnles it had chanced them to haue bene wrapped in manie ſinnes, as Heliodorus, who was ſent of Seleucus the king to ſpoile the treaſurie, this man alſo immediately as he came had bene ſcourged, and repelled verily from his boldnes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But not the nation for the place, but the place for the nation hath God choſen.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And therefore the place alſo it ſelf is made partaker of the peoples euils: but afterward it shal be partaker of the good thinges, and it that was forſaken in the wrath of almightie God, shal be exalted againe with great glorie in the reconciliation of the great Lord.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Therefore Antiochus hauing taken away out of the temple a thouſand and eight hundred talents, ſpedily went backe to Antioch, thinking through pride, that he might bring the land to ſayle vpon, & the ſea to goe vpon, through haughtines of minde.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he left alſo rulers to afflict the nation: at Ieruſalem, Philip a Phrygian borne, more cruel of maners then he himſelf by whom he was appointed:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and in Garizim Andronicus and Menelaus, who lay more greiuouſly vpon the citizens then the reſt.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And wheras he was ſet againſt the Iewes, he ſent the odious prince Apollonius with an armie of two & twentie thouſand, commanding him to kil al of perfect age, to ſel the wemen and the young ones.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Who when he was come to Ieruſalem, feyning peace, reſted vntil the holie day of the Sabbath: and then the Iewes keping holie day, he commanded his men to take weapons.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he murdered al that were gone forth to behold the gammes: & running through the citie with armed men he ſlew a very greate multitude.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Iudas Machabeus, who was the tenth, was retyred into a deſert place, and there amongſt wilde beaſtes he led his life in the mountaines with his companie: and they abode eating meate of graſſe, that they might not be partakers of the contamination.
label: 2 Machabees

text: BVT not long after the king ſent a certaine ancient man of Antioch, that should compel the Iewes to remoue themſelues from the lawes of their fathers and of God:
label: 2 Machabees

text: to contaminate alſo the temple that was in Ieruſalem, and to cal it by the name of Iupiter Olympius: and in Garizim, according as they were that inhabited the place, of Iupiter Hoſpitalis.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the inuaſion of the euiles was ſore and grieucus to al:
label: 2 Machabees

text: for the temple was ful of the lecherie and glottonie of the Gentiles: & of them that played the harlots with whoores. And wemen thruſting themſelues of their owne accord into the ſacred houſes, bringing in thouſe thinges which were not lawful.
label: 2 Machabees

text: The altar alſo was ful of vnlawful thinges, which were forbidden by the lawes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And neither were the Sabbaths kept, nor the ſoleme dayes of the fathers obſerued neither plainely did anie man confeſſe him ſelfe to be a Iewe.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But they were led with bitter neceſſitie in the kings birth day to ſacrifices: and when the feaſt of Bacchus was kept, they were compelled to goe about crowned with Iuie vnto Bacchus.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And there went forth a decree into the next cities of the Gentiles, the Ptolomeans geuing the aduiſe, that they alſo in like manner should doe againſt the Iewes, that they might ſacrifice:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and them that would not paſſe to the ordinances of the heathen, they should kil. A man then might ſee the miſerie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For 1. two wemen were accuſed to haue circuncided their children: whom, the infantes hanging at their breaſts, when they had openly led them about through the citie, they threwe downe headlong by the walles.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And others coming together to the next caues, & ſecretely 2. keping the day of the Sabbath, when they were diſcouered to Philip, were burnt with fyre, becauſe they feared for religion and obſeruance, to helpe themſelues with their hand.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But I beſeech them that shal read this booke, that they abhorre not for the aduerſities, but that they account thoſe thinges, which haue happened, not to be for the deſtruction, but for the chaſtening of our ſtocke.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For not to ſuffer ſinners a long time to doe as they wil, but forthwith to punish, is a token of a great benefite.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For, not as in other nations our Lord patiently expecteth, that when the day of iudgement shal come, he may punish them in the fulnes of ſinnes:
label: 2 Machabees

text: ſo alſo doth he determine in vs, that our ſinnes being come to the end, ſo at length he may punish vs.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For which cauſe he neuer certes remoueth away his mercie from vs: but chaſtening his people by aduerſitie, he forſaketh them not.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But let theſe thinges be ſayd of vs in few wordes for an admonition of the readers. And now we muſt come to the ſtorie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Therfore 3. Eleazarus one of the chief of the Scribes, a man ſtriken in age, and comely of countenance, with open mouth gaping was compelled to eate ſwines flesh.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But he embracing rather a moſt glorious death then an hateful life, went before voluntarily to the punishment.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And conſidering how he ought to come patiently ſuſteyning, he determined not to committe vnlawful thinges for loue of life.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But they that ſtood by, moued with vnlawful pitie, for the old frendshipe of the man, taking him in ſecrete, deſired that flesh might be brought, which it was lawful for him to eate, that he might feyne to haue eaten, as the king had commanded,
label: 2 Machabees

text: of the flesh of the ſacrifice: that by this fact he might be deliuered from death: and for the old freindshipe of the man, they did him this courteſie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But he begane to thinke vpon the worthie preeminence of his age and ancientnes, and the houre heares of natural nobilitie, & his doinges from a childe of very good conuerſation, and according to the ordinances, and the holie law made of God, he anſwered quickly, ſaying: that he would rather be ſent vnto hel.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For it is not meete, quoth he, for our age to feyne: that manie young men thinking, that Eleazarus of foure ſcore yeare & tenne is paſſed to the life of Aliens:
label: 2 Machabees

text: they alſo through my diſſimulation, and for a litle time of corruptible life, may be deceiued, and hereby I may purchaſe a ſtayne, and a curſe to mine old age.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For although at this preſent time I be deliuered from the punishments of men, yet neither aliue nor dead shal I eſcape the hand of the Almightie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Wherfore in departing manfully out of this life, I shal appeare worthie of mine old age:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and to yong men I shal leaue a conſtant example, if with readie mind and ſtoutly I ſuffer an honeſt death, for the moſt graue and moſt holie lawes. Theſe thinges being ſpoken, forthwith he was drawen to execution.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And they that led him, and had bene a litle before more milde, were turned into wrath for the wordes ſpoken of him, which they thought were vttered through arrogancie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But when he was now in killing with the ſtrokes, he groned, and ſayd: O Lord, which haſt the holie knowlege, thou knoweſt manifeſtly that wheras I might be deliuered from death, I doe ſuſteyne ſore paines of the bodie: but according to the ſoule, for thy feare I doe willingly ſuffer theſe thinges.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And this man certes in this maner departed this life, leauing not only to yong men, but alſo to the whole nation the memorie of his death for an example of vertue and fortitude.
label: 2 Machabees

text: AND it came to paſſe, 4. that ſeuen brethren together with their mother being apprehended, to be compelled by the king to eate againſt the law ſwines flesh, were tormented with whippes and ſcourges.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But one of them which was the firſt, ſayd thus: What ſeekeſt thou, and what wilt thou lerne of vs? we are readie to dye rather then to tranſgreſſe the lawes of God, coming from our fathers.
label: 2 Machabees

text: The king therfore being wrath commanded frying pannes, and braſen pottes to be heated:
label: 2 Machabees

text: the which forthwith being heated, he commanded his tongue, that had ſpoken firſt, to be cut out: and the skinne of his head being drawen of, the endes alſo of his handes and feete to be chopped of, the reſt of his bretheren, and his mother looking on.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when he was now made in al partes vnprofitable, he commanded fire to be put vnto him, and that breathing as yet he should be fried in the frying panne: wherin when he was long tormented, the reſt together with the mother exhorted one an other to dye manfully,
label: 2 Machabees

text: ſaying: Our Lord God wil behold the truth, and wil take pleaſure in vs, as Moyſes declared in the profeſſion of the Canticle: And in his ſeruants he wil take pleaſure.
label: 2 Machabees

text: That firſt therfore being dead in this maner, they brought the next to make him a mocking ſtocke: & the skinne of his head with the heares being drawen of, they asked if he would eate, before that he were punished throughout the whole bodie in euerie member.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But he anſwering in his countrie ſpeach, ſaid: I wil not doe it. Wherfore this alſo in the next place, receiued the torments of the firſt:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and being at the verie laſt gaſpe, thus he ſaid: Thou in dede ô moſt wicked man in this preſent life deſtroyeſt vs: but the king of the world wil raiſe vs vp which dye for his lawes, in the reſurrection of eternal life.
label: 2 Machabees

text: After him the third is had in deriſion, and being demanded his tongue, he quickly put it forth, and conſtantly ſtretched out his handes:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and with confidence he ſaid: From heauen doe I poſſeſſe theſe, but for the lawes of God now doe I contemne theſe ſelfe ſame, becauſe I hope that I shal receiue them againe of him.
label: 2 Machabees

text: So that the king, and they that were with him merueled at the yong mans courege, becauſe he eſtemed the torments as nothing.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And this being thus dead, the fourth they vexed in like maner tormenting him.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when he was now euen to dye, thus he ſaid: It is better for them that are put to death by men to exſpect hope of God, that they shal be rayſed vp againe by him. For to thee there shal not be reſurrection vnto life.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when they had brought the fifth, they tormented him. But he looking vpon him,
label: 2 Machabees

text: ſayd: Thou hauing power among men, wheras thou art corruptible doeſt what thou wilt: but thinke not that our ſtock is forſaken of God.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And doe thou patiently abide, and thou shalt ſee his great power, in what ſort he wil torment thee, and thy ſeede.
label: 2 Machabees

text: After him they brought the ſixth, and he beginning to dye, ſayd thus: Be not deceiued vainely: for we ſuffer this for our owne ſakes, ſinning againſt our God, and thinges worthie of admiration are done in vs:
label: 2 Machabees

text: but doe not thinke that thou shalt eſcape vnpunished, for that thou haſt attempted to fight againſt God.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But the mother aboue meaſure meruelous, and worthie of good mens memorie, which beholding her ſeuen ſonnes perishing in one dayes ſpace, bare it with a good hart, for the hope that she had in God:
label: 2 Machabees

text: exhorted euerie one of them in their countrie language manfully, being replenished with wiſedome: and ioyning a mans hart to a womans cogitation,
label: 2 Machabees

text: she ſayd to them: I know not how you appeared in my wombe: for neither did I geue you ſpirit and ſoule and life, and the members of euerie one I my ſelfe framed not.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But in deede the Creator of the world, that hath formed the natiuitie of man, and that inuented the origine of al, & he wil reſtore againe with mercie vnto you ſpirit and life, as now you deſpiſe your ſelues for his lawes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Antiochus thinking himſelfe contemned, and withal deſpiſing the voice of the vpbrayder, when the yonger was yet aliue, he did not only exhort with wordes, but alſo with oth he affirmed that he would make him rich & happie, and being turned from the lawes of his fathers, he would account him a freind, and geue him thinges neceſſarie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But when the yong man was not inclined to theſe thinges, the king called the mother, and counſelled her to deale with the yong man to ſaue his life.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when he had exhorted her in manie wordes, she promiſed that she would counſel her ſonne.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Therfore bending towards him, mocking the cruel tyrant, she ſayd in her countrie language: My ſonne haue pitie on me, which haue borne thee in my wombe nine moneths, and gaue thee milke for three yeares, and nourished thee, and brought thee vnto this age.
label: 2 Machabees

text: I beſeech thee my ſonne, that thou looke to heauen and earth, and to al thinges that are in them: and vnderſtand that God of nothing made them and mankinde:
label: 2 Machabees

text: ſo shal it come to paſſe, that thou wilt not feare this tormenter but being made a worthie partaker with thy bretheren, take thou death, that in that mercie I may receiue thee againe with thy bretheren.
label: 2 Machabees

text: When she as yet was ſaying theſe thinges, the yong man ſayd: For whom ſtay you? I obey not the commandement of the king, but the commandement of the law, which was geuen vs by Moyſes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But thou that art become the inuenter of al malice againſt the Hebrewes, shal not eſcape the hand of God.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For we for our ſinnes doe ſuffer theſe thinges.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And if the Lord our God hath bene angrie with vs a litle for rebuke & correction: yet he wil be reconciled againe to his ſeruants.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But thou ô wicked, and of al men moſt flagicious, be not in vaine extolled with vaine hopes, inflamed againſt his ſeruantes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For thou haſt not yet eſcaped the iudgement of the almightie God, and him that beholdeth al thinges.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For my bretheren hauing now ſuſteyned short payne, are become vnder the teſtament of eternal life: but thou by the iudgement of God shalt receiue iuſt punishment for thy pride.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And I as alſo my brethren doe yeld my life and my bodie for the lawes of our fathers: inuocating God to be propicious to our nation quickly, and that thou with torments and ſtripes maiſt confeſſe that he onlie is God.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But in me and in my brethren shal the wrath of the Almightie ceaſe, which hath iuſtly bene brought vpon al our ſtocke.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Then the king incenſed with anger, raged againſt him more cruelly aboue al the reſt, taking it grieuouſly that he was mocked.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And this ſame therfore died vnſpotted, wholy truſting in our Lord.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And laſt of al after the ſonnes the mother alſo was conſumed.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Therfore of the ſacrifices, and of the exceeding cruelties there is ynough ſayd.
label: 2 Machabees

text: BVT Iudas Machabeus and they that were with him, went in ſecretely into the townes: and calling together their kinſemen and taking vnto them thoſe that continewed in Iudaiſme, they brought out to them ſix thouſand men.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And they inuocated our Lord, that he would haue reſpect vnto his people that was troden of al, and would haue mercie on the temple, that was contaminated of the impious:
label: 2 Machabees

text: he would haue pitie alſo vpon the deſtruction of the citie, which was forthwith to be made flat with the ground, and would heare the voice of the bloud crying to him:
label: 2 Machabees

text: he would remember alſo the moſt vniuſt deathes of innocent children, and the blaſphemies done to his name, and would take indignation for them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Machabeus hauing gathered a multitude, became intolerable to the heathen: for the wrath of our Lord was turned into mercie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And coming vpon the caſtels, and cities vnlooked for, he burnt them: & taking commodious places, he made not few ſlaughters of the enemies:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and eſpecially in the nightes he was caried to ſuch excurſions, and the fame of his manlines was ſpred abrode euerie where.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Philip ſeing the man to come forward by litle and litle, and that thinges for the more part ſucceeded with him proſperouſly, wrote to Ptolomee the gouernour of Cœleſyria and Phoenicia, to geue ayde to the kinges affaires.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he with ſpede ſent Nicanor the ſonne of Patroclus, of the principals of his freindes, geuing him of the nations mingled together, no leſſe then twentie thouſand armed men, to deſtroy vtterly al the ſtocke of the Iewes, adioyning alſo vnto him Gorgias a man of warre, and in martial affayres of very great experience.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Nicanor appointed, that he would ſupplie vnto the king the tribute that was to be geuen to the Romanes, two thouſand talents out of the captiuitie of the Iewes:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and forthwith he ſent to the cities by the ſea ſide, calling men together to the buying of the Iewish ſlaues, promiſing that he would ſel ninetie ſlaues for a talent, not looking to the vengeance, which was to folow him from the Almightie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Iudas when he vnderſtood it, shewed to thoſe Iewes that were with him, the coming of Nicanor.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Of whom certaine fearing, and not crediting the iuſtice of God, fled away:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and others if they had any thing left, ſold it, & withal beſought our Lord, that he would deliuer them from the impious Nicanor, who had ſold them before he came neere them:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and if not for them, yet for the teſtament that was with their fathers, and for the inuocation of his holie & magnifical name vpon them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Machabeus calling together ſeuen thouſand, that were with him, deſired that they would not be reconciled to the enemies, nor feare the multitude of the enemies coming againſt them vniuſtly, but would fight manfully:
label: 2 Machabees

text: hauing before their eyes the contumelie, that was vniuſtly done by them to the holie place, and moreouer the iniurie alſo of the citie being made a laughing ſtocke, beſides alſo the ordinances of the anceſters broken.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For they in dede truſt to their weapons, ſayd he, and to their boldnes alſo: but we truſt in the Almightie Lord, who can vtterly deſtroy both them coming againſt vs, and the whole world with one becke.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he admonished them alſo of the aydes of God, that were geuen to their fathers: and that vnder Sennacherib an hundred foure ſcore fiue thouſand perished.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And of the battel, that they had againſt the Galatians in Babylonia, how al they, when it came to the point, the Macedonians their felowes ſtaggering, being only ſix thouſand ſlewe an hundred twentie thouſand, by reaſon of the ayde geuen them from heauen, and for theſe thinges obteyned verie manie benefites.
label: 2 Machabees

text: With theſe wordes they were made conſtant, and readie to dye for the lawes, and their countrie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: He appointed therfore his brethren captains ouer both orders, Simon, and Ioſeph, and Ionathas, vnder euerie one putting a thouſand and fiue hundreth.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Beſide this alſo the holie booke being read vnto them by Eſdras,
label: 2 Machabees

text: and a ſigne of Gods helpe being geuen, in the foreward the duke himſelf ioyned battel with Nicanor. And the Almightie being made their helper, they ſlew aboue nine thouſand men: and the greater part of Nicanors armie being made weake with woundes, they forced to flee.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And taking away their money that came to buy them, they purſued them on euerie hand,
label: 2 Machabees

text: but they returned being taken short with the time: for it was the day before the Sabbath: for the which cauſe they continewed not purſewing them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But gathering together the armour and ſpoiles of them, they kept the Sabbath: bleſſing our Lord that deliuered them this day, diſtilling the beginning of mercie vpon them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But after the ſabbath they diuided the ſpoyles to the feeble and to orphans, and to widowes: & the reſt themſelues had with their felowes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Theſe thinges therfore being done, and obſecration being made in common of al, they deſired our merciful Lord, that he would be reconciled to his ſeruants vnto the end.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And of them that were with Timothee and Bacchides fighting againſt them, they ſlew aboue twentie thouſand, & wanne the high holdes: and they diuided manie prayes, making equal portion to the feeble, pupils, and widowes, yea and to the elder men.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when they had diligently gathered together their armour, they layd al together in conuenient places, and the reſidue of the ſpoiles they caried to Ieruſalem:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and Philarches that was with Timothee, they ſlewe, a wicked man, which in manie thinges had afflicted the Iewes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when they kept the feaſt of victorie in Ieruſalem, him that had burnt the holie gates, that is, Calliſthenes, when he was fled into a certaine houſe, they burnt, a worthie reward being repayed him for his impieties:
label: 2 Machabees

text: But the moſt impious Nicanor, who had brought a thouſand merchants to the ſale of the Iewes,
label: 2 Machabees

text: being humbled through the helpe of our Lord by them, whom he eſteemed no bodie, laying aſide his garment of glorie, fleeing by the midland, came alone to Antioch, hauing gotten great infelicitie by the deſtruction of his armie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he that had promiſed that he would render tribute to the Romanes of the captiuitie of Ieruſalem, now profeſſed that the Iewes had God their protectour, & that for him they could not be wounded, becauſe they folowed the lawes appointed by him.
label: 2 Machabees

text: AT that time Antiochus returned out of Perſis dishonourably.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For he had entered into the citie which is called Perſipolis, and he attempted to ſpoile the temple, and to oppreſſe the citie: but the multitude running together to armes, they were put to flight: and ſo it chanced that Antiochus after his flight returned with dishonour.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when he was come about Ecbatana, he vnderſtood the thinges that were done to Nicanor and Timothee.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And ſwelling in anger, he thought that he might wreake the iniurie of them, that had put him to flight, vpon the Iewes. And therfore he commanded his chariotte to be driuen, iorneing without intermiſſion, the heauenlie iudgement vrging him forward, becauſe he ſpoke ſo proudly, that he would come to Ieruſalem, & make it an heape of the ſepulchre of the Iewes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But he that ſeeth al thinges our Lord the God of Iſrael, ſtroke him with an vncurable and inuiſible plague. For as he ended this verie ſpeach, a cruel plague of the bowels tooke him, and bitter torments of the inner parts:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and in dede very iuſtly, as who had tormented the bowels of others with manie and new torments, albeit he by no meanes ceaſed from his malice.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And beſide this replenished with pride, breathing fire in his minde againſt the Iewes, and commanding the matter to be haſtened, it chanced him going with violence to fal from the chariot, and his limmes to be vexed with a greeuous bruiſing of the bodie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he that ſeemed to himſelf to rule euen ouer the waues of the ſea, replenished with pride aboue the meaſure of man, and to weye the heights of mountaines in a balance, now being humbled to the ground was caried in a portatiue ſeate, teſtifying the manifeſt power of God in himſelf:
label: 2 Machabees

text: ſo that out of the bodie of the impious man, wormes crawled abundantly, and his liue flesh fel of for paynes, with his ſmel alſo & ſtinke the armie was anoyed.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he that a litle before thought to touch the ſtarres of heauen, him no man could carie for the intolerable ſtinke.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Hereby therfore he begane, being brought from his great pride, to come to the knowlege of himſelf, admonished by the plague of God, his paines increaſing euerie moment.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when neither himſelf now could abide his owne ſtinke, thus he ſayd: It is reaſon to be ſubiect to God, & a mortal man not to thinke of himſelf equally with God.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And this wicked man prayed to our Lord, of whom he was not to obteyne mercie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the citie to the which he came in haſt to haue brought it to the ground, & to haue made it a ſepulchre of bodies heaped together, now wisheth to make it free:
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the Iewes whom he ſayd he would not vouchſafe worthie, no not of burial, but would geue them to birds & wilde beaſtes to be ſpoiled, & deſtroy them with the litle ones, now he promiſeth to make them equal with the Athenians.
label: 2 Machabees

text: The holie temple alſo, which before he had ſpoiled, he would adorne with goodlie donaries, and would multiplie the holie veſſels, and of his reuenewes would allow the charges perteyning to the ſacrifices.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Beſides theſe thinges, that he would be a Iew alſo, & would walke through euerie place of the earth, and would declare the power of God.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But the paines ceaſing not (for the iuſt iudgement of God was come vpon him) deſpayring he wrote to the Iewes by the maner of a ſupplication an epiſtle conteyning theſe words:
label: 2 Machabees

text: To HIS VERY GOOD SVBIECTES the Iewes the king & prince Antiochus, much health, & welfare, and to be happie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: If you and your children farewel, & if thinges be with you to your mind, we geue very great thankes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And I being in infirmitie, and mindeful of you benignely, being returned out of the places of Perſis, & taken with a grieuous infirmitie, haue thought it neceſſarie to haue a care for the common profite:
label: 2 Machabees

text: not deſpayring of myſelf, but hauing great hope to eſcape the ſicknes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But conſidering that my father alſo, at what times he led his armie in the higher places, he shewed who should take the princedome after him:
label: 2 Machabees

text: that if any mishappe should chance, or hard tydings be told, they that were in the countries, knowing to whom the whole gouernement was committed, might not be trubled.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Beſides this, conſidering that al the poteſtates, and bordering neighboures wayte for times, and expect the euent, I haue appointed my ſonne Antiochus king, whom, I hauing recourſe oftentimes to the higher kingdoms did commend to manie of you: & I haue writen to him that which is ſet downe here beneath.
label: 2 Machabees

text: I pray you therfore, and deſire you mindful of the benefits both publike and priuate, that euerie one keepe his fidelitie to me, and to my ſonne.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For I truſt that he wil deale modeſtly & gently, and folowing my purpoſe, and that he wil be common vnto you.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Therfore the murderer, and blaſphemer being very ſore ſtrooken, and as himſelf had handled others, in a ſtrange countrie among the mountaynes, with a miſerable death departed this life.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Philip his foſter brother remoued his bodie: who fearing the ſonne of Antiochus, went to Ptolomee Philometor into Ægypt.
label: 2 Machabees

text: BVT Machabeus, and they that were with him, our Lord protecting them, recouered the temple & the citie againe:
label: 2 Machabees

text: but the altars, which the aliens had ſet vp through the ſtreets, and alſo the temples he threw downe.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And hauing purged the temple, they made an other altar: and out of fyred ſtones taking fire they offered ſacrifices after two yeares, and ſet incenſe, and lampes, and the breads of propoſition.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Which thinges being done, they beſought our Lord proſtrate on the ground, that they might no more fal into ſuch euils: but and if they had ſometime ſinned, that they might be chaſtened of him more mildly, & not be deliuered to barbarous, & blaſphemous men.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And what day the temple had bene polluted of the aliens, it happened that on the ſame day was made the purification, the fiue and twentith of the moneth, which was Caſleu.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And with ioy eight dayes they kept in maner of tabernacles, remembring that a litle before they had kept the ſolemne day of Tabernacles in the mountaynes, and in dennes after the maner of beaſts.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For the which cauſe they bare before them ſtalkes of herbs, and greene boughes, and palmes to him, that gaue ſucceſſe to clenſe his place.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And they decreed by common precept, and decree to al the nation of the Iewes euerie yeare to keepe theſe dayes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Antiochus that was called the Noble, his departure out of life was after this ſort.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But now of Eupator the ſonne of Antiochus the impious, we wil tel the thinges that haue bene done, abbridging the euils that were done in the warres.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For he hauing taken vpon him the kingdom, appointed ouer the affaires of the king one Lyſias general of the hoſt of Phænicia and Syria.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For Ptolomee who was called Macer, determined to be a keeper of iuſtice toward the Iewes, and eſpecially for the iniquitie, that was done againſt them, and to deale peaceably with them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But being accuſed for this of his freinds to Eupator, when he was called oftentimes traytour, becauſe he had left Cypres commited vnto him by Philometor, and remouing to Antiochus the Noble, had reuolted alſo from him, he made an end of his life with poyſon.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Gorgias being captayne of the places, taking vnto him ſtrangers often warred againſt the Iewes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the Idumeans that kept the commodious holdes, receiued them that were chaſed from Ieruſalem, and attempted to make battel.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And they that were with Machabeus, beſeeching our Lord by prayers that he would be their helper, made an aſſault vpon the holdes of the Idumeans:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and ſticking to it with great force, they wanne the places, killed them that came in the way, & ſlewe altogether no leſſe then twentie thouſand.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And wheras certaine were fled into two towres very ſtrong, hauing al prouiſion to make reſiſtance,
label: 2 Machabees

text: Machabeus for the expugning of them, leauing Simon and Ioſeph, and alſo Zachæus, and ſuch as were with them very manie, himſelf turned to thoſe battels which forced more.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But they that were with Simon, being led with couetouſnes, were perſwaded with money by certaine that were in the towres: and taking ſeuentie thouſand didrachmaes, they let certayne eſcape.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But when it was told Machabæus what was done, aſſembling the princes of the people he accuſed them, that they had ſold their bretheren for money, their aduerſaries being let goe.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Theſe therfore being become traytours he ſlewe, and forthwith he tooke the two towres.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And with weapons and handes doing al thinges proſperouſly, in the two holdes he ſlewe more then twentie thouſand.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Timothee, who before had bene ouercome of the Iewes, hauing called together an armie of foren multitude, and gathering horſemen of Aſia, came as to take Iurie by armes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Machabeus and they that were with him, when he approched, beſought our Lord, ſprinkling their head with earth, and being girded about the loynes with heareclothes,
label: 2 Machabees

text: lying flatte at the brimme of the altar, that he would be propicious to them, and an enemie to their enemies, and an aduerſarie to their aduerſaries, as the law ſaith.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And ſo after prayer taking weapons, going forth ſomewhat far out of the citie, and being come very neere the enemies they pitched.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And at the very firſt riſing of the ſunne both ioyned battel: theſe in deede hauing our Lord the ſuretie of victorie, and proſperitie with vertue: but they had courege for the captayne of the battel.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But when there was a ſore fight, there appeared to the aduerſaries from heauen fiue men vpon horſes, comelie with golden bridles, conducting the Iewes:
label: 2 Machabees

text: of whom two hauing Machabeus betwen them, compaſſing him round about with their armour, kept him ſafe: and againſt the aduerſaries they threw darts, & fire balles, wherby both confounded with blindnes, and filled with perturbation they fel.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And there were ſlaine twentie thouſand fiue hundred, and horſemen ſix hundred.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Timothee fled into Gazara a ſtrong hold, wherof Chæreas was the captaine.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Machabeus, and they that were with him ioyfully beſieged the hold foure dayes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But they that were within, truſting to the place, blaſphemed aboue meaſure, & caſt forth abominable wordes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But when the fifth day appeared, twentie yong men of them that were with Machabeus, incenſed in their mindes becauſe of the blaſphemie, went manfully to the wal, and with fierce conrege going on, they ſcaled to the top:
label: 2 Machabees

text: Yea and the others alſo mounting vp, attempted to ſet the towres and the gates on fire, and to burne the blaſphemers themſelues aliue.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the hold being ſacked for two dayes together, they ſlewe Timothee that was found hyding himſelf in a certaine place: and his brother Chæreas, and Apollophanes they killed.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Which thinges being done, they bleſſed our Lord in hymnes and confeſſions, who did great thinges in Iſrael, and gaue them the victorie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: BVT a litle after Lyſias the kings procuratour, and coſin, and chiefe ouer the affayers, being greatly offended with theſe thinges, that had hapened,
label: 2 Machabees

text: hauing gathered foure ſcore thouſand, and al the horſemen, came againſt the Iewes, thincking that taking the citie, he should make it an habitation for the Gentiles:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and he should haue the temple to make gayne of money, as the reſt of the temples of the Gentiles, and euerie yeare the prieſthood to be ſold:
label: 2 Machabees

text: neuer recounting the powre of God, but furious in minde, he truſted in the multitude of foote men, and thouſandes of horſemen, and in foure ſcore elephants.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he entred into Iurie, and approching to Beth-ſura, which was in a narrow place from Ieruſalem the ſpace of fiue furlongs, he expugned that hold.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But as Machabeus, and they that were with him, vnderſtood that the holdes were expugned, they beſought our Lord with weeping and teares, and al the multitude together, that he would ſend a good Angel to the ſauing of Iſrael.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Machabeus him ſelf firſt taking weapons, exhorted the reſt together with him, to aduenture, and to geue ayde to their bretheren.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when they went forth together with prompt corege, at Ieruſalem there appeared going before them an horſeman in white clothing, with armour of gold, shaking a ſpeare.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Then al they together bleſſed our merciful Lord, and tooke great corege: being readie to penetrate not only men, but alſo moſt fierce beaſtes, and walles of yron.
label: 2 Machabees

text: They went therfore promptly, hauing an helper from heauen, and our Lord hauing pitie vpon them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And like lyons running violently vpon the enimies, they ouerthrew of them eleuen thouſand footmen, and of horſemen a thouſand ſix hundred:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and they put to flight al, & very many of them being wounded ſcaped away naked. Yea and Lyſias him ſelfe shamefully fleeing eſcaped.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And becauſe he was not ſenſeleſſe recounting with him ſelfe, the diminution made on his ſide, and vnderſtanding the Hebrewes to be inuincible, becauſe they reſted vpon the helpe of the almightie God, he ſent vnto them:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and promiſed that he would conſent to al thinges, that are iuſt, and that he would force the king to be their freind.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Machabeus granted to Lyſias requeſtes, in al things hauing reſpect to the commonwealth and whatſoeuer Machabeus wrote to Lyſias, concerning the Iewes, the king granted it.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For there were epiſtles written to the Iewes from Lyſias, conteyning this tenure: LYSIAS to the people of the Iewes health.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Iohn and Abſalom that were ſent from you, deliuering the wrytings, requeſted that I would accomplishe thoſe thinges which by them were ſignified.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Therfore whatſoeuer might be brought to the king I declared vnto him: and that which the matters permitted I granted.
label: 2 Machabees

text: If therfore you kepe fideletie in the affayres & henceforward, alſo wil endeuour to be a cauſe of doing you good.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And concerning the reſt, word for word I haue geuen commandement both to theiſe, and to them that are ſent of me, to commune with you.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Fare ye wel. In the yeare an hundred fourtie eight, of the moneth Dioſcorus the foure & twenteth day.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But the kings epiſtle conteyned theſe thinges: King Antiochus to Lyſias his brother, health.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Our father being tranſlated amongſt the goddes, we being willing that they that are in our kingdome should liue without truble, and employ diligence to their owne matters,
label: 2 Machabees

text: we haue heard that the Iewes conſented not to my father to turne to the rite of the Greekes, but that they would keepe their owne inſtitution, and therfore that they requeſt vs their rites to be granted them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Being therfore deſirouſe that this nation alſo be quiet, oradyning we haue decreed, that the temple be reſtored vnto them, that they might doe according to the cuſtome of their anceſtours.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Thou shalt do wel therfore if thou ſend to them, & geue the right hand, that our pleaſure being knowen they may be of good cheere, & looke to their owne commodities.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But to the Iewes the kings epiſtle was in this manner: KING Antiochus to the ſenate of the Iewes, and to the reſt of the Iewes health.
label: 2 Machabees

text: If you fare wel, you are ſo as we would: yea our ſelues alſo fare wel.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Menelaus came to vs, ſaying that you would come downe to your countrie men, that are with vs.
label: 2 Machabees

text: To them therfore that come and goe, vntil the thirtith day of the month Xanthicus, we geue the right handes of ſecuritie,
label: 2 Machabees

text: that the Iewes may vſe their owne meates, and their owne lawes, as alſo before: and that none of them by any meanes ſuffer moleſtation for theſe thinges, which haue bene done by ignorance.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And we haue ſent alſo Menelaus to ſpeake to you.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Fare ye wel. In the yeare an hundred fortie eight, of the moneth Xanthicus the fiftenth day.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the Romans alſo ſent an epiſtle, which is thus: QVINTVS Memmius, and Titus Manilius legats of the Romans, to the people of the Iewes health.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Concerning theſe thinges which Lyſias the kings coſin hath granted you, we alſo haue granted.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But touching the thinges which he thought good to be referred to the king, ſend ye forthwith ſome bodie, conferring diligently among your ſelues, that we may decree as is conuenient for you: for we goe to Antioch.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And therfore make haſt to write agayne, that we alſo may know of what minde you are.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Fate ye wel. In the yeare an hundred fourtie eight the fiftenth day of the moneth Xanthicus.
label: 2 Machabees

text: THESE couenants being made, Lyſias went foreward to the king, and the Iewes gaue themſelues to husbandrie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But they that ſtayed there, Timothie & Appollonius the ſonne of Gennaius, & alſo Ierom, & Demophon, beſides theſe alſo Nicanor the gouerner of Cyprus, did not ſuffer them to liue in reſt and quietnes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the Ioppites committed a certaine flagicious fact, which was this: They deſired the Iewes with whom they dwelt, to goe into the botes, which they had prepared, with their wiues & children, as though no ſecret emnities were betwen them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Therfore according to the common decree of the citie, & they agreeing therto, & becauſe of the peace ſuſpecting nothing: when they were gone forward, into the depth, they drowned no leſſe then two hundred.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Which crueltie Iudas as he vnderſtood to be done vpon the men of his nation, commanded the men that were with him: and inuocating God the iuſt iudge,
label: 2 Machabees

text: he came againſt the murderers of his brethren, & the hauen he ſet on fire in the night, the botes he burnt, & them that were fled from the fire, he ſlew with the ſword.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when he had thus done theſe thinges, he departed as to returne againe, and to roote out al the Ioppites.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But when he vnderſtood that they alſo, which were at Iamnia, would doe in like maner to the Iewes dwelling with them,
label: 2 Machabees

text: he came vpon the Iamnites alſo by night, and ſet the hauen on fyre with the shippes, ſo that the light of the fire appeared at Ieruſalem two hundred fourtie furlongs of.
label: 2 Machabees

text: When they were now departed thence nine furlongs, and made their iourney towards Timothee, the Arabians fiue thouſand men, and fiue hundred horſemen ioyned battel with them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when there was a mightie battel, and by the helpe of God it had ſucceded proſperouſly, the reſt of the Arabians that were ouercome, beſought Iudas that the right hand might be geuen them, promiſing that they would geue paſtures, and profite them, in other thinges.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Iudas thinking in very deede that they might be profitable in manie thinges, promiſed peace, and right handes being taken, they departed to their tabernacles.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he ſet alſo vpon a certaine citie ſtrong with bridges, and enuironed with walles, which was inhabited with multitudes of heathen of al ſortes, the name wherof is Caſpin.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But they that were within, truſting in the firmenes of the walles, & the prouiſion of victuals, dealt the more ſlackly, with reuiling wordes prouoking Iudas, and blaſpheming, and ſpeaking ſuch thinges as is not lawful to ſpeake.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Machabeus inuocating the great prince of the world, who without rammes and engines in Ieſus time threwe downe Ierico, fiercely aſſaulted the walles.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the citie being taken by the wil of our Lord he made innumerable ſlaughters, ſo that the poole adioyning of two furlongs in bredth, ſemed to runne died with bloud.
label: 2 Machabees

text: From thence they departed ſeuen hundred fiftie furlongs, and they came to Characa to thoſe Iewes, that are called Tubianeians:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and in thoſe places they tooke not Timothee, and nothing being done he went backe, hauing left in a certaine place a very ſtrong garriſon.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Doſitheus, and Soſipater, who were captayns with Machabeus, ſlewe them that were left of Timothee in the hold, ten thouſand men.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Machabeus ordayning about him ſix thouſand, and placing them by bandes, went forth againſt Timothee, who had with him an hundred twenty thouſand footemen, & of horſemen two thouſand fiue hundred.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the coming of Iudas being knowen, Timothee ſent the wemen and children, and the other baggage before into the fortreſſe, that is called Carnion: for it was inuincible, and hard to come by, by reaſon of the ſtraites of the places.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when the firſt band of Iudas had appeared, feare was ſtroken into the enemies, by the preſence of God, who ſeeth al thinges, and they were put to flight one of an other, ſo that they were rather ouerthrowen of their owne companie, and were weakened with the ſtrokes of their owne ſwordes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Iudas was exceding earneſt punishnig the prophane men, and he ouerthrewe of them thirtie thouſand men.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Timothee him ſelfe fel into the handes of Doſitheus and Siſipaters partes, and with manie prayers he beſought that he might be let go aliue, becauſe he had parents & brethren of manie of the Iewes, whom it might happen by his death to be deceiued.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when he had geuen his faith that he would reſtore them according to the appointmet they let him goe without harme, for the ſafetie of their brethren.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Iudas came backe from Carnion, hauing ſlayne twentie fiue thouſand.
label: 2 Machabees

text: After the flight and ſlaughter of theſe, he moued his armie to Ephron a ſtrong citie, wherin a multitude dwelt of diuerſe nations: & ſtrong young men ſtanding before the walles reſiſted manfully, & in this were manie engins, and prouiſion of dartes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But when they had inuocated the Almightie, who with his power breaketh the forces of the enemies, they tooke the citie: and of them that were within they ouerthrew twentie fiue thouſand.
label: 2 Machabees

text: From thence they departed to a citie of the Scythians, which was diſtant from Ieruſalem ſix hundred furlongs.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But thoſe Iewes that were with the Scythopolitans teſtifying that they were vſed curteouſly of them, euen in the times of miſerie that they dealt modeſtly with them:
label: 2 Machabees

text: geuing them thankes, and exhorting them alſo thence forward to be fauourable toward their ſtock, they came to Ieruſalem the ſolemne day of the weekes approching.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And after Pentecoſt they went againſt Gorgias the gouernour of Idumea.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he went forth with footemen three thouſand, and horſemen foure hundred.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Who buckling together, it chanced few of the Iewes to be ſlayne.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Doſitheus one of the Bacenors an horſeman, a valiant man, held Gorgias: and wheras he would haue taken him aliue, a certayne horſeman of the Thracians came vpon him, and cut of his shoulder: and ſo Gorgias eſcaped into Mareſa.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But they that were with Eſdrin, fighting long, and being wearied, Iudas inuocated our Lord to be their helper, and captayne of the battel:
label: 2 Machabees

text: beginning in his countrey language, and with hymmes raiſing a crie, draue Gorgias ſouldiars into flight.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Iudas hauing gathered an armie came into the citie Odollam: & when the ſeuenth day came on, being purifyed according to the cuſtome, they kept the Sabbath in the ſame place.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the day folowing Iudas came with his companie, to take away the bodies of them that were ouerthrowen, and with their kinſmen to lay them in the ſepulchers of their fathers.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And they found vnder the coates of the ſlayne ſome of the donaryes of the idols, that were in Iamnia, from which the lawe forbiddeth the Iewes: therfore it was made playne to al, that for that cauſe they were ſlayne.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Al therfore bleſſed the iuſt iudgement of our Lord, who had made manifeſt the hidden thinges.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And ſo turning to prayers, they beſought him, that the ſame offence, which was committed, might be forgotten. But the moſt valient Iudas exhorted the people to kepe themſelues without ſinne, ſeing before their eyes what was done, becauſe of the ſinnes of them that were ouerthrowen.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And making a gathering, he ſent twelue thouſand drachmes of ſiluer to Ieruſalem for ſacrifice to be offered for ſinne, wel and religiouſly thinking of the reſurrection.
label: 2 Machabees

text: ( for vnles he hoped that they that were ſlaine, should riſe againe, it should ſeeme ſuperfluous, and vaine to pray for the dead)
label: 2 Machabees

text: And becauſe he conſidered that they, which had taken their ſleepe with godlines, had very good grace layd vp for them.
label: 2 Machabees

text: It is therfore a holie, and healthful cogitation to pray for the dead, that they may be looſed from ſinnes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: IN the yeare an hundred fourtie nine Iudas vnderſtood, that Antiochus Eupator came with a multitude agaynſt Iurie,
label: 2 Machabees

text: and with him Lyſias the procuratour, and cheefe ouer the affayres hauing with him of footemen an hundred tenne thouſand, & of horſemen fiue thouſand, & elephants twentie two, chariots with hookes three hundred.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Menelaus alſo ioyned him ſelfe with them: and with much deceite beſought Antiochus, not for the weale of his contrie, but hoping that he should be appoynted to the principalitie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But the king of kinges ſtirred vp Antiochus mind againſt the ſinner, & Lyſias ſuggeſting that he was the cauſe of al the euils, he commanded (as the cuſtome is with them) that being apprehended he should be killed in the ſame place.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And there was in the ſame place a tower of fiftie cubites, hauing an heape of ashes on euerie ſide: this had a proſpect ſteepe downe.
label: 2 Machabees

text: From thence he commanded the ſacrilegious perſon to be throwne downe into the ashes, al thruſting him forward to death.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And by ſuch law it chanced the tranſgreſſour of the law to dye: & Menelaus not to be put into the earth.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And in deede very iuſtly, becauſe he committed manie offences toward the altar of God, the fyre and ashes wherof was holie: himſelf was condemned into the death of ashes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But the king furiouſe in mind, came to shew himſelfe worſe to the Iewes then his father.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Which thinges when Iudas vnderſtood, he commanded the people that day and night they should inuocate our Lord, that as alwayes now alſo he would helpe them:
label: 2 Machabees

text: as who were afrayed to be depriued of the law, & their countrie, & the holie temple: and that he would not ſuffer the people that had of late taken breath a litle while, to be againe ſubdued to the blaſphemous nations.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Al therfore doing it together, and crauinig mercie of our Lord with weeping & faſtinges, being proſtrate for three dayes continually, Iudas exhorted them to prepare them ſelues.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But he with the ancients conſulted, before the king should bring his armie to Iurie, and winne the citie, to goe out, and to committe the euent of the thing to the iudgement of our Lord.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Committing therfore the power and charge of al to God, the creatour of the world, and hauing exhorted his companie to fight manfully, and to ſtand euen to death for the lawes, the temple, the citie, their countrie, and citizens: he placed his armie about Modin.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And hauing geuen a ſigne to his companie of the victorie of God, with moſt valient yong men piked out, by night ſetting vpon the kings court, in the campe he ſlew foure thouſand men, and the greateſt of the elephants, with them that had bene placed thereupon,
label: 2 Machabees

text: and he filled the campe of the enemies with exceeding feare and perturbation, and the thinges being proſperouſly atcheiued, they departed.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And this was done when the day appeared, the protection of our Lord helping him.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But the king hauing taken a taſte of the hardines of the Iewes, attempted the difficultie of the places by policie:
label: 2 Machabees

text: and he moued his campe to Bethſura, which was a ſtrong hold of the Iewes: but he was put to flight, he fel, he was diminished.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And to them that were within Iudas ſent neceſſaries.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But one Rhodocus of the Iewes armie vttered the ſecretes to the enemies, who being ſought for was apprehended, and shut vp.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Againe the king had talke with them that were in Bethſura: he gaue the right hand: he tooke it: he went away.
label: 2 Machabees

text: He ioyned battel with Iudas, he was ouercome. And as he vnderſtood that Phillippe rebelled at Antioch, who was left ouer the affayres, diſmayed in mynde intreating the Iewes, and yelding vnto them, he ſweareth concerning al thinges that ſeemed reaſon, & being reconciled he offered ſacrifice, honoured the temple, and gaue hoſts.
label: 2 Machabees

text: He embraced Machabeus, & made him gouernor & prince from Ptolemais euen to the Gerrenians.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But after, as he came to Ptolemais the Ptolemaians tooke greuouſly the couenant of amitie, being offended leſt perhaps they would breake their league.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Then Lyſias went vp to the iudgement ſeate, and declared the reaſon, and appeaſed the people, and returned to Antioch: and in this maner the kinges iorney and returne proceded.
label: 2 Machabees

text: BVT after the ſpace of three yeares Iudas vnderſtood, and they that were with him, that Demetrius the ſonne of Seleucus with a ſtrong multitude, and with shippes was come vp by the port of Tripolis to commodious places,
label: 2 Machabees

text: and held the countries againſt Antiochus, and his gouernor Lyſias.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And one Alcimus that had bene highprieſt, but voluntarily was contaminated in the time of the confuſion, conſidering that there was ſaftie for him by no means, nor acceſſe to the altar,
label: 2 Machabees

text: came to king Demetrius in the yeare an hundred fiftie, offering him a crowne of gold, & a palme, & beſides theſe, Talloes, which ſeemed to be of the temple. And that ſame day in deede he held his peace.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But hauing gotten a commodious time for his madnes, being called of Demetrius to counſel, and asked on what thing and counſels the Iewes reſted, he anſwered:
label: 2 Machabees

text: They of the Iewes that are called Aſſidians, of whom Iudas Machabeus is captaine, nourish battels, and moue ſeditions, neither doe they ſuffer the realme to be quiet.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For I alſo being defrawded of my anceſtours glorie (I meane of the high prieſthood) am come hither:
label: 2 Machabees

text: principally in deede keping fidelitie to the kings commodities, but ſecondly alſo prouiding for my citizens, forby their naughtines al our ſtocke is not a little vexed.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But al theſe thinges being knowen, ô king, prouide I pray thee, both for the countrie, & for our ſtocke according to thy humanitie published to al men.
label: 2 Machabees

text: For as long as Iudas is aliue, it is vnpoſſible that there be peace to the affayres.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And ſuch thinges being ſayd of him, the other freinds alſo behauing themſelues as enemies againſt Iudas, incenſed Demetrius.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Who forthwith ſent Nicanor, chiefe ouer the elephants captaine into Iurie:
label: 2 Machabees

text: geuing him commiſſion, that he should take Iudas himſelfe: but them that were with him, he should diſperſe, & make Alcimus the high prieſt of the greateſt temple.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Then the nations, which had fled from Iudas out of Iurie, ioyned themſelues by troupes with Nicanor, eſteming the miſeries, and calamities of the Iewes the proſperities of their owne affayres.
label: 2 Machabees

text: The Iewes therfore hauing heard of Nicanors coming, & the aſſemblie of the nations, being ſprinkled with earth beſought him, that ordayned his people to kepe them for euer, and that protecteth his portion by euident ſignes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And the captaine commanding forthwith they remoued from thence, and they came together to the caſtel of Deſſau.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Simon the brother of Iudas had ioyned battel with Nicanor: but he was made afrayd with the ſodaine coming of the aduerſaries.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Neuertheles Nicanor hearing the manlines of Iudas companions, and greatnes of courege, that they had for the conflicts of their countrie, was afrayde to make tryall by bloud.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Wherfore he ſent Poſidonius, and Theodotius, & Mathias before to geue and take the right handes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when there was long conſultation of theſe thinges, and the captaine himſelf had moued it to the multitude, there was one ſentence of them al to accord vnto amitie.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Therfore they appointed a day, wherin they might ſecretly deale among themſelues, and ſeates were brought forth and ſette for euery one.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Iudas commanded armed men to be in places conuenient, leſt perhaps ſome miſchefe might ſodainly ariſe from the enemies: & they made agreable communication.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Nicanor abode at Ieruſalem, and did nothing vniuſtly, and the flockes of the multitudes, that had bene gathered together he diminished.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he eſteemed Iudas alwayes deare from the hart, and he was inclined to the man.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And he deſired him to marrie a wife, and to beget children. He made a marriage, he liued quietly, and they liued in common.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Alcimus ſeeing their charitie one towardes an other, and the couenantes, came to Demetrius, and ſayd that Nicanor aſſented to forraine matters, and that he ment to make Iudas being a traytour to the kingdom, his ſucceſſour.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Therfore the king being exaſperated with this mans moſt wicked criminations, wrote to Nicanor, ſaying, that he in deede was greatly diſpleaſed for the couenant of their amitie: neuertheles that he commanded him to ſend Machabeus quickly priſoner to Antioch.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Which thinges being knowen Nicanor was amaſed, and tooke it greuouſly, if he should vndoe thoſe thinges which they had couenanted, being nothing hurt of the man.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But becauſe he could not reſiſt the king, he obſerued oportunitie wherby to accomplish the commandement.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Machabeus ſeeing that Nicanor dealt with him more auſterely, and that he exhibited his accuſtomed meeting more ſternely, vnderſtanding this auſteritie not to be of good, a few of his companie gathered together, he hid himſelf from Nicanor.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Which when he vnderſtood that he was ſtoutly preuented of the man, he came to the moſt great & moſt holie temple: and the prieſtes offering the accuſtomed hoſtes, he commanded the man to be deliuered vnto him.
label: 2 Machabees

text: Who ſaying with an oath, that they knew not where he was, that was demanded, ſtretching out his hand to the temple,
label: 2 Machabees

text: he ſware, ſaying: Vnles you wil deliuer Iudas priſoner vnto me, I wil beate downe this temple of God to the flat ground, and wil digge downe the altar, and this temple I wil conſecrate to Liber pater.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And when he had ſayd theſe thinges, he departed. But the prieſtes ſtretching forth their hands vnto heauen, inuocated him that was alwayes the defender of their nation, ſaying thus:
label: 2 Machabees

text: Thou ô Lord of al, which lackeſt nothing, wouldeſt a temple of thy habitation to be made amongſt vs.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And now ô Lord holie of al holies, preſerue for euer this houſe impolluted, which of late hath bene clenſed.
label: 2 Machabees

text: And Razias one of the ancients of Ieruſalem, was accuſed to Nicanor, a man that was a louer of the citie, and wel reported of, who for his affection was called father of the Iewes.
label: 2 Machabees

text: This man long time kept the purpoſe of continencie in Iudaiſme, and content to geue his bodie and life for perſeuerance.
label: 2 Machabees

text: But Nicanor willing to manifeſt the hatred that he had againſt the Iewes, ſent fiue hundred ſouldiars to take him.
label: 2 Machabees

text: for he thought if he had intrapped him, that he should doe the Iewes verie great hurt.

text: BVT Eliphaz the Themanite anſwering, ſayd:

text: I wil shew thee, heare me: that which I haue ſeene I wil tel thee.

text: Wiſemen confeſſe and hide not their fathers.

text: To whom onlie the earth was geuen, and ſtranger hath not paſſed by them.

text: The impious is proud al his daies, and the number of the yeares of his tyrannie is vncertaine.

text: Before his daies be accomplished, he shal perish: and his handes shal wither.

text: I would ſtrengthen you with my mouth, and would moue my lippes, as ſparing you.

text: He hath gathered his furie vpon me, and threatening me hath gnashed againſt me with his teeth, mine enemy hath beheld me with terrible eies.

text: They haue opened their mouthes vpon me, and exprobating haue ſtrooken my cheke, they are filled with my paines.

text: God hath shut me vp with the wicked man, and hath deliuered me to the hands of the impious.

text: He hath cut me with wound vpon wound, he hath come violently vpon me as it were a giant.

text: My face is ſwollen with weeping, and my eyeliddes are dimme.

text: My daies haue paſſed, my cogitations are diſſipated, tormenting my hart:

text: If I shal expect, hel is my houſe, and in darkeneſſe I haue made my bed.

text: I haue ſayd to rottenes: Thou art my father, my mother, and my ſiſter, to wormes.

text: Where is now then my expectation, and my patience who conſidereth.

text: Al my thinges shal deſcend into moſt deepe hel: there at the leaſt, shal I haue reſt thinkeſt thou?

text: BVT Baldad the Suhite anſwering, ſayd:

text: How long wil ye ſpeake vaunting wordes? vnderſtand ye firſt, and ſo let vs ſpeake.

text: Why are we reputed as beaſtes, and accounted vile before you?

text: Let his ſtrength be extenuated with famine, and let hunger inuade his ribbes.
label: Job

text: Let his rootes be dried downward, and his harueſt deſtroyed vpward.

text: Let the memorie of him perish from the earth, and let not his name be renowmed in the ſtreates.

text: His ſeed shal not be, nor his progenie in his people, nor anie remnantes in his countries.

text: In his daie the laſt shal be aſtonied, and horrour shal inuade the firſt.
