text: FLIES dying marre the ſweetnes of ointment. Wiſdom and glorie is more precious, then a litle and temporal follie.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: The hart of a wiſeman is in his righthand, and the hart of a foole is in his lefthand.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: Yea and the foole walking in the way, wheras himſelf is vnwiſe, eſtemeth al men fooles.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: If the ſpirite of him that hath powre, aſcend vpon thee, leaue not thy place: becauſe carefulnes wil make the greateſt ſinnes to ceaſe.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: There is an euil that I haue ſene vnder the ſunne, as it were by errour proceding from the face of the prince:
label: Ecclesiastes

text: a foole ſet in high dignitie, and the rich to ſitte beneth.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: I haue ſene ſeruants vpon horſes: and princes walking on the ground as ſeruants.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: He that diggeth a pitte, shal fal into it: and he that breaketh the hedge, a ſerpent shal bite him.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: He that remoueth ſtones, shal be afflicted in them: and he that cutteth trees, shal be wounded of them.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: If the iron shal be blunt, and that not as before, but shal be made blunt, it shal be sharpened by great labour, and after induſtrie shal wiſdom folow.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: If a ſerpent bite in ſilence, nothing leſſe then it hath he, that detracteth ſecretly.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: The wordes of the mouth of a wiſeman grace: and the lippes of the vnwiſe shal throw him downe headlong.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: The beginning of his wordes is follie, and the later end of his mouth is moſt wicked errour.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: A foole multiplieth wordes. A man is ignorant what hath bene before him: and what shal be after him, who can tel him?
label: Ecclesiastes

text: The labour of fooles shal afflict them, that know not to goe into the cittie.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: Woe to thee ô land, whoſe king is a childe, and whoſe princes eate in the morning.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: Bleſſed is the land, whoſe king is noble, & whoſe princes eate in their time to refection, and not to riotouſnes.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: In ſlouthfulnes the roofe of the houſe shal goe to ruine, & in the infirmitie of the handes the houſe shal droppe through.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: They make bread for laughter, and wine that liuing they may make merie: and to money al thinges obey.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: In thy cogitation detract not from the king, and in the ſecret of thy chamber curſe not the richman: becauſe euen the birdes of the ayre wil carie thy voice, and he that hath winges wil declare the ſentence.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: CAST thy bread vpon the paſſing waters: becauſe after much time thou shalt finde it.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: Geue a portion to ſeuen, and alſo to eight: becauſe thou knoweſt not what euil shal be vpon the earth:
label: Ecclesiastes

text: If the cloudes be ful, they wil powre out raine vpon the earth. If the tree shal fal to the South, or to the North, in what place ſoeuer it shal fal, there shal it be.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: He that obſerueth the winde, ſoweth not: and he that conſidereth the cloudes, shal neuer reape.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: As thou art ignorant which is the way of the ſpirite, & how the bones are framed together in the wombe of her that conceiueth childe: ſo thou knoweſt not the workes of God, who is the maker of al.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: In the morning ſow thy ſeede, and in the euening let not thy hand ceaſe: for thou knoweſt not which may rather ſpring, this or that: and if both together, it shal be the better.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: The light is ſweete: and it is delectable for the eyes to ſee the ſunne.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: If a man shal liue manie yeares, and shal haue reioyced in them al, he muſt remember the darkeſome time, and manie dayes: which when they shal come, the thinges paſt shal be reproued of vanitie.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: Reioyce therfore yongman in thy youth, and let thy hart be in good, in the dayes of thy youth, and walke in the wayes of thy hart, and in the ſight of thyne eyes: and know that for al theſe God wil bring thee into iudgement.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: Take away anger from thy hart, and remoue malice from thy flesh. For youth and pleaſure are vaine.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: REMEMBER thy Creator in the dayes of thy youth, before the time of affliction come, & the yeares approch, of which thou maiſt ſay: They pleaſe me not,
label: Ecclesiastes

text: before the ſunne, and light, and moone, and ſtarres be darke, and the cloudes returne after the raine:
label: Ecclesiastes

text: when the kepers of the houſe shal be moued, and the ſtrongeſt men shal ſtagger, and the grinders shal be idle in a ſmal number: and they shal waxe darke that looke through the holes:
label: Ecclesiastes

text: and they shal shut the doores in the ſtreate, at the baſenes of the grinders voice, and they shal riſe vp at the voice of the birde, and al the daughters of ſong shal be deafe.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: The high thinges alſo shal feare, and they shal be afrayd in the way, the almondtree shal florish, the locuſt shal be fatted, and the capertree shal be deſtroyed: becauſe man shal goe into the houſe of his eternitie, and the mourners shal goe round about in the ſtreate.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: Before the ſiluer coard be broken, and the golden headband recurre, and the water pot be broken vpon the fountaine, and the wheele be broken vpon the ceſterne,
label: Ecclesiastes

text: and the duſt returne into his earth, from whence it was, and the ſpirite returne to God, who gaue it.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: Vanitie of vanities, ſayd Eccleſiaſtes, and al thinges vanitie.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: And wheras Eccleſiaſtes was moſt wiſe, he taught the people, and declared the thinges that he had done: and ſearching forth made manie parables.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: He ſought profitable wordes, and wrote wordes moſt right, and ful of truth.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: The wordes of wiſemen are as prickes, and as nailes deepely ſtricken in, which by the counſel of maiſters are geuen of one paſtour.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: More then theſe my ſonne require not. Of making manie bookes there is no end: and often meditation is affliction of the flesh.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: Let vs al heare together the end of ſpeaking. Feare God, and obſerue his commandments: for this is euerie man:
label: Ecclesiastes

text: and al thinges that are done, God wil bring into iudgement for euerie errour, whether it be good, or euil.
label: Ecclesiastes

text: LET him kiſſe me with the kiſſe of his mouth: becauſe thy breſtes are better then wine,
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: ſmelling fragrantly of the beſt ointments. Oile powred out is thy name: therfore haue yongmaydes loued thee.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Draw me: we wil runne after thee in the odour of thine ointments. The king hath brought me into his cellars: we wil reioyce & be glad in thee, mindful of thy breſts aboue wine: the righteous loue thee.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I am blacke but beutiful, ô ye daughters of Ieruſalem, as the tabernacles of Cedar, as the skinnes of Salomon.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Doe not conſider me that I am browne, becauſe the ſunne hath altered my colour: the ſonnes of my mother haue fought againſt me, they haue made me a keeper in the vinyards: my vinyard I haue not kept.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Shew me ô thou, whom my ſoule loueth, where thou feedeſt, where thou lyeſt in the midday, leſt I beginne to wander after the flockes of thy companyons.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: If thou know not thyſelfe, ô moſt fayreſt among wemen, goeforth, and folow after the ſteppes of the flockes, and feede thy kiddes byſide the tabernacles of the paſtours.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: To my companie of horſemen, in the chariotes of Pharao, haue I likened thee, ô my loue.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy cheekes are beautiful as the turteldoues, thy necke as iewels.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: We wil make thee cheynes of gold, enamoled with ſiluer.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Whiles the king was at his repoſe, my ſpikenard gaue the odour thereof.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: A bundle of myrrhe my beloued is to me, he shal abide betwen my breſtes.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: A cluſtre of cypre my loue is to me, in the vineyardes of Engaddi.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Behold thou art fayre, ô my loue, behold thou art fayre, thyne eyes are as of doues.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Behold thou art fayre my beloued, & comlie: our litle bed is florishing.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: The beames of our houſes are of cedar, our rafters of cypreſſe trees.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I AM the flower of the filde, and the lilie of the valley.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: As the lilie among the thornes, ſo is my loue among the daughters.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: As the apletree among trees of the woddes, ſo is my beloued among the ſonnes. Vnder his shadow, whom I deſired, I ſate: and his fruite was ſweete vnto my throte.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: He brought me into the winceller, he hath ordered in me charitie.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Stay me vp with flowers, compaſſe me about with apples: becauſe I languish with loue.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: His lefthand vnder my head, and his righthand shal embrace me.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I adiure you ô daughters of Ieruſalem, by the roes, and the hartes of the fildes, that you rayſe not, nor make the beloued to awake, vntil herſelfe wil.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: The voice of my beloued, behold he cometh leaping in the mountaines, leaping ouer the little hilles:
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: my beloued is like vnto a roe, and to a fawne of hartes. Behold he ſtandeth behind our walle, looking through the windowes, looking forth by the grates.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Behold my beloued ſpeaketh to me: Ariſe, make haſt my loue, my doue, beautiful one, and come.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: For winter is now paſt, the rayne is gone, and departed.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: The flowers haue appeared in our land, the time of pruning is come: the voice of the turtledoue is heard in our land:
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: the figgetree hath brought forth her greene figges: the florishing vineyards haue geuen their ſauour. Ariſe my loue, my beautiful one, & come.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: My doue in the holes of the rocke, in the holow places of the wal, shew me thy face, let thy voice ſound in mine eares: for thy voice is ſweete, and thy face comely.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Catch vs the litle foxes, that deſtroy the vineyards: for our vineyard hath florished.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: My beloued to me, and I to him, who feedeth among the lilies,
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: til the day breake, and the shadowes decline. Returne: be like, my beloued, to a roe, and to the fawne of hartes vpon the mountaynes of Bether.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: IN my litle bed in the nightes I haue ſought him, whom my ſoule loueth, I haue ſought him, and haue not found.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I wil riſe, and wil goe about the citie: by the ſtreates and high waies, I wil ſeeke him whom my ſoule loueth: I haue ſought him, and haue not found.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: The watchmen which kepe the citie found me; Haue you ſeene him, whom my ſoule loueth.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: When I had a litle paſſed by them, I found him whom my ſoule loueth: I held him: neither wil I let him goe, til I bring him into my mothers houſe, and into the chamber of her that bare me.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I adiure you ô daughters of Ieruſalem by the roes, and the hartes of the fildes, that you rayſe not vp, nor make the beloued to awake, til herſelfe wil.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: What is she, that aſcendeth by the deſert, as a litle rod of ſmoke of the aromatical ſpices of myrtrhe, and frankincenſe, & of al powder of the apothecharie?
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Behold threeſcore valiants of the moſt valiant of Iſrael, compaſſe the litle bed of Salomon:
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: al holding ſwordes, and moſt cunning to battels: euerie mans ſword vpon his thigh for feares by night.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: King Salomon hath made him a portable throne of the wood of Libanus:
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: the pillers therof he hath made of ſiluer, the ſeate of gold, the going vp of purple: the middes he hath paued with charitie for the daughters of Ieruſalem.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Goe forth ye daughters of Sion, and ſee king Salomon in the diademe, wherewith his mother hath crowned him in the day of his deſpouſing, and in the day of the ioy of his heart.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: HOW beautiful art thou my loue, how beautiful art thou! thine eies as it were of doues, beſides that, which lyeth hid within. Thy heares as the flockes of goates, which haue come vp from mount Galaad.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy teeth as flockes of them that are shorne, which haue come vp from the lauatorie, al with twinnes, and there is no barren among them.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy lippes as a ſcarlet lace: and thy ſpeach ſweete. As à peece of a pomegranate, ſo are alſo thy cheekes, beſides that which lyeth hid within.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy necke is as the towre of Dauid, which is built with bulworkes: a thouſand targattes hang on it, al the armour of the valiants.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy two breaſtes as two fawnes the twinnes of a roe, which feede among the lilies,
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: til the day aſpire, and the shadowes decline. I wil goe to the mount of myrrhe, and to the little hil of frankencenſe.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thou art al fayre ô my loue, and there is not a ſpotte in thee.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Come from Libanus my ſpouſe, come from Libanus, come: thou shalt be crowned from the head of Amena, from the toppe of Sanir & Hermon, from the dennes of lions, from the mountaynes of leopardes.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thou haſt wounded my heart, my ſiſter ſpouſe, thou haſt wounded my heart in one of thine eies, and in one heare of thy necke.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: How beautiful are thy breaſtes my ſiſter ſpouſe! thy breaſtes are more beautiful then wine, and the odour of thine ointmentes aboue al aromatical ſpices.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy lippes my ſpouſe are as an honie combe diſtilling, honie and milke are vnder thy tongue: and the odour of thy garments as the odour of frankincenſe.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: My ſiſter ſpouſe is a garden incloſed, a garden incloſed, a fountaine ſealed vp.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy offſprings a paradiſe of pomegranats with orchard fruites. Cypres with ſpiknard,
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: ſpiknard, and ſafren, ſweete cane and cinnamon, with al the trees of Libanus, myrrhe and aloes with al the chiefe ointmentes.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: The fountaine of gardens: the wel of liuing waters, which runne with violence from Libanus.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Ariſe Northwinde, & come Southwinde, blow through my garden, and let the aromatical ſpices therof flowe.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: LET my beloued come into his garden, and eate the fruite of his appletrees. I am come into my garden ô my ſiſter ſpouſe, I haue reaped my myrrhe, with myne aromatical ſpices: I haue eaten the honiecombe with mine honie, I haue drunke my wine with my milke: eate ô frendes, and drinke, and be inebriated my deareſt.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I ſleepe, and my hart watcheth: the voice of my beloued knocking: Open to me my ſiſter, my loue, my doue, mine immaculate: becauſe my head is ful of dew, and my lockes of the droppes of the nightes.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I haue ſpoyled myſelfe of my robe, how shal I be clothed with it? I haue washed my feete, how shal I defile them?
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: My beloued put his hand through the hôle, and my bellie trembled at his touch.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I aroſe, that I might open to my beloued: my handes haue diſtilled myrrhe, and my fingers are ful of moſt approued myrrhe.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I opened the bolt of my dore to my beloued: but he had turned aſide, and was paſſed. My ſoule melted, as he ſpake: I ſought, and found him not: I called, and he did not anſwer me.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: The keepers that goe about the citie found me: they ſtroke me, and wounded me: the keepers of the walles tooke away my cloke.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I adiure you ô daughters of Hieruſalem, if you shal finde my beloued, that you tel him, that I languishe with loue.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: What maner of one is thy beloued of the beloued, ô moſt beautiful of wemen? What maner of one is thy beloued of the beloued, that thou haſt ſo adiured vs?
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: My beloued is white and ruddie, choſen of thouſands.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: His head is as the beſt gold: his heares as the branches of palmetrees, blacke as à rauen.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: His eies as doues vpon the litle riuers of waters, which are washed with milke, and ſitte beſide the moſt ful ſtreames.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: His cheekes are as litle beddes of aromatical ſpices ſet of the pigmentaries. His lippes are as lilies diſtilling principal myrrhe.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: His handes wrought round of gold, ful of hyacinthes. His bellie of iuorie, diſtinguished with ſapphires.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: His thighes as pillers of marble, that are vpon feete of gold. His forme as of Libanus, elect as the cedars.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: His throte moſt ſweete, and he whole to be deſired: ſuch an one is my beloued, and he is my frend, ô daughters of Hieruſalem.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Whither is thy beloued gone ô moſt beautiful of wemen? whither is thy beloued turned aſide, and we wil ſeeke him with thee?
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: MY beloued is gone downe into his garden, to the bed of aromatical ſpices, to feede in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I to my beloued, and my beloued to me, who feedeth among the lilies.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thou art fayre ô my loue, ſweete, and comelie as Hieruſalem: terrible as the armie of a campe ſet in aray.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Turne away thine eies from me, becauſe they haue made me flee away. Thy heares as a flocke of goates, which haue appeared from Galaad.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy teeth as à flocke of sheepe, which haue come vp from the lauatorie, al with twinnes, and there is no barren among them.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: As the barke of a pomegranate, ſo are thy cheekes beſide thy hidden.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: There are threeſcore queenes, & foureſcore concubines, and of yongmaydes there is no number.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: My doue is one, my perfect one, she is the only to her mother, elect to her that bare her. The daughters haue ſeene her, and declared her to be moſt bleſſed: the queenes and concubines, and haue prayſed her.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: What is she, that cometh forth as the morning ryſing, fayre as the moone, elect as the ſunne, terrible as the armie of a campe ſet in aray?
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I came downe into the garden of nuttes, to ſee the fruites of the valles, and to looke if the vineyarde had florished, and the pomegranats budded.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I knew not: my ſoule trubled me for the chariotes of Aminadab.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Returne, returne ô Sulamiteſſe: returne, returne that we may behold thee.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: WHAT shalt thou ſee in the Sulamiteſſe but the companies of campes? How beautiful are thy paſes in shoes, ô princes daughter! the ioyntes of thy thighes are as iewels, that are made by the hand of the artificer.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy nauel as à round bowle, neuer wanting cuppes. Thy bellie as an heape of wheate, compaſſed about with lilies.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy two breſts, as two fawnes the twinnes of a roe.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy necke as a towre of yuorie. Thine eies as the fishpooles in Heſebon, which are in the gate of the daughter of the multitude. Thy noſe as the towre of Libanus; that looketh againſt Damaſcus.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy head as Carmelus: and the heares of thy head as a kings purple tyed to cundite pipes.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: How beautiful art thou, and how comely my deareſt, in delightes!
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy ſtature is like to a palmetree, & thy breaſtes to cluſters of grapes.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I ſayd: I wil goe vp into the palmetree, and wil take hold of the fruites therof: and thy breaſts shal be as the cluſters of a vineyard: and the odour of thy mouth as it were of apples.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thy throate as the beſt wine, worthie for my beloued to drinke, & for his lippes and his teeth to ruminate.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I to my beloued, and his turning is toward me.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Come my beloued, let vs goe forth in to the filde, let vs abide in the villages.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Let vs riſe early to the vineyards, let vs ſee if the vineyard florishe, if the flowers be readie to bring forth fruites, if the pomegranates florish: there wil I giue thee my breaſts.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: The Mandragoraes haue geuen a ſmel. In our gates al fruites: the new and the old, my beloued, I haue kept for thee.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: WHO shal giue to me thee my brother, ſucking the breaſts of my mother, that I may finde thee without, and kiſſe thee, and now no man deſpiſe me?
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I wil take hold of thee, and wil bring thee into my mothers houſe: there thou shalt teach me, and I wil giue thee a cuppe of ſpiced wine, and new wine of my pomegranats.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: His left hand vnder my head, and his right hand shal embrace me.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I adiure you ô daughters of Ieruſalem, that you rayſe not vp, nor make the beloued to awake til herſelfe wil.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Who is this, that cometh vp from the deſert, flowing with delightes, leaning vpon her beloued? Vnder the appletree I rayſed thee vp: there thy mother was corrupted, there she was defloured that bare thee.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Put me as a ſeale vpon thy hart, as a ſeale vpon thyne arme: becauſe loue is ſtrong as death: ielouſie is hard as hel, the lampes therof lampes of fyre and flames.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Manie waters can not quench charitie, neither shal floudes ouerwhelme it: if a man shal giue al the ſubſtance of his houſe for loue, as nothing he shal deſpiſe it.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Our ſiſter is litle, and hath no breaſts. What shal we doe to our ſiſter in the day when she is to be ſpoken vnto?
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: If she be a wal, let vs build vpon it bulwarkes of ſiluer: if she be a doore, let vs ioyne it together with bordes of ceder.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: I am a wal: and my breaſts are aſ a towre, ſince I was made before him as one finding peace.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: The peacemaker had a vinyard, in that which hath peoples: he deliuered the ſame to keepers, a man bringeth for the fruite thereof a thouſand peeces of ſiluer.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: My vineyard is before me. A thouſand are thy peacemakers, and two hundreth for them, that keepe the fruites thereof.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Thou that dwelleſt in the gardens, the frends doe harken: make me heare thy voice.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: Flee, ô my beloued, and be like to the roe, and to the fawne of harts vpon the mountaines of aromatical ſpices.
label: Canticle of Canticles

text: LOVE iuſtice, you that iudge the earth. Thincke of our Lord in goodnes, and in ſimplicitie of hart ſeeke him:
label: Wisdom

text: becauſe he is found of them, that tempt him not: and he appeareth to them, that haue faith in him.
label: Wisdom

text: For peruerſe cogitations ſeperate from God: and proued powre chaſteneth the vnwiſe:
label: Wisdom

text: becauſe wiſdom wil not enter into a malicious ſoule, nor dwel in a bodie ſubiect to ſinnes.
label: Wisdom

text: For the Holie Ghoſt of diſcipline, wil flie from him that feyneth, and wil withdraw himſelfe from the cogitations, that are without vnderſtanding, and he shal be chaſtened of iniquitie enſewing:
label: Wisdom

text: For the ſpirite of wiſdom is gentle, and wil not deliuer the curſer from his lippes: becauſe God is witnes of his reynes, and he is a true ſearcher of his hart, and an hearer of his tongue.
label: Wisdom

text: Becauſe the Spirite of our Lord hath replenished the whole world: and that, which contayneth al thinges, hath the knowledge of voice.
label: Wisdom

text: For this cauſe he that ſpeaketh vniuſt thinges, can not be hid, neither shal the chaſtiſing iudgment paſſe him.
label: Wisdom

text: For in the cogitations of the impious there shal be examination: and the hearing of his workes shal come to God, to the chaſtiſing of his iniquities.
label: Wisdom

text: Becauſe the eare of ielouſie heareth al thinges, and the tumult of murmurings shal not be hid.
label: Wisdom

text: Kepe your ſelues therfore from murmuring, which profiteth nothing, and refraine your tongue from detraction, becauſe an obſcure ſpeache shal not paſſe in vaine: and the mouth that lyeth, killeth the ſoule.
label: Wisdom

text: Zeale not death in the errour of your life, neither procure ye perdition by the workes of your handes.
label: Wisdom

text: Becauſe God made not death, neither doth he reioyce in the perdition of the liuing.
label: Wisdom

text: For he created al thinges to be: and he made the nations of the earth to health: and there is no medicine of deſtruction in them, nor kingdome of hel in the earth.
label: Wisdom

text: ( For iuſtice is perpetual and immortal.)
label: Wisdom

text: But the impious with handes & wordes haue prouoked it: and eſteming it a freind, haue fallen to decay, and haue made couenantes with it: becauſe they are worthie to be of the part therof.
label: Wisdom

text: FOR they haue ſaid thinking with themſelues not wel: Little, and with tediouſnes is the time of our life: and in the end of a man there is no recouerie, and there is none knowne that hath returned from hel:
label: Wisdom

text: becauſe of nothing were we borne, and after this, we shal be as if we had not bene: becauſe the breath is a ſmoke in our noſthrels: & ſpeach a ſparke to moue our hart.
label: Wisdom

text: Which being extinguished, our bodie shal be ashes, and the ſpirit shal be powred abrode as ſoft ayre, and our life shal paſſe as the trace of a cloude, and shal be diſſolued as a miſt, which is driuen away by the beames of the ſunne, and oppreſſed with the heate therof:
label: Wisdom

text: and our name in time shal be forgotten, and no man shal haue remembrance of our workes.
label: Wisdom

text: For our time is the paſſing of a shadow, and there is no returne of our end: becauſe it is ſealed, and no man returneth.
label: Wisdom

text: Come therfore, and let vs enioy the good thinges that are, and let vs quickly vſe the creature as in youth.
label: Wisdom

text: Let vs fil ourſelues with precious wine, and oyntments: and let not the flowre of the time paſſe vs.
label: Wisdom

text: Let vs crowne ourſelues with roſes, before they wither: let there be no medow, which our riote shal not paſſe through.
label: Wisdom

text: Let none of vs be exempted from our rioteouſnes: euerie where let vs leaue ſignes of ioy: becauſe this is our portion, and this our lot.
label: Wisdom

text: Let vs oppreſſe the poore iuſt man, and not ſpare the widow, nor reuerence the oldmans grey head of long time.
label: Wisdom

text: But let our ſtrength be the law of iuſtice: for that which is weake, is found vnprofitable.
label: Wisdom

text: Let vs therfore circumuent the iuſt, becauſe he is vnprofitable to vs, and he is contrarie to our workes, and reprochfully obiecteth vnto vs the ſinnes of the law, and defameth in vs the ſinnes of our diſcipline.
label: Wisdom

text: He boaſteth that he hath the knowlege of God, and nameth himſelfe the ſonne of God.
label: Wisdom

text: He is made vnto vs to the defaming of our cogitations.
label: Wisdom

text: He is greuous vnto vs euen to behold, becauſe his life is vnlike to others, and his wayes are changed.
label: Wisdom

text: We are eſtemed of him as triflers, and he abſteyneth from our wayes as from vncleannes, and he preferreth the later ends of the iuſt, and glorieth that he hath God for his father.
label: Wisdom

text: Let vs ſee therfore if his wordes be true, and let vs proue what thinges shal come to him, and we shal know what shal be his later ends.
label: Wisdom

text: For if he be the true ſonne of God, he wil defend him, & wil deliuer him from the hands of the aduerſaries.
label: Wisdom

text: By contumelie and torment let vs examine him, that we may know his reuerence, and proue his patience.
label: Wisdom

text: To a moſt shameful death let vs condemne him: for there shal be reſpect had vnto him by his wordes.
label: Wisdom

text: Theſe thinges haue they thought, and haue erred: for their malice hath blinded them.
label: Wisdom

text: And they haue not knowen the ſacraments of God, nor hoped for the reward of iuſtice, nor eſtemed the honour of holie ſoules.
label: Wisdom

text: For God created man incorruptible, and to the image of his owne likenes he made him.
label: Wisdom

text: But by the enuie of the diuel, death entred into the world:
label: Wisdom

text: and they folow him that are of his part.
label: Wisdom

text: BVT the ſoules of the iuſt are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shal not touch them.
label: Wisdom

text: They ſemed in the eies of the vnwiſe to die: and their deceaſe was counted affliction:
label: Wisdom

text: and that which with vs is the way, is deſtruction: but they are in peace.
label: Wisdom

text: And though before men they ſuffered torments, their hope is ful of immortalitie.
label: Wisdom

text: Vexed in few thinges, in many they shal be wel diſpoſed of: becauſe God hath tempted them, and hath found them worthie of him ſelfe.
label: Wisdom

text: As gold in the furnace he hath proued them, and as an hoſt of holocauſt he hath receiued them, and in time there shal be reſpect of them.
label: Wisdom

text: The iuſt shal shine, and as ſparkes in a place of reedes they shal runne abrode.
label: Wisdom

text: They shal iudge nations, & haue dominion ouer peoples, and their Lord shal reigne for euer.
label: Wisdom

text: They that truſt in him, shal vnderſtand truth: and the faithful in loue shal reſt in him: becauſe reſt and peace is to his elect.
label: Wisdom

text: But the impious according to the thinges which they haue thought, shal haue correption: which haue neglected the iuſt, & haue reuolted from our Lord.
label: Wisdom

text: For he that reiecteth wiſdom, and diſcipline, is vnhappie: and their hope is vaine, and labours without fruite and their workes vnprofitable.
label: Wisdom

text: Their wiues are ſenſles, and their children moſt wicked.
label: Wisdom

text: Curſed is their creature: becauſe happie is the barren woman: and the vndefiled, which hath not knowen bed in ſinne, she shal haue fruite in viſitation of holie ſoules:
label: Wisdom

text: and the eunuch, that hath not wrought iniquitie with his hands, nor thought moſt wicked things againſt God: for the choſen gift of fayth shal be geuen to him, and a moſt acceptable lot in the temple of God.
label: Wisdom

text: For of good labour there is glorious fruite, and the roote of wiſdom which falleth not.
label: Wisdom

text: But the children of adulterers shal be in conſumation, and the ſede of the vnlawful bed shal be deſtroyed.
label: Wisdom

text: And if certes they be of long life, they shal be reputed for nothing, & their laſt oldage shal be without honour.
label: Wisdom

text: And if they dye quickly they shal haue no hope, nor ſpeach of comfort in the day of acknowledging
label: Wisdom

text: For of a wicked nation the endes are cruel
label: Wisdom

text: O How beautiful is the chaſte generation with glorie: for the memorie therof is immortal: becauſe it is knowen both with God, and with men.
label: Wisdom

text: When it is preſent, they imitate it, and they deſire it when it hath withdrawen it-ſelf, and it triumpheth crowned for euer, winning the reward of vndefiled conflictes.
label: Wisdom

text: But the multitude of the impious, that hath manie children shal not be profitable, and baſtarde plants shal not take deepe roote, nor lay ſure fundation.
label: Wisdom

text: And if in the boughes for a time they shal ſpring being weakly ſet, they shal be moued of the winde, and by the vehemencie of the windes they shal be rooted out.
label: Wisdom

text: For the vnperfect boughes shal be broken, and their fruites shal be vnprofitable, and ſowre to eate, and meete for nothing.
label: Wisdom

text: For the children that be borne of wicked ſleepes, are witneſſes of wickednes againſt the parents in their examination.
label: Wisdom

text: But the iuſt if he be preuented with death, shal be in a place of refreshing.
label: Wisdom

text: For venerable oldage is not that of long time, nor accounted by the number of yeares: but the vnderſtanding of a man are grey heares:
label: Wisdom

text: and an immaculate life is old age.
label: Wisdom

text: Pleaſing God he is made beloued, and liuing among ſinners he was tranſlated.
label: Wisdom

text: He was taken away leſt malice should change his vnderſtanding, or leſt anie guile might deceiue his ſoule.
label: Wisdom

text: For the bewitching of vanitie obſcureth good thinges, and the inconſtancie of concupiſcence peruerteth the vnderſtanding that is without malice.
label: Wisdom

text: Being conſummate in short ſpace he fulfilled much time:
label: Wisdom

text: for his ſoule pleaſed God: for this cauſe he haſtened to bring him out of the middes of iniquities: but the peoples that are ſeing, and not vnderſtanding, nor putting ſuch thinges in their hartes:
label: Wisdom

text: that the grace of God, and mercie is toward his ſaintes, and reſpect toward his elect.
label: Wisdom

text: But the iuſt dead condemneth the impious aliue, and youth ſoone ended, the long life of the vniuſt.
label: Wisdom

text: For they shal ſee the end of the wiſe, and shal not vnderſtand what God hath thought of him, and why our Lord hath fenſed him.
label: Wisdom

text: For they shal ſee and shal contemne him: but our Lord shal laugh them to ſcorne,
label: Wisdom

text: and they shal fal after this without honour, and in contumelie among the dead for euer: becauſe he shal breake them puffed vp without voice, and shal remoue them from the fundations, and they shal be made deſolate vnto the higheſt degree: and shal be moorning, and the memorie of them shal perish.
label: Wisdom

text: They shal come fearful in cogitation of their ſinnes, and their iniquities on the contrarie shal conuince them.
label: Wisdom

text: THEN shal the iuſt ſtand in great conſtancie againſt thoſe that haue afflicted them, and taken away their labours.
label: Wisdom

text: They ſeing shal be trubled with horrible feare, and shal meruel at the ſodennes of vnexpected ſaluation,
label: Wisdom

text: ſaying within themſelues, repenting, and ſighing for anguish of ſpirit: Theſe are they, whom we had ſometime in deriſion, and in a parable of reproch.
label: Wisdom

text: We ſenſleſſe eſtemed their life madnes, and their end without honour.
label: Wisdom

text: Behold how they are counted among the children of God, and their lot is among the ſaints.
label: Wisdom

text: We therfore haue erred from the way of truth, and the light of iuſtice hath not shined to vs, and the ſunne of vnderſtanding roſe not to vs.
label: Wisdom

text: We are weried in the way of iniquitie and perdition, and haue walked hard wayes, but the way of our Lord we haue not knowen.
label: Wisdom

text: What hath pride profited vs? or what commoditie hath the vaunting of riches brought to vs?
label: Wisdom

text: Al thoſe thinges are paſſed away as a shadow, and as a meſſenger running before,
label: Wisdom

text: and as a shippe, that paſſeth through the ſurging waters: wherof, when it is paſt, the trace can not be found, nor the path of that shippes keele in the waues:
label: Wisdom

text: or as a bird, that flyeth through in the ayre, of which there is no token can be found of her paſſage, but only a ſound of the winges beating the light winde: and by vehemence of going cutting the ayre, mouing the winges she is flowen through, and afterward there is no ſigne found of her way:
label: Wisdom

text: or as when an arrow is shotte forth to a ſette marke, the diuided ayre is forthwith cloſed in itſelf againe, ſo that the paſſage therof is not knowen:
label: Wisdom

text: ſo we alſo being borne forthwith ceaſed to be: and of vertue certes haue bene able to shew no ſigne: but in our naughtines we are conſumed.
label: Wisdom

text: Such thinges ſayd they in hel, which ſinned:
label: Wisdom

text: becauſe the hope of the impious is as duſt, which is taken away with the winde: and as a thinne froth, which is diſperſed by the ſtorme: and as ſmoke that is ſcatered abrode by the winde: and as the memorie of a gheſt of one day that paſſeth.
label: Wisdom

text: But the iuſt shal liue for euer, and their reward is with our Lord, and cogitation of them with the Higheſt.
label: Wisdom

text: Therfore shal they receiue a kingdom of honour, & a crowne of beautie at the hand of our Lord: becauſe with his right hand he wil couer them, and with in his holie arme he wil defend them.
label: Wisdom

text: And his zele wil take armour, and he wil arme the creature to the reuenge of the enemies.
label: Wisdom

text: He wil put on iuſtice for a breſtplate, & wil take ſincere iudgement for an helmet:
label: Wisdom

text: he wil take equitie for an inuincible shilde:
label: Wisdom

text: and he wil sharpen fierce wrath for a ſpeare, and the round world shal fight with him againſt the ſenſleſſe.
label: Wisdom

text: The shottes of lightenings shal goe directly, & as it were from a bow of the clouds wel bent they shal be caſt forth, and shal light on a certaine place.
label: Wisdom

text: And from rocked wrath shal thicke haile ſtones be caſt, the water of the ſea shal rage againſt them, and the riuers shal runne together roughly.
label: Wisdom

text: A ſpirit of powre shal ſtand againſt them, and as a hurlewinde shal diuide them: and their iniquitie shal bring al the land to a deſert, and naughtines shal ouerthrow the ſeates of the mightie.
label: Wisdom

text: WISEDOM is better then ſtrength: and a wiſeman then a ſtrong.
label: Wisdom

text: Heare therfore ye kinges, & vnderſtand, lerne ye iudges of the endes of the earth.
label: Wisdom

text: Geue eare ye, that rule multitudes, and that pleaſe yourſelues in multitudes of nations:
label: Wisdom

text: becauſe the powre is geuen you of our Lord, and ſtrength by the Higheſt, who wil examine your workes, and ſearch your cogitations:
label: Wisdom

text: becauſe when you were the miniſters of his kingdom, you iudged not rightly, nor kept the law of iuſtice, nor haue walked according to the wil of God.
label: Wisdom

text: Horribly and quickly wil he appeare to you: becauſe moſt ſeuere iudgement shal be done on them, that beare rule.
label: Wisdom

text: For to the litle one mercie is granted: but the mightie shal mightely ſuffer torments.
label: Wisdom

text: For God wil not except any mans perſon, neither wil feare the greatnes of any man: becauſe he made the litle and the great, & he hath equally care of al.
label: Wisdom

text: But to the ſtronger more ſtrong torment is imminent.
label: Wisdom

text: To you therfore ô kings are theſe my wordes, that you may lerne wiſdom, and not fal.
label: Wisdom

text: For they that haue kept iuſt thinges iuſtly, shal be iuſtified: and they that haue lerned theſe thinges, shal find what they may anſwer.
label: Wisdom

text: Couet ye therfore my wordes, and loue them, and you shal haue diſcipline.
label: Wisdom

text: Wiſdom is cleere, and ſuch as neuer fadeth, and is eaſely ſene of them that loue her, and is found of them that ſeeke her.
label: Wisdom

text: She preuenteth them that couete her, that she firſt may shew herſelf vnto them.
label: Wisdom

text: He that awaketh early to her, shal not labour: for he shal find her ſitting at her doores.
label: Wisdom

text: To thinke therfore of her, is perfect vnderſtanding: and he that watcheth for her, shal quickly be ſecure.
label: Wisdom

text: Becauſe she goeth about ſeeking them that be worthie of her, and in the wayes she wil shew her ſelf to them cheerefully, and in al prouidence she wil meete them.
label: Wisdom

text: For the beginning of her is the moſt true deſire of diſcipline.
label: Wisdom

text: The care therfore of diſcipline, is loue: and loue, is the keeping of her lawes: and the keeping of the lawes, is the conſummation of incorruption:
label: Wisdom

text: and incorruption maketh to be next to God.
label: Wisdom

text: Therfore the deſire of wiſdom leadeth to the euerlaſting kingdom.
label: Wisdom

text: If therfore you be delighted with thrones, and with ſcepters ô ye kinges of the people, loue wiſdom, that you may reigne for euer.
label: Wisdom

text: Loue the light of wiſdom al ye that beare rule ouer peoples.
label: Wisdom

text: But what wiſdom is, and how she was made, I wil declare: and I wil not hide from you the myſteries of God, but from the beginning of her natiuitie I wil ſearch out, and ſette the knowlege of her into light, and wil not let paſſe the truth:
label: Wisdom

text: neither wil I goe with pyning enuie: becauſe ſuch a man shal not be partaker of wiſdom.
label: Wisdom

text: But the multitude of the wiſe is the health of the round world: and a wiſe king is the ſtabilitie of the people.
label: Wisdom

text: Therfore take ye diſcipline by my wordes, and it shal profite you.
label: Wisdom

text: I ALSO certes am a mortal man, like to al, and of the earthlie kinred of him, that was made firſt, and in the wombe of my mother was I fashioned flesh,
label: Wisdom

text: the time of ten monethes was I brought together in bloud, of the ſeede of man, and the delectation of ſleepe concurring.
label: Wisdom

text: And I being borne receiued the common ayre, and fel vpon the earth, that is made alike, and the firſt voice like to al men did I put forth weeping.
label: Wisdom

text: I was nourished in ſwadling clothes, and great cares.
label: Wisdom

text: For none of the kinges had other begynning of natiuitie.
label: Wisdom

text: There is one entrance therfore into life to al men, and like departure.
label: Wisdom

text: For this cauſe I wished, and vnderſtanding was geuen me: and I inuocated, and the ſpirit of wiſdom came vpon me:
label: Wisdom

text: and I preferred her before kingdoms and thrones, and riches I counted to be nothing in compariſon of her.
label: Wisdom

text: Neither did I compare the precious ſtone to her: becauſe al gold in compariſon of her, is a litle ſand, and ſiluer in the ſight of her shal be eſtemed as clay.
label: Wisdom

text: Aboue health and beautie did I loue her, and purpoſed to haue her for light: becauſe her light can not be extinguished.
label: Wisdom

text: And al good thinges came to me together with her, and very much honeſtie by her handes,
label: Wisdom

text: and I reioyced in al: becauſe this wiſdom went before me, and I was ignorant that she is the mother of al theſe.
label: Wisdom

text: Which I lerned without fiction, and doe communicate without enuie, and her honeſtie I hid not.
label: Wisdom

text: For she is an infinite treaſure to men: which who ſo haue, are made partakers of the frenship of God, commended for the gifts of diſcipline.
label: Wisdom

text: And to me God hath geuen to ſpeake according to my minde, and to preſume thinges worthie of thoſe, that are geuen me: becauſe he is the guide of wiſdom, and the creator of the wiſe:
label: Wisdom

text: for in his hand are both we, & our wordes, and wiſdom, and the knowlege and diſcipline of workes.
label: Wisdom

text: For he gaue me the true knowlege of thoſe thinges, which are: that I may know the diſpoſition of the round world, and the vertues of the elements,
label: Wisdom

text: the beginning, & end, & middes of times, the permutations of changeable ſeaſons, and conſummations of times,
label: Wisdom

text: the courſes of the yeare, and diſpoſitions of the ſtarres,
label: Wisdom

text: the natures of beaſtes, and furies of wilde beaſtes, the force of windes, and the cogitations of men, the differences of plantes, and vertues of rootes,
label: Wisdom

text: and whatſoeuer are hid thinges and not forſene, I haue lerned: for wiſdom the worker of al taught me.
label: Wisdom

text: For in her is the ſpirite of vnderſtanding, holie, onlie, manifold, ſubtil, eloquent, moueable, vndefiled, ſure, ſwete, louing good, sharpe, who nothing hindereth wel doing,
label: Wisdom

text: gentle, benigne, ſtable, certaine, ſecure, hauing al powre, forſeing al thinges, and that conteyneth al ſpirites: intelligible, cleane, ſubtile.
label: Wisdom

text: For wiſdom is more moueable then al moueable thinges: and reacheth euerie where becauſe of her cleannes.
label: Wisdom

text: For she is a vapour of the powre of God, & a certaine ſincere emanation of the glorie of God omnipotent: and therfore no defiled thing cometh vnto her.
label: Wisdom

text: For she is the brightnes of eternal light, & the vnſpotted glaſſe of Gods maieſtie, and the image of his goodnes.
label: Wisdom

text: And wheras she is one, she can doe al thinges: and permanent in herſelfe she reneweth al thinges, and by nations tranſporteth herſelf into holie ſoules, she maketh the frendes of God, and Prophetes.
label: Wisdom

text: For God loueth none, but him, that dwelleth with wiſdom.
label: Wisdom

text: For she is more beautiful then the ſunne, and aboue al diſpoſition of the ſtarres, being compared to light she is found the firſt.
label: Wisdom

text: For night ſuccedeth to it, but malice ouercometh not wiſdom.
label: Wisdom

text: SHE reacheth therfore from end vnto end mightely, and diſpoſeth al thinges ſwetely.
label: Wisdom

text: Her haue I loued, and haue ſought her out from my youth, and haue ſought to take her for my ſpouſe, and I was made a louer of her beautie.
label: Wisdom

text: She glorifieth her nobilitie, hauing conſociation with God: yea and the Lord of al hath loued her.
label: Wisdom

text: For she is the miſtreſſe of the diſcipline of God, & the chooſer of his workes.
label: Wisdom

text: And if riches be deſired in life, what is richer then wiſdom, which worketh al thinges?
label: Wisdom

text: And if vnderſtanding doe worke: who is the worker of thoſe things that are, more then she?
label: Wisdom

text: And if a man loue iuſtice: her labours haue great vertues: for she teacheth ſobrietie, and prudence, and iuſtice, and ſtrength, then the which nothing is more profitable in life to men.
label: Wisdom

text: And if a man deſire multitude of knowlege: she knoweth thinges paſt, & coniectureth of thinges to come: she knoweth the ſubtilities of wordes, and the ſolution of arguments: she knoweth ſignes and wonders before they be done, and the euentes of times and ages.
label: Wisdom

text: I purpoſed therfore to bring her to me to liue together: knowing that she wil communicate vnto me of good thinges, and wil be a comfort of my cogitation & tediouſnes.
label: Wisdom

text: I shal haue for her ſake glorie with the multitudes, and honour with the ancient being yong:
label: Wisdom

text: and I shal be found sharpe in iudgement, and in the ſight of the mightie I shal be meruelous, and the faces of princes wil meruel at me.
label: Wisdom

text: Holding my peace they shal expect me, and whiles I ſpeake manie wordes, they shal lay their hands on their mouth.
label: Wisdom

text: Moreouer by her I shal haue immortalitie: and I shal leaue an eternal memorie to them, that shal be after me.
label: Wisdom

text: I shal diſpoſe peoples: and nations shal be ſubiect to me.
label: Wisdom

text: Horrible kings hearing shal feare me: in the multitude I shal ſeme good, and in battel ſtrong.
label: Wisdom

text: Entring into my houſe, I shal reſt with her: for her conuerſation hath no bitternes, nor her companie tediouſnes, but ioy and gladneſſe.
label: Wisdom

text: Thinking theſe thinges with myſelfe, and recording in my hart, that immortalitie is in the kindred of wiſedom,
label: Wisdom

text: and good delectation in her frendship, and in the workes of her handes honeſtie without defect, and wiſdom in the diſputation of her talke, and glorie in the communication of her wordes: I went about ſeeking, that I might take her to me.
label: Wisdom

text: And I was a wittie childe, and had gotten a good ſoule.
label: Wisdom

text: And wheras I was more good, I came to a bodie vndefiled.
label: Wisdom

text: And as I knew that I could not otherwiſe be continent, vnleſſe God gaue it, this verie thing alſo was wiſdom, to know whoſe this gift was: I went to our Lord, and beſought him, and ſaid from my whole hart.
label: Wisdom

text: GOD of my fathers, and Lord of mercie, which madeſt al thinges with thy word,
label: Wisdom

text: and by thy wiſdom didſt appoint man, that he should haue dominion of the creature, that was made by thee,
label: Wisdom

text: that he should diſpoſe the roundworld in equitie and iuſtice, and execute iudgement in direction of hart:
label: Wisdom

text: geue me wiſdom the aſſiſtant of thy ſeates, and repel me not from thy children:
label: Wisdom

text: becauſe I am thy ſeruant, and the ſonne of thy handmaide, a weake man, and of ſmal time, and leſſe to the vnderſtanding of iudgement and lawes.
label: Wisdom

text: And if one be perfect among the children of men, and thy wiſdom be abſent from him, he shal be counted for nothing.
label: Wisdom

text: Thou haſt choſen me king to thy people, and iudge of thy ſonnes, and daughters:
label: Wisdom

text: and badſt me build a temple in thy holie mount, and an altar in the citie of thy habitation, a ſimilitude of thy holie tabernacle, which thou didſt prepare from the beginning:
label: Wisdom

text: and thy wiſdom with thee, which knew thy workes, which then alſo was preſent when thou madeſt the roundworld, and knew what was pleaſing to thyne eyes, and what was direct in thy precepts.
label: Wisdom

text: Send her from thy holy heauens, and from the ſeate of thy greatnes, that she may be with me, and may labour with me, that I may know what is acceptable with thee:
label: Wisdom

text: for she knoweth al thinges, & vnderſtandeth, and shal conduct me in my workes ſoberly, & shal keepe me with her might.
label: Wisdom

text: And my workes shal be acceptable, and I shal gouerne thy people iuſtly, and shal be worthie of the ſeates of my father.
label: Wisdom

text: For who of men is able to know the counſel of God? or who can thinke what God wil?
label: Wisdom

text: For the cogitations of mortal men be fearful, and our prouidences vncertaine.
label: Wisdom

text: For the bodie, that is corrupted burdeneth the ſoule, and the earthlie habitation preſſeth downe the vnderſtanding that thinketh manie thinges.
label: Wisdom

text: And we doe hardly coniecture the thinges that are in the earth: and the thinges that are in ſight, we finde with labour. But the thinges that are in the heauens who shal ſearch our?
label: Wisdom

text: And thy ſenſe who shal know, vnles thou geue wiſdom, and ſend thy holie ſpirit from on high:
label: Wisdom

text: and ſo the pathes of them, that are on the earth may be corrected, and men lerne the thinges that pleaſe thee?
label: Wisdom

text: For by wiſdom they were healed, whoſoeuer haue pleaſed thee ô Lord from the begynning.
label: Wisdom

text: SHE kept him, that was firſt made of God father of the world, when he was created alone,
label: Wisdom

text: and she brought him out of his ſinne, and gaue him powre to conteyne al thinges.
label: Wisdom

text: After the vniuſt departed in his anger from her, by the furie of brothers manſlaughter perished.
label: Wisdom

text: For whoſe cauſe, when water deſtroyed the earth, wiſdom healed it againe, gouerning the iuſt by contemptible wood.
label: Wisdom

text: She euen in the conſent of wickednes, when the nations had confederated themſelues, knewe the iuſt, and preſerued him without blame to God, and in his ſonnes mercie kept the ſtrong.
label: Wisdom

text: She deliuered the iuſt, fleing from the impious that perished, when the fyre came downe vpon Pentapolis:
label: Wisdom

text: to whom for a witnes of their wickednes the deſert land ſtandeth ſmoking, and trees hauing fruites at vncertain ſeaſon; and the memorie of an incredulous ſoule a ſtanding piller of ſalt.
label: Wisdom

text: For pretermitting wiſdom they did not only ſlippe in this, that they were ignorant of good thinges, but they left alſo vnto men a memorie of their foolishnes, that in thoſe thinges, in which they ſinned in, they could not be hid neither.
label: Wisdom

text: But wiſdom hath deliuered them, that obſerue her from ſorowes.
label: Wisdom

text: And the iuſt fleing his brothers wrath, she conducted by the right wayes, and shewed him the kingdom of God, and gaue him the knowlege of the holie, did honeſt him in labours, and accomplised his labours.
label: Wisdom

text: In the fraude of the circumuenters of him she was preſent with him, and made him honorable.
label: Wisdom

text: She kept him from the enemies, and from ſeducers she defended him, and from ſeducers she defended him, and gaue him a ſtrong fight, thas he might ouercome, and know that wiſdom is mightier then al.
label: Wisdom

text: She forſooke not the iuſt being ſold, but deliuered him from ſinners: and she went downe with him into the pitte,
label: Wisdom

text: and in bands leaft him not, til she brought him the ſcepter of a kingdome, and might againſt them, that oppreſſed him: and shewed them to be lyers, that ſpotted him, and gaue him eternal glorie.
label: Wisdom

text: The iuſt people, and ſeede without blame she deliuered from the nations, that oppreſſed them.
label: Wisdom

text: She entered into the ſoule of the ſeruant of God, and ſtood againſt dreadful kinges in wonders and ſignes.
label: Wisdom

text: And she rendred to the iuſt the hope of their labours, and conducted them in a meruelous way: and she was vnto them for a couerr in the day, and for the light of ſtarres by night:
label: Wisdom

text: and she tranſported them through the Redſea, and caried them ouer through a great water.
label: Wisdom

text: But their enemies she drowned in the ſea, and from the depth of hel she brought them out. Therfore the iuſt tooke the ſpoyles of the impious,
label: Wisdom

text: and they ſang thy holie name ô Lord, and thy victorious hand they praiſed together:
label: Wisdom

text: becauſe wiſdom hath opened the mouth of the dumme, and the tongues of infants she hath made eloquent.
label: Wisdom

text: SHE directed their workes in the handes of a holy prophet.
label: Wisdom

text: They made a iourney through the deſerts, that were not inhabited: and in deſert places they pitched cottages.
label: Wisdom

text: They ſtood againſt the aduerſaries, and reuenged themſelues of the enemies.
label: Wisdom

text: They thirſted, and inuocated thee, and water was geuen them out of a moſt high rorcke, and quenching of their thirſt out of the hard ſtone.
label: Wisdom

text: For by the thinges wherby their enemies ſuffered punishment, for defect of their drinke, and therein, when the children of Iſrael abunded, they did reioyce;
label: Wisdom

text: by theſe thinges, when others lacked the ſame, it went wel with them.
label: Wisdom

text: For in ſteede of the fountaine of an euerlaſting riuer, thou gaueſt mans bloud to the vniuſt.
label: Wisdom

text: Who when they were diminished in the deſtruction of the murdered infants, thou gaueſt them abundant vnlooked for:
label: Wisdom

text: shewing by the thirſt, that then was, how thou didſt exalt thine, & didſt kil their aduerſaries.
label: Wisdom

text: For when they were tempted, and in deede with mercie taking diſcipline, they knew how the impious being iudged with wrath did ſuffer torments.
label: Wisdom

text: Theſe certes admonishing as a father thou didſt proue: but them examining as a hard king thou didſt condemne.
label: Wisdom

text: For the abſent and the preſent were tormented alike.
label: Wisdom

text: For duble tediouſnes had taken them, and ſighing with the memorie of good thinges paſt.
label: Wisdom

text: For when they vnderſtood by their punishement that it went wel with them, they remembred our Lord, meruecling at the end of the euent.
label: Wisdom

text: For whom before they derided, being caſt forth in that wicked laying out to perish, him they merueled at in the end of the euent: not thirſting in like maner to the iuſt:
label: Wisdom

text: but for ſenſeles cogitations of their iniquitie, for that ſome erring did worshippe dumme ſerpents, and ſuperfluous beaſts, thou didſt ſend vpon them a multitude of dumme beaſts for reuenge:
label: Wisdom

text: that they might know that by what thinges a man ſinneth, by the ſame alſo he is tormented.
label: Wisdom

text: For thine omnipotent hand, which made the world of inuiſible matter, was not vnable to ſend vpon them a multitude of beares, or fierce lyons,
label: Wisdom

text: or vnknowen beaſts ful of anger of a new kind; or breathing the vapour of fires, or caſting forth the ſauour of ſmoke, or shooting horrible ſparkes from their eies:
label: Wisdom

text: of which not onlie their hurt was able to deſtroy them, but alſo their ſight to kil them for feare.
label: Wisdom

text: Yea and without theſe with one ſpirit, they might haue beene ſlaine ſuffering perſecution of their owne factes, and diſperſed by the ſpirit of thy powre: but thou haſt diſpoſed al thinges in meaſure, and number, and weight.
label: Wisdom

text: For, to be of great force reſted alwaies in thee onlie: & who shal reſiſt the powre of thyne arme?
label: Wisdom

text: Becauſe as the leaſt weight of the balance, ſo is the roundworld before thee, and as a droppe of the dewe before day, that falleth vpon the earth.
label: Wisdom

text: But thou haſt mercie on al, becauſe thou canſt do al thinges, and diſſembleſt the ſinnes of men for repentance.
label: Wisdom

text: For thou loueſt al thinges that are, and hateſt nothing of thoſe which thou haſt made: for thou didſt not ordaine, or make any thing hating it.
label: Wisdom

text: And how could any thing continew, vnles thou wouldeſt? or be preſerued which was not called of thee?
label: Wisdom

text: But thou ſpareſt al: becauſe they are thine ô Lord, which loueſt ſoules.
label: Wisdom

text: O how good, and ſweete is thy ſpirit ô Lord in al!
label: Wisdom

text: And therfore thoſe, that erre, by partes thou doeſt chaſtiſe: and doeſt admonish, and ſpeake to them, concerning the thinges wherin they ſinne: that leauing naughtines, they may beleue in thee ô Lord.
label: Wisdom

text: For, thoſe old inhabitantes of thy holie land, whom thou didſt abhorre,
label: Wisdom

text: becauſe they did workes odious to thee by ſorceries, and vniuſt ſacrifices,
label: Wisdom

text: and the murderers of their owne children without mercie, and eaters of mens bowels, and deuourers of bloud from the middes of thy ſacrament,
label: Wisdom

text: and the parents authors of aydeleſſe ſoules, thou wouldſt deſtroy by the handes of our parents,
label: Wisdom

text: that they might receiue a peregrination worthie of the children of God, which is a land of al moſt deare to thee.
label: Wisdom

text: But them alſo as men thou didſt ſpare, and didſt ſend fore-runners of thine hoſt, waſpes, that by litle and litle they might deſtroy them.
label: Wisdom

text: Not becauſe thou waſt vnable in battel to ſubdewe the impious to the iuſt, or with cruel beaſtes, or with a sharpe word to deſtroy them together:
label: Wisdom

text: but iudging by partes thou gaueſt place of repentance, being not ignorant, that the nation of them is wicked, and their malice natural, & that their cogitation could not be changed for euer.
label: Wisdom

text: For it was a curſed ſeede from the begynning: neither fearing any, didſt thou geue pardon to their ſinnes.
label: Wisdom

text: For who shal ſay to thee: what haſt thou done? or who shal ſtand againſt thy iudgement? or who in thy ſight shal come reuenger of the wicked men? or who shal impute it to thee, if the nations perish, which thou haſt made?
label: Wisdom

text: For there is no other God but thou, who haſt care of al, that thou mayſt shew that thou doeſt not geue iudgement vniuſtly.
label: Wisdom

text: Neither king, nor tyrant in thy ſight shal enquire of them, whom thou haſt deſtroyed.
label: Wisdom

text: For ſo much then as thou art iuſt, thou doeſt diſpoſe al thinges iuſtly: thou alſo eſtemeſt it diſagreable from thy powre, to condemne him, who ought not to be punished.
label: Wisdom

text: For thy powre is the begynning of iuſtice: and for this that thou art Lord of al, thou makeſt thyſelf to ſpare al.
label: Wisdom

text: For thou sheweſt powre, which art not thought to be abſolute in powre, and thou conuinceſt the boldnes of them, that know thee not.
label: Wisdom

text: But thou dominatour of powre, iudgeſt with tranquilitie, and with great reuerence diſpoſeſt of vs: for it is in thy powre when thou wilt, to be able.
label: Wisdom

text: And thou haſt taught thy people by ſuch workes, that they muſt be iuſt and gentle, and haſt made thy children of good hope: becauſe iudging thou geueſt in ſinnes place of repentance.
label: Wisdom

text: For if thou didſt punish the enemies of thy ſeruants, and that deſerued to die, with ſo great conſideration, geuing time and place, whereby they might be changed from their wickednes.
label: Wisdom

text: With what diligence haſt thou iudged thy children, to whoſe parents thou gaueſt othes and couenants of good promiſes?
label: Wisdom

text: Therfore when thou geueſt vs diſcipline, thou ſcourgeſt our enemies very manie wayes, that iudging we may thinke vpon thy goodnes: and when we are iudged, we may hope for thy mercie.
label: Wisdom

text: Wherfore to them alſo, which in their life haue liued foolishly & vniuſtly, thou haſt geuen great torments by the ſame thinges, which they did worshipe.
label: Wisdom

text: For they wandered long in the way of errour, eſteming for goddes thoſe thinges, that in beaſts are ſuperfluous, liuing after the maner of ſenſles infants.
label: Wisdom

text: For this cauſe thou haſt geuen iudgement on them as on ſenſles children to be in deriſion.
label: Wisdom

text: But they that were not amended by ſcornes and reprehenſions, haue tried the worthie iudgement of God.
label: Wisdom

text: For in what thinges they ſuffering tooke indignation, by thoſe whom they thought goddes, when ſeing they were deſtroyed in them, him, whom in time paſt they denied that they knewe, they acknowleged the true God: for the which cauſe the end alſo of their condemnation shal come vpon them.
label: Wisdom

text: BVT al men be vaine, in whom there is not the knowlege of God: and of theſe good thinges, which are ſene they could not vnderſtand him that is, neither attending to the workes haue they agniſed who was the workeman:
label: Wisdom

text: but either the fyre, or the wind, or the ſwift ayre, or a circle of ſtarres or exceding much water, or the ſunne and the moone, they thought to be goddes rulers of the world.
label: Wisdom

text: With whoſe beautie if being delighted, they thought them goddes: let them know how much the Lord of them is more beautiful then they. For the author of beautie made al thoſe thinges.
label: Wisdom

text: Or if they merueled at their vertue, & operations, let them vnderſtand by them, that he which made theſe, is ſtronger then they:
label: Wisdom

text: for by the greatnes of the beautie, and of the creature the creator of them may be ſene, to be knowen therby.
label: Wisdom

text: But notwithſtanding there is yet in theſe leſſe complainte. For they alſo perhaps erre, ſeeking God, and deſirous to finde him.
label: Wisdom

text: For whereas they conuerſe in his workes, they enquire: & they are perſwaded that the thinges be good which are ſeene.
label: Wisdom

text: But againe neither ought theſe to be pardoned.
label: Wisdom

text: For if they could know ſo much, that they were able to eſtimate the world: how did they not more eaſely find the Lord therof?
label: Wisdom

text: But they are vnhappie, & their hope is among the dead, who haue called the workes of mens handes godds, gold & ſiluer, the inuention of art, and the ſimilitudes of beaſtes, or an vnprofitable ſtone the worke of an old hand.
label: Wisdom

text: Or if an artificer a carpenter, cut ſtreight timber out of the wood, & pare of al the barke therof cunningly, and vſing his art, diligently frameth a veſſel profitable for the common vſe of this life,
label: Wisdom

text: and vſeth the chippes of that worke to dreſſe his meate:
label: Wisdom

text: and maketh that which is left therof, which is for no vſes, but being a crooked peece of wood, and ful of knobes, carueth it diligently in the holownes therof, and by the skil of his art fashioneth it, and maketh it like to the image of a man,
label: Wisdom

text: or compareth it to ſome beaſt, ſtraking it ouer with redde, and with paynting making the colour therof ruddie, and layeth a colour ouer euerie ſpot that is in it:
label: Wisdom

text: and maketh a worthie habitation for it, and ſetting it in a wal, and faſtening it with yron,
label: Wisdom

text: leſt perhaps it fal, prouiding for it, knowing that it can not helpe it ſelfe: for it is an image, and it nedeth helpe.
label: Wisdom

text: And concerning his ſubſtance, & his children, & for mariage, making a vow he ſeeketh to it. He is not ashamed to ſpeake with him, that is without ſoule:
label: Wisdom

text: and for health certes he beſecheth the weake, and for life asketh the dead, and for helpe inuocateth him that is vnprofitable:
label: Wisdom

text: and for a iourney asketh him, that can not walke: and for getting, and for working, and for the euent of al thinges he asketh him, that in al is vnprofitable.
label: Wisdom

text: AGAYNE an other thinking to ſayle, and begynning to make a iorney through the fierce waues, inuocateth wood more fraile then the wood that carieth him.
label: Wisdom

text: For couetouſnes of getting inuented it, and the crafteſman by his wiſdom framed it.
label: Wisdom

text: But thy prouidence, ô Father, doth gouerne: becauſe thou haſt geuen a way euen in the ſea, and among the waues a moſt ſure path,
label: Wisdom

text: shewing that thou art able to ſaue out of al thinges, yea if a man goe to the ſea without art.
label: Wisdom

text: But that thy workes might not be voyde of wiſdom: for this cauſe alſo men commit their liues euen to a little wood, and paſſing ouer the ſea are deliuered by shippe.
label: Wisdom

text: But from the begynning alſo when the prowde giants perished, the hope of the world fleing to a shippe, rendered to the world ſeede of natiuitie, which was gouerned by thy hand.
label: Wisdom

text: For bleſſed is the wood, by the which iuſtice is made.
label: Wisdom

text: But the idol that is made by handes, curſed is both it, and he that made it: becauſe he in deede wrought it: and the ſame being fraile, was called god.
label: Wisdom

text: But to God the impious and his impietie are odious alike.
label: Wisdom

text: For that which is made, with him that made it, shal ſuffer torments.
label: Wisdom

text: For this cauſe alſo in the idol of the nations there shal be no reſpect: becauſe the creatures of God were made to hatred, and for tentation to the ſoules of men, and for a ſnare to the feete of the vnwiſe.
label: Wisdom

text: For the begynning of fornication is the deuiſing of idols: and the inuenting of them is the corruption of life.
label: Wisdom

text: For neither were they from the begynning, neither shal they be for euer.
label: Wisdom

text: For this vanitie of men came into the world: and therfore there is found a short end of them.
label: Wisdom

text: For the father being ſorowful with bitter moorning, made vnto himſelf the image of his ſonne quickly taken away: and him, that then was a dead man, now he began to worshipe as god, and appointed holie thinges and ſacrifices among his ſeruants.
label: Wisdom

text: Afterward by ſucceſſion of time, the wicked cuſtom preuayling, this errour was kept as a law, and thinges grauen were worshipped by the commandement af tyrants.
label: Wisdom

text: And thoſe, whom openly men could not honour, for that they were far of, their figure being brought from a far, they made an euident image of the king, whom they would honour: that by their carefulnes they might honour as preſent, him that was abſent.
label: Wisdom

text: And to the worshipping of theſe, the excellent diligence alſo of the artificer, holpe them forward, that were ignorant.
label: Wisdom

text: For he willing to pleaſe him, that entertained him, laboured by his art, to fashion the ſimilitude in better ſort.
label: Wisdom

text: And the multitude of men caried away by the beautie of the worke, him that a little before had bene honoured as a man, now they eſtemed for a god.
label: Wisdom

text: And this was the deceyuing of mans life: becauſe men ſeruing either affection, or kinges, gaue the name that is not communicable to ſtones and wood.
label: Wisdom

text: And it was not ſufficient that they erred about the knowlege of God, but alſo liuing in a great battail of ignorance ſo manie and ſo great euils they cal peace.
label: Wisdom

text: For either ſacrificing their children, or making abſcure ſacrifices, or hauing watches ful of madnes,
label: Wisdom

text: they now neither keepe life, nor mariage cleane, but one killeth an other by enuie, or playing the adulterer maketh him ſorowful:
label: Wisdom

text: and al thinges are mingled together, bloud, manſlaughter, theft and fiction, corruption, and infidelitie, truble, and periurie, diſquieting of the good,
label: Wisdom

text: forgetfulnes of God, inquination of ſoules, immutation of natiuitie, inconſtancie of mariage, diſorder of adulterie, and vnchaſtnes.
label: Wisdom

text: For the worshippe of idols not to be named, is the cauſe of al euil, and the beginning and end.
label: Wisdom

text: For either when they reioyce, they are madde: or certes prophecie falſe thinges, or liue vniuſtly, or quickly forſweare themſelues.
label: Wisdom

text: For whiles they truſt in idols, which are without ſoule, ſwearing amiſſe they hope not to be hurt.
label: Wisdom

text: Two euil thinges therfore shal happen to them worthely, becauſe they haue thought euil of God, attending to idols, and haue ſworne vniuſtly, in guile contemning iuſtice.
label: Wisdom

text: For it is not the powre of them, that are ſworne by, but the punishment of them that ſinne, goeth alwayes through the trangreſſion of the vniuſt.
label: Wisdom

text: BVT ô thou our God, art ſweete, and true, patient, and diſpoſing al thinges in mercie.
label: Wisdom

text: For if we ſinne, we are thine, knowing thy greatnes: and if we ſinne not we know that we are counted with thee.
label: Wisdom

text: For to know thee, is abſolute iuſtice: and to know iuſtice, and thy powre, is the roote of immortalitie.
label: Wisdom

text: For mens invention of euil art hath not brought vs into errour, nor the shadow of a picture being a labour without fruite, a shape grauen by diuerſe colours,
label: Wisdom

text: the ſight wherof geueth concupiſcence to the ſenſles, and he loueth the shape without life of a deade image.
label: Wisdom

text: The louers of euils, are worthie to haue their hope in ſuch thinges, both they that make them, and that loue, and that worshippe them.
label: Wisdom

text: Yea and the potter preſſing ſofte earth, with labour fashioneth euerie veſſel to our vſes, and of the ſame clay maketh the veſſels, that are cleane to vſe, and in like maner them, that are contrarie to theſe: but what the vſe of theſe veſſels is, the potter is iudge.
label: Wisdom

text: And with vaine labour he fashioneth a god of the ſame clay: he which a litle before was made of earth, and a litle after returneth backe whence he was taken, being exacted the debte of the life which he had.
label: Wisdom

text: But his care is, not becauſe he shal labour, nor becauſe he hath a short life, but he contendeth with goldſmithes and ſiluer ſmithes: yea and he imitateth the copper ſmithes, and counteth it a glorie, becauſe he maketh vaine thinges.
label: Wisdom

text: For his hart is ashes, and his hope vaine earth, and his life viler then clay:
label: Wisdom

text: becauſe he was ignorant who made him, and who inſpired into him the ſoule which worketh, and who breathed into him the vital ſpirite.
label: Wisdom

text: Yea and they eſtemed our life to be a paſtime, and the conuerſation of life made for a gayne; & that we muſt get euerie way euen of euil.
label: Wisdom

text: For he knoweth that he offendeth aboue al men, which of the matter of earth fashioneth frayle veſſels, and ſculptils.
label: Wisdom

text: For al the vnwiſe, and vnhappie aboue meaſure of the ſoule, proude are the enemies of thy people, and rule ouer them:
label: Wisdom

text: becauſe they haue eſtemed al the idols of the nations for goddes, which neither haue vſe of eies to ſee, nor noſthrels to take breath, nor eares to heare, nor fingers of the hands to handle, yea and their feete are ſlow to walke.
label: Wisdom

text: For a man made them: and he that borowed breath, the ſame fashioned them. For no man can make God like to himſelf.
label: Wisdom

text: For wheras him ſelf is mortal, he maketh a dead thing with his wicked handes. For he is better then they, whom he worshippeth, becauſe he in deede liued, though he were mortal, but they neuer.
label: Wisdom

text: But they worship alſo moſt miſerable beaſts: for the ſenſleſſe thinges compared to theſe, are worſe then they.
label: Wisdom

text: Yea neither by ſight can any man ſee good of theſe beaſts. But they haue fled from the prayſe of God, and from his bleſſing.
label: Wisdom

text: FOR theſe thinges, and by the like to theſe, they haue worthely ſuffered torments, and were deſtroyed by a multitude of beaſts.
label: Wisdom

text: For the which torments thou didſt wel diſpoſe of thy people, to whom thou gaueſt the deſire of their delectation a new taſte, preparing them the quaile for meate:
label: Wisdom

text: that they in deede coueting meate, becauſe of thoſe thinges which were shewed and ſent them, might be turned away euen from neceſſarie concupiſcence. But they in short time being made needie, taſted a new meate.
label: Wisdom

text: For it behoued that without excuſe deſtruction should come vpon them exerciſing tyrannie: but to theſe onlie to shew how their enemies were deſtroyed.
label: Wisdom

text: For when the cruel wrath of beaſtes came vpon them, they were deſtroyed with the bytings of peruerſe ſerpents.
label: Wisdom

text: Howbeit thy wrath endured not for euer, but for chaſtiſement they were trubled a short time, hauing a ſigne of ſaluation for the remembrance of the commandment of thy law.
label: Wisdom

text: For he that turned to it, was not healed by that which he ſaw, but by thee the ſauiour of al:
label: Wisdom

text: and in this thou didſt shew to our enemies, that thou art he which deliuereſt from al euil.
label: Wisdom

text: For the bitings of locuſts, and flies killed them, and there was found no remedie for their life: becauſe they were worthie to be deſtroyed by ſuch thinges.
label: Wisdom

text: But neither the teeth of venemous dragons ouercame thy children: for thy mercie coming healed them.
label: Wisdom

text: For in memorie of thy wordes they were examined, & were quickly ſaued, leſt falling into deepe obliuion, they might not vſe thy helpe.
label: Wisdom

text: For neither herbe, nor playſter healed them, but thy word, ô Lord, which healeth al thinges.
label: Wisdom

text: For it is thou, ô Lord, that haſt powre of life and death, and bringeſt downe to the gates of death, and bringeſt againe:
label: Wisdom

text: but man certes killeth by malice, and when the ſpirit is gone forth, it shal not returne, neither shal he cal backe the ſoule, that is receiued:
label: Wisdom

text: but it is vnpoſſible to eſcape thy hand.
label: Wisdom

text: For the impious denying to knowe thee, haue bene ſcourged by the ſtrength of thine arme, ſuffering perſecution by ſtrange waters, and haile, and rayne, and conſumed by fyre.
label: Wisdom

text: For that which was meruelous in water, which extinquisheth al thinges, fyre more preuayled: for the world is reuenger of the iuſt.
label: Wisdom

text: For a certayne time, the fyre was mitigated, that the beaſts which were ſent to the impious might not be burnt, but that they ſeing might know that by Gods iudgement they ſuffer punishment.
label: Wisdom

text: And at a certaine time the fyre aboue his powre burnt in water on euerie ſide, that it might deſtroy the nation of a wicked land.
label: Wisdom

text: For the which thinges thou didſt nourish thy people with the meate of Angels, and bread prepared thou gaueſt them from heauen without labour, hauing in it al delectation, and the ſweetnes of al taſte.
label: Wisdom

text: For thy ſubſtance did shew thy ſweetnes which thou haſt toward thy children, and ſeruing euerie mans wil, it was turned to that, that euerie man would.
label: Wisdom

text: Yea ſnow and yce ſuſteyned the force of fyre, and melted not: that they might know that fyre burning in hayle, and lightening in rayne deſtroyed the fruites of the enemies.
label: Wisdom

text: And this againe, that the iuſt might be nourished, it forgat alſo his owne ſtrength.
label: Wisdom

text: For the creature ſeruing thee the Creatour, is fierce into torment againſt the vniuſt: and is made more gentle to doe good for them, that truſt in thee.
label: Wisdom

text: For this cauſe euen then being transformed into al thinges they ſerued thy grace the nource of al, at their wil that deſired thee:
label: Wisdom

text: that thy children might know, whom thou louedſt ô Lord, that not the fruites of natiuitie doe feede men, but thy word preſerueth them, that beleue in thee.
label: Wisdom

text: For that which could not be deſtroyed by fyre, forthwith being heated with a litle beame of the ſunne did melt:
label: Wisdom

text: that it might be knowen to al men, that we ought to preuent the ſunne to bleſſe thee, and at the ryſing of light to adore thee.
label: Wisdom

text: For the fayth of the vngratful shal melt as winter yce, & shal perish as vnprofitable water.
label: Wisdom
